500690|2026-03.headline: GSFC FY26 standalone sales rose 15% to INR10,827 crore and PAT 14% to INR652 crore; Q4 sales hit a record INR2,622 crore.
500690|2026-03.overview: GSFC reported record Q4 FY26 sales of INR2,622 crore, with fertilizer sales of INR1,985 crore also a Q4 high. For FY26, standalone sales grew 15% to INR10,827 crore, operating EBITDA rose 24% to INR781 crore, and PAT rose 14% to INR652 crore. The Industrial Products segment posted its highest annual profit in four years (INR200 crore) and its best Q4 EBIT in ten quarters, helped by HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, though caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure. Management said Q1 FY27 faces unsettled raw material markets, and it is managing the fertilizer mix around sulphur and ammonia supply.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: FY26 fertilizer sales volume rose 12% to 22.31 lakh MT from 19.88 lakh MT, led by AS, APS and DAP; fertilizer production hit a five-year high of 17.59 lakh MT. Segment sales rose INR1,196 crore for the year.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Delivered highest annual profit of INR200 crore in four years and highest Q4 EBIT in ten quarters. Growth came from HX Crystal, traded ammonia and melamine exports, while caprolactam and nylon realisations were under pressure from lower global spreads.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 fertilizer: raw material markets unsettled; government NBS rate revision for H1 FY27 gives a 10% uplift across nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur nutrients to support kharif supply.
Management said there will be no production shortfall in Q1 FY27 for fertilizers, with ammonium sulphate imports arriving in the current month.

Industrial products: caprolactam-benzene spreads expected to recover, but elevated caprolactam and nylon 6 prices of Q4 unlikely to hold; melamine and technical grade urea face softer demand; export volumes expected to hold.

Fertilizer margin: DAP and urea margins expected unchanged as they are protected by government; government special package for extra DAP costs expected via circular soon; NPK grades could move plus or minus 5-10%.
IP segment expected to offset any fertilizer margin loss; caprolactam-benzene spread was above $800/MT currently versus about $670/MT in Q4.
capex_capacity: Capitalised major growth projects worth over INR670 crore in FY26, per management.
Sikka DAP train (1,300-1,400 MT/day) being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected in July or August 2026.
Ammonia plants 3 and 4 running at 100%; ammonia stock around 16,000 MT at Baroda complex.
Sulphuric acid tanks at full inventory level, but sulphur supply under long-term contracts (Reliance, Nayara, BPCL, IOCL) is not 100%, so imports are being sought.
demand_pricing: Fertilizer demand described as robust, supported by higher subsidy support; company running at optimum fertilizer utilisation with ammonium sulphate output at maximum possible given sulphur constraints.
Sulphur international price cited at about $850/MT; natural gas prices controlled by government, with increases absorbed through subsidy.
Melamine and technical grade urea demand soft; HX Crystal domestic demand constant; agrochemical sector absorbing geopolitical knock-on effects.
Government subsidy dues received for urea up to fourth week of April 2026 and P&K up to third week of April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How is the organisation positioned for FY27 given geopolitical disruption and import dependence, and what consistent numbers should investors expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called the situation abnormal with raw material prices up manifold. Ammonia is made from domestically supplied gas at Fertilizer Nagar, where gas prices are government-controlled and absorbed via subsidy; sulphuric acid stock is sufficient for Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the inventory position and replenishment pipeline for raw materials?
qa_highlights.answer: Ammonia stock about 16,000 MT at Baroda with 100% plant run rates; sulphuric acid tanks full. Sulphur supply under long-term contracts is partial and expensive, so spot imports are being arranged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company continuing ammonia trading?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ammonia is imported through the company's own Sikka jetty and storage, with volumes for industry sold and ammonia traded from Jamnagar.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fertilizer plant changeover to produce alternative grades, and what is the outlook for each segment?
qa_highlights.answer: One DAP train at Sikka (1,300-1,400 MT/day) is being converted to produce APS or DAP; completion expected July or August 2026. Fertilizer running at optimum levels; IP spreads improved to over $800/MT from about $670/MT.

qa_highlights.question: What fertilizer per-ton margin and blended volume should be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise margin given volatility. DAP and urea margins are unchanged due to government protection; NPK grades may vary by plus or minus 5-10%, offset by IP segment performance.

risks_watch: Sulphur and ammonia supply constraints and high import prices; sulphur supply not at 100% of contract volumes.
Government special package for DAP cost reimbursement not yet issued; margin protection depends on the circular.
Caprolactam and nylon 6 prices expected to fall from Q4 peaks; melamine and technical urea demand soft.
Monsoon progress and possible El Nino affecting kharif demand.
Subsidy receivable timing: urea and P&K dues cleared only to late April 2026.
500690|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and the IP turnaround, but cautious and somewhat evasive on forward fertilizer margins and raw material costs, which management said are too volatile to quantify. Stable operations and government backing were stressed more than specific FY27 targets.
key_quotes: So whatever margin loss we will be having in the fertilizer will be compensated by the IP product segment as I told that it is shaping up very nicely the prices of the chemical side.
We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with no long-term debt, healthy net worth and adequate liquidity.
So there will not be any production deficiency in the current quarter.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: DAP and urea margins are held flat by government protection (management: 'margin will remain same as in the past'), and caprolactam and nylon 6 prices are expected to fall from Q4 peaks, offsetting any IP-led gains.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Sikka DAP train (1,300-1,400 MT/day) conversion to APS or DAP is under construction with completion expected July or August 2026, and over INR670 crore of major growth projects were capitalised in FY26.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY26 fertilizer volume rose 12% to 22.31 lakh MT and production hit a five-year high of 17.59 lakh MT; management expects no Q1 FY27 production shortfall and robust demand supported by subsidy.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no FY27 numerical guidance and called raw material markets unsettled; the 15% FY26 sales growth is not being extended into a raised target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Sulphur supply under long-term contracts is not at 100% (sulphur international price about $850/MT), and NPK grades could move plus or minus 5-10%, while the government DAP special package is not yet issued.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The Sikka DAP train conversion to produce APS or DAP completes July or August 2026, which would add alternative grades, but no product launch was framed as such.

rows.label: Government NBS rate revision gives 10% uplift for H1 FY27
rows.why: The NBS rate revision for H1 FY27 gives a 10% uplift across nitrogen, phosphorus and sulphur nutrients to support kharif supply.

rows.label: Caprolactam-benzene spread recovery offsetting fertilizer margin
rows.why: The caprolactam-benzene spread is above $800/MT versus about $670/MT in Q4, and management expects IP to offset any fertilizer margin loss, though elevated Q4 caprolactam and nylon 6 prices are unlikely to hold.

rows.label: Subsidy receivable timing
rows.why: Urea subsidy dues were received only up to the fourth week of April 2026 and P&K dues up to the third week, so receivable collection is lagging and the DAP special package circular is still pending.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY26 record and IP turnaround and stressed government backing, but cautious and evasive on forward fertilizer margins and raw material costs, which it called too volatile to quantify; analysts pressed on margin per ton and blended volume.

500690|2026-09.headline: GSFC Q2 FY27 consolidated sales rose 49% YoY, but PBT fell 42% and PAT fell 38% as fertilizer EBIT collapsed to INR17 crores on raw material costs.
500690|2026-09.overview: Revenue hit a record Q2 on DAP realisation support, but sulfur (up 327%) and natural gas (up 62%) costs crushed fertilizer margins. Fertilizer EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores a year earlier, while Industrial Products EBIT rose to INR66 crores from INR54 crores on better caprolactam, nylon and Anone realisations. Management said the company has no long-term debt, and it has approved a roughly INR3,000 crore phosphoric and sulfuric acid project at Sikka. H2 outlook hinges on the NBS subsidy rates for October to March, which have not yet been notified.

segments.name: Fertilizer
segments.commentary: Sales up 55% YoY (+INR1,387 crores) despite volume down 6% to 5.69 lakh MT from 6.08 lakh MT. DAP revenue rose INR1,659 crores on the government DAP special package, but EBIT fell to INR17 crores from INR224 crores.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Sales up INR185 crores (30% YoY). Caprolactam sales up INR58 crores and nylon up INR60 crores on higher realisations; Anone up INR36 crores on volume; TGU up INR26 crores; melamine down INR5 crores. Caprolactam-benzene spread rose to USD 849/MT from USD 512/MT.

guidance_outlook: Management was optimistic on H2 FY27, conditional on the NBS subsidy rates for 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, which had not been notified at the time of the call.
Management said the Q2 profit deficit would be compensated in the next quarter if the subsidy rates are raised and approved.
Caprolactam-benzene spread is expected to moderate in Q3 FY27 as regional supply normalises.
Melamine and technical-grade urea demand expected steady; HX crystal exports may improve given subdued domestic demand.
Solar power arrangement at Sikka expected to save INR20-25 crores per quarter.
Management said no buyback or other value-creation measures have been discussed by the Board yet.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid and sulfuric acid (PA-SA) project at Sikka: about INR3,000 crores, EPC contract recently awarded, 30-33 months to completion. It is expected to meet 50% of DAP and NPK raw material needs captively.
C-Train modification for 1,200 MT per day APS production in place of DAP at Sikka commissioned on 23 October 2026, per market requirement.
Management estimated about 20% margin from producing phosphoric acid in-house versus purchasing it.
Rock procurement will be under a long-term contract, but contractors will not fix prices, so the price will be set at the purchase date.
demand_pricing: Rabi season opens with fertilizer inventory at the highest level in 3 years, especially urea and NPK, which intensifies competition.
Subdued southwest monsoon and low reservoir levels in southern India likely to constrain fertilizer demand.
DAP-NPK price distortion is steering farmers toward DAP, hurting NPK offtake. NBS rates are seen as key to resolving this.
Management said DAP margin is about 4% (fully compensated under the advantage/disadvantage regime) and urea margin about 3-4%. NPK margins depend on the subsidy rates still to come.

Urea subsidy receipts were received up to the third week of October. Management said urea's share of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable is only about INR100-300 crores, which the company expects to recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and economics of the Sikka capex for phosphoric and sulfuric acid?
qa_highlights.answer: Project financed at about INR3,000 crores, EPC awarded, 30-33 months to complete. About 50% of DAP and NPK requirement to be captively sourced, with about 20% margin from in-house PA production.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 outlook given volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management was optimistic, citing the pending NBS subsidy rates from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027. It said the Q2 deficit would be made up in Q3 if rates rise, and that cost cuts under a BCG-suggested plan are being applied at Sikka.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR3,400 crore subsidy receivable relates to urea?
qa_highlights.answer: Urea subsidy was received up to the third week of October. Urea accounts for only about INR100-200 crores (up to INR300 crores), with the bulk tied to DAP and NPK.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any value-creation plan such as a buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback or other measures have been discussed at the Board yet; management will revert at an appropriate time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the operational efficiency gain beyond subsidy?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar power at Sikka replacing costly grid power is expected to add about INR20-25 crores per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How is distribution and Industrial Products growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Fertilizer distribution is set by the government. Industrial products are sold on market demand pan-India, and management sees better IP prospects from captive raw materials and product mix, since chemical prices are not under MRP control.

risks_watch: NBS subsidy rates for Oct 2026 to Mar 2027 are not yet notified. Fertilizer margins depend almost entirely on them.
Urea subsidy pool gas rate finalisation between FICC and GAIL has been pending since April 2026, so urea subsidy may still be revised.
Sulfur (+327%) and natural gas (+62%) costs remain elevated; Middle East and Europe tensions are a key swing factor.
Record fertilizer inventory ahead of Rabi, weak monsoon and southern reservoir levels, and DAP-NPK price distortion may pressure volumes and NPK offtake.
Caprolactam-benzene spread expected to moderate in Q3 FY27, which would weigh on the caprolactam-nylon chain.
Sikka PA-SA project runs 30-33 months, and its ultimate margin depends on PA and sulfur prices at commissioning.
500690|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the balance sheet, but guarded on margins: management repeatedly deferred H2 profitability to the unannounced NBS subsidy rates. Answers on buybacks and value creation were non-committal.
key_quotes: So the company has delivered its ever highest Q2 and H1 top lines, achieving total sales of INR4,711 crores on a stand-alone basis in quarter 2 '26-'27
The subsidy is very important because whatever margins are coming, it is from subsidy.
Whatever the deficit in the profits we have incurred during the last quarter, this will be compensated in the next quarter.

500696|2026-03.headline: HUL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 8% with 7% USG led by volumes; EBITDA margin 23.7% at top of guidance; FY27 guided better than FY26.
500696|2026-03.overview: March quarter 2026 consolidated revenue rose 8% with 7% underlying sales growth (USG), the company's highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, driven mainly by volume (UVG 6%). EBITDA grew 6% with margin at 23.7%, the higher end of guidance, while PAT before exceptionals was Rs 2,711 crore (+4%); reported PAT rose 20% helped by the Nutritionalab divestment versus an OZiva fair-value base effect. For FY26, turnover was Rs 63,763 crore with 5% USG and 4% UVG, and the second half outpaced the first; EBITDA grew 2% at a 23.6% margin. Management flagged a sharp March-onward rise in crude-linked input costs (8-10% material cost inflation) from the Middle East crisis and has taken 2-5% price increases, with more pricing possible.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; includes Nutritionalab divestment gain, offset by OZiva fair-value base effect

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 9% on high-single-digit UVG, strongest in 11 quarters; liquids grew double digit and crossed Rs 4,000 crore turnover. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 8% on mid-single-digit UVG; hair care grew strong double digit; premium skin care grew double digit while mass skin (Glow & Lovely, talc) was subdued. FY26 USG 6%. Minimalist ARR about Rs 850 crore; Simple ARR above Rs 160 crore.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5%, pricing-led; skin cleansing grew high single digit (highest in 12 quarters) and premium cleansing bars grew double-digit volume. Oral care grew low single digit. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5% on high-single-digit UVG; coffee grew double digit, tea grew low-single-digit volume, lifestyle nutrition grew double digit. FY26 USG 5% on mid-single-digit UVG.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top line expected to be better than FY26 (USG basis), despite Middle East and currency volatility.
Mid-term EBITDA margin guidance kept at 22.5% to 23.5%; management expects Q1 FY27 to be at the lower end given cost pressure.

Material cost inflation of 8-10% seen for the June quarter; 2-5% price increases taken so far, with further calibrated price increases in Fabric Wash and Household Care in June quarter and beyond if costs persist.
Full-year FY27 pricing not guided; management said it is too difficult to give a number.
A&P spend stepped up by Rs 270 crore in absolute terms in FY26; non-working media being optimised while core brands stay fully funded.
capex_capacity: Rs 2,000 crore capex signed off for premium formats (liquids in Home Care, Personal Care and Beauty); timeline not specified.
Rs 3,500 crore deployed in FY26 on bolt-on acquisitions including Minimalist and OZiva.
Direct General Trade coverage increased by around 2 lakh outlets in FY26; specialty retail (open format stores, chemists, cosmetic stores) infrastructure being built.
Quick Commerce customer availability up about 1,400 basis points (as shared last quarter); a dedicated Quick Commerce organisation created.
Management said it remains open to bolt-on acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Demand described as stable; rural and urban demand growing at roughly equal rates in FY26.
No pre-buying by trade ahead of March/April price increases; no restocking effect in Q4 per management.
Home Care negative UPG is anniversarising; tea volumes low-single-digit with deflation in pricing cited as the cause.
Bodywash share up about 400 bps (Nielsen-based); body wash and premium skin cleansing growing double digit.

Monsoon forecast at 92% of normal; management cited higher reservoir levels, MSP increases of 5-6%, and record government grain stocks as offsets, and expects no rural demand impact unless rainfall falls below 85%.
E-commerce grew over 25% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by volume gains after GST cuts, and what are the drivers of UVG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three volume buckets: market development (liquids Rs 4,000 crore, mostly volumetric), share gains on core brands, and channel capability build-out; it said elasticity gains are being reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on margins amid input cost volatility, and would volume priority mean margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 8-10% on material basket versus 2-5% pricing taken so far; savings funnel accelerated; margin band of 22.5-23.5% retained, with lower end likely in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Home Care price hikes more modest than in the FY23 cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude-driven inflation is seen as volatile and geopolitical rather than structural, so price increases are being taken in steps; further hikes will follow if costs persist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mass skin care dragging Beauty & Wellbeing and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Glow & Lovely and talc were subdued (talc hit by seasonal weakness in March); premium skin care is growing double digit with a premium skin portfolio ARR near Rs 1,400 crore; focus on democratising new formats like sunscreen and light moisturisers.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 pricing outlook and Minimalist size?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year pricing number given; Minimalist ARR is about Rs 850 crore; cosmetics sub-category growth not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Lifestyle Nutrition sustainability given milk inflation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Horlicks is consumed in water as well as milk, is focusing on nutrition benefits, and new segments (RTD, protein, Horlicks Superfoods relaunch) are still small with headroom.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation of 8-10% with crude volatility (Brent cited between $85 and $120) and rupee depreciation; pricing lag could pressure margins below the 22.5-23.5% band.
Monsoon and El Nino risk to H2 rural demand; management's threshold is rainfall below 85%.
Mass skin care and Personal Care volume weakness; Personal Care grew only 5% and is pricing-led.
Price elasticity and possible down-trading if further price increases are taken; Home Care rebalancing of price and volume expected in the short term.
Horlicks/Boost recovery still early; Horlicks Superfoods national rollout and protein launch pending.
Foods remains outside the Unilever transaction perimeter; questions on the strategy alignment were addressed.

Management declined to split the portfolio into growth and core buckets or give full-year pricing and cosmetics growth figures.
key_quotes: Importantly, this represents our highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, reflecting both the ongoing transformation of our portfolio and the step-up of on-ground execution.

So, we have said a band of 22.5% to 23.5%. Now that band allows us to operate at sometimes a higher end of the band when things are favourable in terms of cost scenario, and maybe lower end of the band when things are not so favourable.
Competitive volume-led growth is our number one priority.

500696|2026-06.headline: HUL Q1 FY27 underlying sales growth accelerated to 10% (5% volume, 5% price), with EBITDA margin at 23% within guided range.
500696|2026-06.overview: HUL reported Q1 FY27 turnover of INR 17,184 crores with 10% underlying sales growth, the highest in 13 quarters, split equally between volume and price. Growth accelerated from 3% in H1 FY26. EBITDA rose 8% YoY to INR 3,947 crores at a 23% margin, within the guided range. Reported PAT of INR 2,680 crores fell 2% YoY because of a one-off tax credit of about INR 330 crores in the base quarter; adjusted for this, PAT grew 11%. Management reaffirmed that FY27 will be better than FY26 and that the EBITDA margin will stay around the guided range, while flagging monsoon, crude and geopolitical risks.

financial_highlights.change: -2% YoY; base included ~INR 330 crore one-off tax credit
Stepped up sequentially; highest in 11 quarters

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 14% on high-single-digit UVG, the strongest in 3 years. Fabric Wash grew double digits, volume-led; Household Care (Vim Liquid) grew double digits in USG and UVG. Calibrated price increases taken on crude-linked inputs.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 12% on high-single-digit UVG. Hair Care grew double digits, volume-led; Skin Care and Colour Cosmetics grew high single digit, with Premium Skin Care at double digit and Minimalist accelerating. Health & Wellbeing (OZiva) was soft as the business transitions toward emerging demand spaces.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 4%, driven by price increases taken for palm oil inflation for a second year. Skin Cleansing grew mid single digit (Dove and Pears premium bars double digit; Bodywash double digit); soaps volumes declined mid-single digit per analyst question. Oral Care grew mid single digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 7% on mid-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew double digit volume-led; Premium Tea low-single-digit UVG. Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit (Horlicks, Boost); Boost crossed INR 1,000 crore turnover. Packaged Foods grew high single digit.

guidance_outlook: FY27 expected to be better than FY26; guidance retained, but no quarterly guidance given.
EBITDA margin expected to remain around the current guided range despite elevated commodities and currencies.
Demand environment expected to remain stable; no inflation-led demand impact seen.
Guidance is risk-adjusted for macro and portfolio risks, per management.
Capital Markets Day scheduled for September 2026 for strategy update.
capex_capacity: Haridwar and Sonepat factories recognized in WEF Global Lighthouse Network; HUL now holds 8 designations across 6 sites.
Liquids Lab of the Future in Mumbai, AI-enabled, said to cut formulation timelines by up to 6x.
Unilever Fragrance House launched in India as part of a global fragrance capability programme.
Digital-first distribution centre in Vijayawada with AI-enabled real-time visibility.
demand_pricing: Turnover-weighted market share gains claimed across the portfolio; management does not guide by segment.
Price increases calibrated; cost inflation roughly 10% vs pricing around 5% per analyst citation, not disputed by management.
Quick commerce grew 40-50% per management, with new pack architecture; GT growth stepped up led by small towns and rural.
Rural and urban both growing robustly; mass and premium both competitive, with premiumization in line with market trend.
Tea early-season read shows inflationary trend; pricing decisions to follow buying season.

qa_highlights.question: Has the outlook tone changed versus last quarter given monsoon and geopolitical concerns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change; it remains well positioned, and is only cautioning on how the volatile economic scenario pans out.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the mid-single-digit soaps volume decline, and what is market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to palm oil inflation over two years; it is focusing on premiumization (Dove, Pears double digit, Bodywash double digit) and does not disclose segment share, saying it is winning turnover-weighted share overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is A&P under-investment happening to protect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said A&P is at its highest in 11-12 quarters, with better ROI from AI-enabled programmes and media procurement savings, so like-for-like comparisons are not strictly valid.

qa_highlights.question: Is the El Nino and monsoon risk material to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a difficult versus good agriculture year moves GDP by 50-60 bps; MSP hikes of 5-6% insulate rural income, and a rainfall deficit of about 15% is seen as not meaningfully impacting the economy.

qa_highlights.question: At what crude level can 23% margin be held without further price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a precise crude threshold, but said it can maintain margins with about half of inflation passed through and that crude of $75-100/bbl is manageable; $140-160 would be a different discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the quick commerce slowdown affecting HUL?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said QCom grew 40-50% and the channel remains structurally attractive, with new entrants and tailored assortments and pack architecture.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (palm oil, crude-linked derivatives, tea) and the pace of calibrated pricing needed to hold 23% EBITDA margin.
Soaps volume decline under palm oil-led price pressure and value competition in soaps and liquids.
Monsoon progression (rainfall deficit cited at about 15%) and El Nino impact on rural demand.
OZiva growth moderation in Health & Wellbeing and the stated transition of the business.
Management's shift from prior quarter's language on navigating volatility to cautioning on monsoon and geopolitics; watch wording at the September Capital Markets Day.

500696|2026-09.headline: HUL Q2 FY27 underlying sales growth of 15% with 7% volume growth; PAT before exceptionals up 9% to Rs 2,795 crore.
500696|2026-09.overview: HUL reported Q2 FY27 turnover of Rs 18,071 crore, with 15% USG (its highest in 14 quarters) and 7% UVG, despite roughly 8% price growth. EBITDA margin was 22.6%, within the guided 22-24% range, down about 140 bps YoY and 40 bps QoQ as gross margin fell about 400 bps on input cost inflation. EBITDA rose 8% to Rs 4,089 crore and PAT before exceptionals rose 9%; reported PAT was flat because the base quarter had Rs 273 crore of one-off tax gains. Management said it passed through absolute cost increases, protected volumes, and offset gross margin pressure with A&P productivity and overhead leverage.

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: USG 22% on double-digit UVG; Fabric Wash grew double digit across bars, powders and liquids. Management cut Home Care A&P by about Rs 250 crore in the quarter; segment absolute EBIT margin about 16% on revenue near Rs 7,000 crore.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: USG 16% on double-digit UVG, with Hair Care accelerating. Health & Wellbeing was subdued; OZiva's 2-year CAGR is beyond strong double digits but growth is non-linear.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: USG 9%. Skin Cleansing grew double digit with volume-led growth in Pears and Dove bars; Oral Care grew low single digit with premium innovations up double digit.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: USG 9% on low-single-digit UVG. Coffee grew high single digit; mass tea was soft while Red Label Instant Tea scaled; Lifestyle Nutrition grew double digit.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term EBITDA margin expected within the current guided range of 22% to 24%; management said cyclical dips can take margin to the lower end.
Management expects commodity inflation to remain elevated, but does not expect inflation of the scale seen in June and September quarters to recur.
Calibrated price increases to continue in measured steps if inflation rises.

Kissan condiments relaunched with new packaging.

Quick commerce players are supplied mostly direct; premium channel expansion seen as beneficial.
Market shares improved at company level and in Home Care per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is volume growth at risk given inflation and price hikes, especially in rural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited sequential improvement in volume momentum and rising rural demand, with growth broad-based across urban and rural and categories.

qa_highlights.question: Have gross margins bottomed, and will more pricing be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing covers absolute cost increases; EBITDA margin fell only 40 bps QoQ; structural portfolio mix should support margins in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ~8% price increase fully cover cost inflation, and can gross margin return toward 50-51%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costs are covered; tea pricing largely taken. It declined to give a numeric gross margin target and pointed to a 3 to 5 year structural improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Home Care profit growth lagged strong volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a price-versus-cost lag from petrochemical-linked inputs and said Home Care remains structurally premium; it declined to guide Home Care margin back toward 19-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Lifebuoy underperforming, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said soaps cleansing grew double digit sequentially and Lifebuoy faces uptrading within its own portfolio; it cited Lifebuoy Ice Bath launch and further work to stay competitive.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% pre-COVID peak margin a reasonable 3 to 5 year aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 22-24% range was widened by 50 bps each side for cyclicality, with a structural shift toward higher-margin categories over 3 to 5 years, but gave no numeric aspiration.

500710|2026-03.headline: JSW Dulux Q4 FY26 revenue rose 6.2% on 23% blended volume growth, with price and mix cuts holding back realisations and EBITDA margin near 14.4%.
500710|2026-03.overview: Management reported a record 23% blended volume growth across decorative and industrial paints, with revenue up 6.2%, the gap driven mainly by price and mix after premium price corrections from September-October 2025. Like-for-like EBITDA grew about 2% and PBT declined slightly, while the EBITDA margin was stated at around 14.4%. Management said raw material inflation since March 2026 has forced a price increase of about 9.7% through mid-May, with an estimated further 3-4% needed. The company also booked INR64.8 crore from the final real estate sale and proposed a final dividend of INR50 per share.

500710|2026-06.headline: JSW Dulux Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18.8% to ₹965 crore on ~25% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% with PAT lifted by one-offs.
500710|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 18.8% like-to-like to ₹965 crore, with volume up about 25% (about 18-19% after price). Gross margin was 37.4%, which management says was depressed by roughly 2 points of high-cost inventory and about 2.5 points from reclassifying promotional spends to gross revenue; underlying gross margin was put at 39.5-40%. EBITDA rose 14.7% to ₹115.1 crore but margin diluted about 50 bps to 11.9% after headcount additions (~160 people) and R&D investment. Reported PAT of ₹135.5 crore includes one-offs: ₹55.9 crore dividend from ICICI R&T and ₹108 crore income tax refund (incl. ₹21.5 crore interest) for AY 2013-14.

Other income; linked to real estate monetisation

qa_highlights.question: What execution changes are driving better decorative performance, beyond headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-market segmentation by share tiers; reinforced Velvet Touch and WeatherShield; focus on undercoats such as primers in weak states; digital lead management, AI/analytics and an architect/painter programme. Hybrid direct model being tested in top 20 towns.

qa_highlights.question: How does volume-value gap reconcile with mix improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three factors: high-cost inventory, ~2.5% gross-to-net reclassification, and faster growth in lower-margin industrial and other businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Target for top-three position and inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined JSW Paints and JSW Dulux revenue is about ₹6,000 crore. Aim is to become number two; industrial to be number one in 1-1.5 years and wider ambition by 2030-31. No explicit M&A mentioned.

qa_highlights.question: Competitive intensity and discounting vs. new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition to remain intense for 1-2 years; company does not match new entrant discounts and benchmarks against the market leader.

qa_highlights.question: Decorative outperformance vs Asian Paints and Berger (8-9% volume growth)?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to premium-led growth, distribution expansion, digital tools and recovery in smaller dealers after new-entrant pressure; no single driver cited.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for July-August?
qa_highlights.answer: July was weaker due to late rains, but management expects Q2 in a similar band and targets double-digit growth in volume and value.

500730|2026-03.headline: NOCIL Q4 FY26 revenue rose 5% QoQ to Rs.330 crore on 7% volume growth, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.4% amid raw material inflation.
500730|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs.330 crore, up 5% QoQ from Rs.316 crore, with volumes up 7% QoQ, driven by domestic demand after GST 2.0 and steady single-digit international growth. Operating EBITDA fell to Rs.21 crore (6.4% margin) from Rs.27 crore in Q3, hit by gas-driven utility costs, shutdown maintenance and a Rs.7-8 crore inventory-related stock change debit. FY26 revenue fell to Rs.1,303 crore from Rs.1,393 crore, with full-year volumes up 3% and PAT down to Rs.56 crore from Rs.103 crore. Management raised prices on non-contractual business in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27 in response to sharp raw material inflation linked to Middle East disruption.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew single digits QoQ, aided by GST 2.0 demand; management estimates a 100-150 bps market share gain. Volume split FY26 is 70% domestic, 30% exports.

segments.name: International / Exports
segments.commentary: International volumes grew steady single digits in Q4. Export value share is about 33% (67:33 domestic:export by value). US volumes, hit roughly 50% last quarter by duties, are recovering but management expects traction only in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty rubber chemicals
segments.commentary: Specialty is about 15% of mix today, with management targeting about 20% after the new Rs.130 crore integrated specialty facility ramps up.

guidance_outlook: Management expects H2 FY26 volume momentum (up 12% YoY) to continue into coming quarters, and says Q4 volumes can serve as the base run rate.
Targets double-digit volume growth in coming years.
Targets EBITDA improvement of about 150 bps from the FY26 base going forward.
Price increases on non-contractual business taken in March and on contractual business from Q1 FY27; management sees the current raw material spike as volatility, not structural demand weakness.
Expects 6-8 months from commissioning before material traction from tyre-based customers on new capacity; non-tyre business should start earlier.
Tax rate reverts to normal rates in FY27 with no specific reduction expected.
capex_capacity: TDQ capex at Dahej (announced 26 March 2024) is complete; trial production has started and samples go to customers for approval. Total capex is under Rs.250 crore.

New Rs.130 crore capex announced 16 March 2026 for a comprehensive integrated specialty rubber chemicals facility at Dahej, expected complete by H1 FY28. Mostly growth capex with some intermediates; largely merchant per management, with a part captive.
Installed capacity cited by analysts at about 1,38,000-1,39,000 tons; management declined to give effective capacity, saying utilisation is roughly 65%.
CWIP was about Rs.220 crore at FY26 end; no project debt drawn yet, with bank lines above Rs.100 crore available at repo-linked rates.
Full-year FY26 capex was largely funded from internal working capital release; analysts estimated Rs.170-180 crore working capital saving.
demand_pricing: Realisations were under pressure from low-priced imports through Q4; management says the market corrected finished goods prices after April input price rises.
About 65-70% of volume is under contract, with the rest non-contractual; roughly 40% of revenue is exposed to anti-dumping products.

DGTR gave positive final findings in March 2026 for antioxidant TDQ and Sulphenamides (CBS and NS), subject to central government approval, which management expects around mid-June (about 90 days). Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA findings are pending, with Pilflex 13 expected within a month or two.
Imports rose in Jan-Feb 2026 YoY; management linked this to FTA routes (Thailand, Korea) and year-end advance-licence imports. The company is pressing the government on FTA value-addition norms.
Management assumes 2-2.5% long-term global rubber demand growth, and 7% domestic demand growth per ICRA.
Competitive intensity is rising from Chinese players in latex, and 6PPD alternatives are at trial stage, with the company working on them.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers negotiating on price or prioritising volume security, and what is the contract mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says talks are positive but weighted to supply reliability; contract share is about 65-70%, with the rest non-contract and repriced first.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA not benefit from inflation given inventory on hand?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy high-cost inventory from the prior year spilled into H1 FY26, and the FTA-driven removal of basic duty on one product compressed spreads. Q4 also had a Rs.7-8 crore stock change debit and March production cuts from gas costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides lift margins, and what are the timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quantum is premature to assess; the Finance Ministry decision is expected around mid-June, and historically exporters have absorbed duties, so net benefit is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume and mix outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets double-digit volume growth in coming years, with new products adding to volumes gradually through FY27 and not yet material.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs.130 crore project's volume impact and is it merchant?
qa_highlights.answer: Largely additional capacity, not debottlenecking; the Rs.250 crore Dahej capex volume is fully merchant. The Rs.130 crore project is partly captive intermediates. Capacity figures were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still confident about cost reduction and conversion cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilities and other expenses fell by about Rs.10-11 crore; other expenses fell Rs.18-20 crore in FY26. No specific FY27 conversion-cost target was given.

risks_watch: Raw material supply (amines, MIBK) and gas-linked costs amid Middle East disruption; management says supplies are secure for the next few weeks.
Outcome of central government review of ADD on TDQ and Sulphenamides (around mid-June), and pending Pilflex 13 and 4ADPA DGTR findings.
Whether price hikes actually stick in Q1 FY27 given import competition and customer volume-security concerns.

Ramp-up timing of new Dahej capacity, with tyre-customer approvals taking 6-8 months.
Environmental regulation risk on 6PPD, the largest rubber chemical, with alternatives still in trial.

500730|2026-06.headline: NOCIL Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 403 crore and EBITDA margin hit 11.2%, but volumes fell 3% QoQ on supply constraints.
500730|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 403 crore, up 20% YoY and 22% QoQ, with volumes up 9% YoY but down 3% QoQ. Management attributed the sequential volume dip to utility and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation, which pushed some orders into later quarters. EBITDA rose to Rs 45 crore (11.2% margin) and PAT to Rs 28 crore, though management described several conversion-cost items as one-offs. Anti-dumping duty on Sulphonamides (CBS and NS) was approved on 20 June 2026, while the Pilflex 13 duty awaits Government approval. FY27 guidance was set at revenue of Rs 1,400-1,600 crore and EBITDA around 10%.

segments.name: Non-tyre chemicals

segments.name: Exports

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 EBITDA run rate sustainable, and what are the one-off conversion cost items?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to around 10% EBITDA for FY27. Conversion cost rose from Rs 110 crore to Rs 130 crore QoQ due to freight, CSR spend, utility cost from gas constraints, plant maintenance, and a Rs 45 crore stock change. Management called some items one-offs, quantified only as 'a few crores' of maintenance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 volume growth guidance (around 10%) below expectations of double-digit export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the impact has been mainly in non-tyre and not in tyre, and it has not cut the 10% FY27 volume growth outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ADD benefit will flow to EBITDA, and what is the inventory gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to quantify the ADD benefit. It did not provide an inventory gain estimate and will come back on that later.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the 9% volume growth came from tyre and non-tyre?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was skewed towards tyres, with a lower contribution from non-tyre.

qa_highlights.question: Will the TDQ plant generate revenue this year, and at what utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, revenue is expected this year. Non-tyre customers come first, followed by tyre companies over the next couple of quarters as approvals come through. No utilisation figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why might the Pilflex 13 ADD be approved this time when it was rejected in 2021?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Central Government has discretion, with a decision expected within about 90 days, possibly by end-September. It argued that domestic producers are under more stress now, so the case is stronger.

500730|2026-09.headline: NOCIL H1 FY27 revenue rose 26% to Rs.830 crore on higher prices; Q2 volumes fell 3% YoY on supply and logistics constraints, and FY27 guided to upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore.
500730|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs.427 crore, up 33% YoY and 6% QoQ, driven mainly by higher average selling prices, while volumes fell 3% YoY and 7% QoQ due to temporary supply-side and logistics constraints linked to the geopolitical situation. Q2 EBITDA was Rs.36 crore (8.4% margin), up 61% YoY but down 20% QoQ; PAT was Rs.24 crore, up 98% YoY and down 13% QoQ. Management says the supply issues are now addressed, expects volumes to recover in H2, and remains confident of FY27 revenue at the upper end of Rs.1,400-1,600 crore with EBITDA margin around 10%. Import dumping and higher utility, coal, gas and freight costs weighed on the quarter.

segments.name: Exports

Antidumping duty on 4ADPA (precursor to PILFLEX-13) was not notified or accepted by the government; the effect on domestic peers would be indirect and uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of H2 volume growth, given FY27 assumptions imply an index of about 165, and does this carry into FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 8-10% volume growth for the year, with H2 index at least 160-165, coming from both domestic and international markets; it agreed 10% is a fair FY28 assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Is the revenue and margin guidance conservative given run-rate math implying about Rs.180 crore EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged some conservatism given the evolving environment, but said it will strive to achieve more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for conversion costs, which rose by Rs.10-20 per kg as freight and power benefits faded?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher coal and gas costs and sea freight drove the increase; management expects H2 leverage from higher volumes to help once supply constraints are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much additional margin can ADD on 4ADPA provide, and what is the sulfonamides benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: 4ADPA duty on PILFLEX-13 precursor was not notified; the impact on domestic peers is indirect. Sulfonamides import data is unavailable, so the benefit cannot be quantified, though some is factored into pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the realisation increase comes from ADD versus cost pass-through, and is the steady-state margin weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADD is only on sulfonamides, a small portion of the business; the price increase mainly reflects cost pass-through, plus an improved value-add shift this year, with the ADD share not quantifiable.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory risk is there from input-price reversal, and when will TDQ be capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital has fallen to about 25% of sales; inventory is held for roughly 40-60 days with no significant near-term effect. TDQ capitalisation awaits customer approvals, hoped for in Q3, adding about Rs.3 crore depreciation per quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gross profit per tonne sustained, and how much is ADD versus market conditions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ADD was part of Q2 gross margin but not all of it; market conditions improved versus last year, with the gross profit run rate up from about Rs.520-525 crore to Rs.700 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the implied H2 realisation and capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current pricing shows a marginal uptick in Q3 versus H1; the Rs.130 crore Board-sanctioned capex will be spent across H2 FY27 and H1 FY28 alongside maintenance capex.

500770|2026-03.headline: Tata Chemicals Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 274 crores from INR 327 crores, with a INR 1,837 crore goodwill impairment in US.
500770|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue fell 2% YoY to INR 3,438 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA at INR 274 crores versus INR 327 crores a year earlier on subdued soda ash prices across geographies. An exceptional charge of INR 1,837 crores for US goodwill impairment (USD 208 million) and a INR 159 crores deferred tax write-off drove a loss after exceptional items. Standalone revenue rose 3% to INR 1,254 crores but EBITDA fell 6% to INR 216 crores on lower realisation. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input and shipping costs, which were largely passed through, and that the company exited unremunerative Southeast Asia exports.

500770|2026-06.headline: Tata Chemicals Q1 FY27: standalone EBITDA up 35% on volumes and FX-led soda ash pricing, while consolidated EBITDA fell about INR 100 crore on sharply lower realisations.
500770|2026-06.overview: Tata Chemicals reported Q1 FY27 with consolidated revenue up 14% YoY but EBITDA down about INR 100 crore despite lower realisations, mainly from soda ash pressure in the industrial segment. Standalone performed strongly: revenue up 10%, EBITDA up 35%, and PAT from continuing operations up 12%, helped by higher volumes, an INR 2,000/tonne soda ash price increase in India, and fixed-cost control. The company moved to three reporting segments (Living Essentials, Industrial Essentials, Farm Essentials) to highlight non-cyclical revenue, and net debt fell INR 5,692 crore QoQ on asset monetisation (management later cited about INR 300 crore of debt reduction versus March). Management flagged that cost pressures from the Middle East conflict (Kenya HFO, UK gas, India limestone and coal logistics) could intensify after October.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rationale for the segment reclassification, and will it change the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is to reshape the portfolio toward non-cyclical, sustainability-led products with stickier customers and lower price volatility, with capital allocation following. Geography-wise P&L will still be disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp India margin expansion despite lower soda ash and bicarbonate volumes (down about 12% and 19% QoQ)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited plant optimisation that shifted production toward higher salt volumes, lower-cost coal inventory that will unwind next quarter, and some bicarbonate tender contracts forgone for pricing reasons. It said about 18% is a sustainable India EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the status and economics of the sodium-ion battery and recycling businesses?

qa_highlights.answer: Management said annualised capex will be around depreciation and not above it. The CFO confirmed about INR 1,200 crore (FY26 consolidated depreciation) as the FY27 figure.

qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost includes about INR 43 crore of one-off items, with the rest mainly rupee depreciation and Q1 variable pay. IMACID did not run in Q1 due to high sulfur prices and is expected to be profitable for FY27.

500770|2026-09.headline: Tata Chemicals standalone Q2 FY27 EBITDA rose 22% to ₹292 crore, while consolidated profit fell to ₹381 crore from ₹537 crore on UK gas costs and Kenya suspension.
500770|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue grew 8% YoY in Q2 to about ₹1,300 crore and EBITDA rose 22% to ₹292 crore, helped by higher salt, FOS and silica volumes. Standalone PAT fell 31% to ₹122 crore. Consolidated results were hit by sharp UK gas cost increases, higher freight and energy costs, lower overseas soda ash realisations and the suspension of Kenya operations. Management described soda ash pricing as under pressure with range-bound expectations, citing China oversupply and a 1.89 million tonne Chinese producer inventory.

segments.commentary: Performed better on higher salt, FOS and silica volumes; depreciation from capitalised projects and higher finance cost weighed on profit. Domestic soda ash pricing softened late in the year as imports rose.

segments.commentary: Revenue rose on volumes from contracts acquired in Chapter 11 process (~0.5 million tonnes over two years), partly offset by lower export pricing. Searles Valley acquisition cost $22 million, amortised as intangible over 5 years.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on lower salt realisations; variable costs rose sharply on gas prices, and bicarbonate also faced higher soda ash feedstock costs. Management called the spikes very recent.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.commentary: Operations remain suspended following a Ministry of Mining notice; management said the business had continued to earn positive margins before suspension.

segments.name: Agrochemicals / Crop care (Soil health)
segments.commentary: Demand was affected by a deficient monsoon and delayed sowing, with recovery later in the season; crop care and soil health grew and profitability was pressured by input costs.

segments.commentary: Sales performance was in line with expectation; company has exited most Southeast Asia contracts as they were unremunerative.

qa_highlights.question: Accounting treatment and pricing of the Searles Valley deal?

qa_highlights.question: Will other US producers' shutdowns lead Tata Chemicals to cut US capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it had exited most Southeast Asia business earlier as unremunerative, and it will focus on North and South America and Asian markets with positive netbacks.

500780|2026-03.headline: Zuari Industries guides net debt to about INR700 crores by FY26-end, dependent on ~INR850-900 crore Dubai inflows over six months.
500780|2026-03.overview: Sugar operations delivered record crushing of 159.7 lakh quintal and 101.7% capacity utilisation in FY26, with sugar realisation up to INR4,053/quintal from INR3,894. Standalone PAT turned to INR12 crore from a loss of INR37 crore, and consolidated PAT was INR105 crore versus a loss of INR94.4 crore. Management says the St. Regis Dubai project (98% complete, BCC received 21 May 2026) is the main deleveraging lever, with external borrowings of about INR1,900 crore expected to fall to about INR700 crore by year-end. Ethanol remains under pressure from stagnant prices and roughly 100% industry overcapacity, and the Envien bioethanol JV is still stabilising with OMC tenders delayed.

500780|2026-06.headline: Zuari Q1 FY27 standalone loss widened to INR9.5 crore PAT on sugar margin squeeze; Dubai St. Regis repatriation of INR142.58 crore received so far against INR900 crore FY27 target.
500780|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income rose 26% YoY to INR283.9 crore on higher sugar volumes and realisations, but EBITDA fell to INR31.3 crore from INR36.9 crore and PAT swung to a loss of INR9.5 crore from a loss of INR3.9 crore. Management attributed margin pressure to an 8% rise in UP cane SAP (INR370 to INR400 per quintal). Consolidated PAT was a marginal INR0.05 crore, supported by associate income, mainly Zuari Agro Chemicals. Management reiterated the INR900 crore Dubai repatriation target for FY27 and said that sugar prices are at record highs, which it expects to support the next quarters.

500790|2026-06.headline: Nestlé India says volume growth has been double-digit for recent quarters and ad spend is up ~40%, but gives no numeric FY27 guidance.

Management said volume-led growth has accelerated over the last four to five quarters, with double-digit volume growth in recent quarters versus a 4.2% five-year volume CAGR. Advertising investment has been raised by close to 40% in recent quarters, which management funds from cost-saving programmes (2.6% of cost base saved in 2025 versus a normal 1.8–1.9%). Management declined to give forward projections, said 40% ad growth will not persist every quarter, and flagged macro headwinds from energy, packaging, oil, shipping and currency.

500825|2026-03.headline: Britannia Q4 FY26 revenue rose 7.1% to INR 4,686 crore, with PAT up 21.1% to INR 678 crore helped by a tax case release.
500825|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR 4,686 crore (+7.1% YoY) and FY26 revenue was INR 18,858 crore (+7.5%). Q4 PAT of INR 678 crore (+21.1%) was lifted by income tax case closures, so underlying profit growth was weaker. Management attributed the India slowdown in March to dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs after the GST transition, which hit wholesale and rural channels, plus West Asia disruption to international dispatches. Management guided to price increases from this quarter to offset fuel and laminate inflation.

financial_highlights.change: +21.1% YoY; 14.5% of revenue; boosted by income tax case releases

segments.name: Domestic India
segments.commentary: Growth was about 9% to 9.5% in Q4 before dual-pricing drag; management said it expects a few hundred bps of lost sales to recover. Retail (75% of business) is growing well, while wholesale (25%) was hit.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce was 6% of domestic sales in FY26 versus 4% in FY25, and management put it above 12% excluding the INR 5 and INR 10 packs. Quick commerce is about 70% of e-commerce, which management expects to reach 85%.

segments.name: International (West Asia)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability were hit in Q4 by vessel unavailability through the Strait of Hormuz and weaker demand in West Asia markets. Management said the business was negative for March, and Oman production for North America has moved back to Mundra.

segments.name: Adjacencies and signature brands
segments.commentary: Wafers are growing at healthy double digits and dairy at double digits, led by ghee. Treat, Little Hearts and Jim Jam are growing about 3x company growth, and cake and rusk is growing about 1.4x biscuits.

guidance_outlook: Calibrated price increases start from Q1 FY27, through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10.
Management expects the domestic market to stabilize by quarter-end as dual pricing fades, and expects wholesale and rural volumes to recover.
Sourcing optimisation between India and international plants is expected to be fully operational by mid-May 2026.
Management expects biscuit industry sequential growth to resume from June with monsoon and school reopening.
Management is committed to continued cost efficiency programmes (CEP) and plans to step up advertising and brand investment, with no quantified FY27 margin guidance.
No specific FY27 revenue or margin number was given; management said it is confident of a good year.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing for North America was moved from Oman back to Mundra, enabling dispatch to North America.
Management is evaluating alternate fuels and energy sources as long-term hedges against fuel supply shocks.
Renewable electricity share in own plants rose 14%, and specific water consumption fell 7%.
Management did not announce new capacity or capex figures.
demand_pricing: Dual pricing of INR 5 and INR 10 packs (competitor selling at INR 4.5 and INR 9) hit rural and wholesale channels from January through March; the 60-65% of biscuits sold at these price points are most exposed.
Management said the gap is about 200 to 400 bps in sales, but it cannot precisely quantify the impact.
Price realisation on the INR 5 and INR 10 segment is lower than the competitor's, so management believes value share is unaffected.

Raw material view: wheat is deflationary but has risen over the past month on rains and quality; palm oil is covered for 5 months; sugar stable; cocoa lower; laminate and fuel (LPG, CNG) are inflationary.
Wheat inventory is covered for about 5.5 to 6 months at attractive prices; palm oil is covered for 5 months.
Other expenses rose 18% on 7% revenue growth, driven by higher advertising and brand investment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone growth lower in Q4 when Nov-Dec ran at about 12% and Jan-Feb at about 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the first two months of Q4 were reasonable, with dual pricing in rural and wholesale channels hitting throughout the quarter, and West Asia pulling March down. Domestic growth was about 9% to 9.5% before the dual-pricing drag.

qa_highlights.question: How much did dual pricing dampen sales growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was hypothetical to quantify, but the impact was roughly 200 to 400 bps. Growth in general trade key accounts is high-single to double digit, modern trade is about 15% to 16%, and e-commerce is above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What pricing action is needed given competitors are vacating INR 4.5 and INR 9 packs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will take selective price increases through grammage adjustments and some packs above INR 10. Other biscuit companies are moving gradually to full price points.

qa_highlights.question: Is Britannia under-indexed on INR 5 and INR 10 packs in e-commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not actively promote these packs online because premium packs drive more value and channel conflict is a concern. The packs remain available through search and in baskets.

qa_highlights.question: Will GST cut benefits reach biscuits, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the GST benefit is less visible on INR 5 and INR 10 packs than on higher price points. It expects benefits to show more in medium to long term, with the growth recovery in June.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q4 volume growth and how do pack counts look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth was about 5.5% by grammage. It acknowledged that transactions fell in wholesale and rural channels and expects this to correct over the next few months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for FY27 given cost pressures and higher investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will be selective on marketing spend, targeting the marketing mix for better returns, and expects to manage margins within a certain band. No quantified FY27 margin guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company pursue inorganic growth and new platforms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is actively scanning acquisitions that add new capabilities or address unmet needs, and that more platforms will be added, including health.

risks_watch: Recovery of dual-pricing-hit wholesale and rural channels and whether the INR 5 and INR 10 price points normalise.
Q4 PAT includes income tax case releases, so the reported 21.1% PAT growth is not recurring.
Fuel and laminate inflation, plus West Asia shipping and LPG constraints, could pressure margins and international operations.
Competitor (number 2 player) reported double-digit volume growth, which may signal share loss in INR 5 and INR 10 channels.
Rising other expenses (+18% YoY) from brand investment could weigh on margins in FY27.
Price increases could affect volumes, which management argues will remain resilient.

500825|2026-06.headline: Britannia Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 9.5% to INR 4,964 crore, with ~9% tonnage volume growth and PAT margin at 11.9%.
500825|2026-06.overview: Management said revenue from operations on a consolidated basis was about INR 4,964 crore, up 9.5% YoY, with standalone growth at 10%. PAT was 11.9% of revenue and grew 13.6% YoY. Management said the quarter exited in mid-teens growth after dual-pricing disruption in rural and wholesale channels faded in June. Input cost inflation from LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar and milk is a headwind, and management said only about half of it has been offset through price increases so far.

none booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27

segments.name: General Trade (GT)
segments.commentary: Management said GT demand picked up, with the recent run-rate about 1.5x the full-year FY26 growth rate. Key states are growing and other states are growing about 1.3x faster.

segments.name: E-commerce / Quick commerce
segments.commentary: E-commerce grew at strong double digits. Quick commerce is about 80-85% of e-commerce and is growing at healthy double digits.

segments.name: Other channels
segments.commentary: Newer channels were growing at about 2.5x the GT rate overall.

segments.name: Dairy and adjacencies
segments.commentary: Dairy grew at double digits. Cake, rusk and wafers grew at double digits led by portfolio innovation. Croissant lines were growing above 30% and Croissant run-rate was about INR 200 crore annualised (INR 100 crore ARR doubled).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Mixed quarter: pressure in Middle East and Saudi Arabia and headwinds in North America, offset by growth in Africa led by Kenya. Management expects a return to growth from this quarter.

segments.name: Eastern India
segments.commentary: Growing in double digits per management.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give explicit FY27 guidance. It said the team is confident of a good year, defined as balanced growth across volume, value and profitability.
Management expects roughly 1.5-2% more price realisation from shrinkflation changes to come through in the coming quarters, after about 1% in Q1.
Management said it is watching sugar, palm oil, milk and LPG/PNG costs ahead of the festive season and said the current cost level is higher than in February 2026.
Management said Q2 faces a base effect in September from the GST price transition last year, and July and August were normal months.
Brand-building spend is running ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given.
capex_capacity: Management said it is working to reduce LPG/PNG dependence through biomass and alternate fuels, but no timelines were given.
Renewable energy share in plant power rose 16%, and management is working to expand it under state rules.
A new Chief Business Officer for Dairy was appointed and a Strategy and Corporate Development head joined, with management saying the leadership team is now complete.
demand_pricing: Q1 volume growth was about 9% in tonnage terms; pricing contributed about 1% and was mainly shrinkflation in INR 5 and INR 10 packs.
Management said dual pricing disruption in rural and wholesale was felt in April and early May and ended in June. Demand was described as holding up.
Industrial fuel inflation was steep: LPG and PNG roughly 2.5x in April-May, now about 1.5x February levels. Palm oil is near INR 140 per kg, up more than 20%.
Management said it could mitigate about half of input inflation through price increases so far.
Sugar rose more than INR 7 per kg in the last 2-3 weeks. Flour has held up, but El Nino and rainfall are a watch item for wheat prices.
Management said it has regained market share on a sequential basis across many biscuit categories, following the end of dual pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the mid-teens exit growth in June, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company sells in based on sell-out, so no loading. The dual-pricing impact ended in June, which brought back some buyers, and organic demand held up. It gave no forward indication.

qa_highlights.question: How will ad spend and input inflation affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said LPG prices are about 1.5x February levels and sugar and palm oil are also up. Brand spend is ahead of sales growth, with no percentage given. Management said half of inflation has been offset by price increases.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 EBITDA margin hold at or above FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the input cost base is higher than in February. It did not commit to full-year margins, but said it is confident of managing levers across value, volume and margin.

qa_highlights.question: Are there PLI benefits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no PLI incentive was booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27, because the threshold growth was not achieved.

qa_highlights.question: How is Britannia responding to GT competition in Eastern India and other areas?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited regional empowerment, targeted media and influencer spend, and local product innovation such as Milk Bikis Thirukkural packs in Tamil Nadu. Sub-distributors are being converted to direct distributors.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the GST impact on volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said over 60% of sales are at INR 5 and INR 10 price points, so GST-cut elasticity will be gradual and smaller than for higher-priced packs.

500830|2026-03.headline: Colgate India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 1,583 crore, with domestic growth at 9.2% and gross margin at 69.6%.
500830|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 net sales were Rs 1,583 crore, up 9% YoY, with domestic growth of 9.2% and growth broad-based across Core, Premium, toothpaste, toothbrush and personal care. Full-year FY26 sales were flat at Rs 5,984 crore, and full-year EBITDA margin was 31.2% including an 80 bps GST input-credit (IDS) impact. Q4 NPAT was Rs 353 crore, and excluding one-offs (restructuring, GST, prior-period tax refunds, labour code) management said profit grew about 9%. Management declared an interim dividend of Rs 48 per share and said it is still paying out virtually 100% of NPAT.

financial_highlights.change: excluding one-offs, management says profit grew about 9%
absolute spend up 10%; FY26 13.7% of sales
stated as improved on prior years despite GST-blocked capital

segments.name: Toothpaste (Core: Colgate Strong Teeth, Max Fresh)
segments.commentary: Max Fresh is described as the fastest-growing franchise in the portfolio, with a blue variant in testing and new Sensorials variants (berry added). Management said consideration for all sub-brands is flat or rising versus original levels.

segments.name: Premium (Colgate Total, Visible White, PerioGard)
segments.commentary: Premium mix is up 35% over the past two years per management. Visible White Purple was launched 18 months ago and is described as the most successful launch in Colgate's history; PerioGard franchise is said to be doubling YoY. Management did not disclose the premium share of sales; e-commerce is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Toothbrush
segments.commentary: Management says Colgate is 1.7x its nearest competitor in the entry tier. New launches include a Rs 10 brush with 16g to 20g of toothpaste offered in the pack and a PerioGuard brush.

segments.name: Personal care (Palmolive)
segments.commentary: Palmolive focus is hand wash and body wash. Management said foaming hand wash is the leader in the category and growing at double digits in key channels; body wash is a partnership-led watch item.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin is expected to stay in the range seen in recent quarters over the next two quarters despite commodity and currency headwinds, offset by the Funding the Growth programme.
EBITDA is not guided to a specific level or expansion; it will be calibrated to advertising investment, with top-line growth and absolute profit as the stated priorities.
A price increase to offset the post-West Asia inflation is expected to be taken within a few weeks; category price increases are expected to be in the low single digits.
Management targets balanced volume and price-led growth but gave no numerical growth target.
Management is pursuing GST input-credit mitigation through supplier duty representations, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and transporter rate changes.
Brand investment is expected to rise further from the Q4 level of 12.6% of sales; FY26 was 13.7%.
capex_capacity: No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed in the call.
Direct outlets reach is 1.7 lakh; 2 lakh stores were added to reach in 2025.
Plant sustainability: recyclable tubes now fully adopted, renewable energy share moved from 40% to 60%, plastic neutrality at 101%, recyclable/reusable/compostable packaging at 95%.
demand_pricing: Q4 growth was balanced between price and volume, and management said Q4 volume was flat.
Post-GST price cuts have been lapped after the Q1 calendar 2026 anniversary, so the price increase is now needed for input-cost inflation.
Rural demand is recovering and is beginning to converge with urban growth, though rural is growing more slowly than in 2025.
Promotional intensity has not eased; management is using AI tools to cull promotions and redeploying the spend.
Premium portfolio is growing faster than the core; management cited the 130-140 index to the core as the premium threshold.
Quick commerce share is ahead of total e-commerce, which is ahead of the offline business.

qa_highlights.question: How has the QR-linked dentist recommendation programme helped premiumisation, and how is B2B sales to dentists growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 4.5 million people were scanned, with around 20% of scans going to a dentist; the programme is being repeated and expanded to a virtual format via QR codes on 500 packs. B2B sales to the profession grew at about a 50-60% two-year CAGR, with a field force of about 150 people.

qa_highlights.question: Competitors have launched similar products (for example Purple); is the market expanding and what is the D2C threat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Purple is accelerating and it aims to hold the largest share of the whitening segment. Most D2C brands are still small, and Colgate's quick-commerce share is ahead of its e-commerce share, so there is no loss of share.

qa_highlights.question: Is pricing growth in Q4 from the price increase, and will the West Asia-linked inflation be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 growth was about half price and half volume, with the post-GST price cuts now lapped. A price increase for inflation is expected within a few weeks; gross margin should stay in range but EBITDA will depend on advertising.

qa_highlights.question: How should volume growth be viewed going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aim is balanced volume and price growth, not reliance on price as in the past, and not relying too heavily on volume.

qa_highlights.question: How is premium defined and what share of sales does it represent?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium is defined as products at a 130-140 price index to the core range and outside Active Salt, Max Fresh and Cibac. Premium's contribution has risen 35% in two years; management declined to disclose the premium share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY26 EBITDA margin at a sustainable level, and is there room to expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin will keep improving through the Funding the Growth programme. It gave no EBITDA margin target, saying advertising spend is the key variable and top-line and absolute profit growth are the priorities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the GST inverted duty structure and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 80 bps (full year) and 160 bps (Q4) IDS impact stays in the baseline. Mitigation includes lower GST on transport services, refunds in non-manufacturing states, and supplier representations for lower input GST.

qa_highlights.question: Did higher-grammage packs drive Q4 growth, and what is the top-line growth target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grammage increases of about 11% on a few packs were a pass-through of the GST cut, but were not the main driver of growth. 30-40% of SKUs are already higher-grammage. No numeric growth target was given; management stated top-line growth is a priority.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from commodity and currency costs, and the GST inverted duty structure (IDS) impact of 80 bps for FY26 and 160 bps in Q4.
Rising advertising intensity (Q4 12.6% of sales, FY26 13.7%) may keep EBITDA margins under pressure.
Competitive intensity in premium whitening, with copycat launches and D2C brands in toothpaste; promotional intensity has not eased.
Timing and size of the price increase for input-cost inflation; whether volume growth can be sustained alongside price.
Whether the rural demand recovery continues and whether the Q4 acceleration in growth holds.
500830|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the brand, premium portfolio and cash generation, but cautious on FY27 margins, with no EBITDA guidance. Management was evasive on the premium share of sales and on the timing and size of pricing.
