500840|2026-03.headline: EIH Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue up 10% but EBITDA up only 1% on business mix, wage code and higher expenses; FY26 PAT hit by Rs 30 Cr wage code charge.
500840|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a very volatile year (Operation Sindoor, West Asia conflict, monsoon rains, December flight disruptions, late-February West Asia war) but said EBITDA was the highest in company history. Q4 consolidated revenue grew 10% while EBITDA grew 1%, with profit from operations down 5% on higher tax expense, business mix shift toward lower-margin OFS (flight catering), higher airport levy, repair and maintenance, CSR, legal and donation costs. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 8% and EBITDA 3%; reported PAT fell on a one-time Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and the Mashobra fair-value charge from the prior year, and management said excluding these profit grew 2%. Management said April and May trends were better than expected, led by domestic demand.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated profit from operations, Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: +3% YoY; PAT lower on Rs 30 Cr wage code impact and Mashobra one-time charge

financial_highlights.metric: Own hotels FY26 room revenue / F&B revenue
Cash and funds balance, end FY26
financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,335 Cr vs Rs 1,051 Cr at end March 2025

segments.name: Oberoi hotels (luxury)
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 4.2% vs luxury segment 6%, dragged by Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; FY26 RevPAR up 10.4% vs Indian luxury 6.4%. RGI 204 in Q4 and 191 for FY26, both above last year.

segments.name: Trident hotels (upper upscale)
segments.commentary: FY26 RevPAR up 10.2%, against 5% for the upper upscale segment, on both occupancy and ARR gains versus competition.

segments.name: International hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 RevPAR up 13%, with Mauritius, Oberoi Zahra and Sahl Hasheesh the main contributors.

segments.name: OFS (flight catering)
segments.commentary: Q4 business about Rs 145 Cr, driven mainly by existing airlines with larger flight counts and market share; this segment carries airport levy costs that weighed on margins.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give forward numbers; said April and May were better than expected, led by strong domestic demand.
Foreign business (about 50% of Q4 business historically) hit by West Asia war; management expects the impact to be limited in summer months, with foreign travel peaking October to March.
Management expects a big summit in Q2 and Q3 FY27 to benefit demand, following AI Summit benefit in February-March.
Capex of about Rs 600-700 Cr a year to continue for the next one to two years, rising in FY29-30 when larger hotels open.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata partial opening still targeted for September 2026; Trident Vizag opens 2027; 825 owned/associate keys and 1,893 managed keys in pipeline by 2030.
Mashobra hotel O&M continues until October 2026; management awaits further developments.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex about Rs 680 Cr: about Rs 330 Cr on Mumbai land conversion (leasehold to freehold), Rs 125 Cr on Oberoi Rajgarh, about Rs 100 Cr on ongoing renovations (Kolkata and others), remainder replacement capex.
Oberoi Rajgarh opened November 2025, total 3,800 keys in business with Rajgarh added in Q3; about 400 international keys.

Pipeline: 825 owned/associate keys by 2030, starting with Trident Vizag (2027) via EIH Associated Hotels; Hebbal mixed-use site (about 1.3 million sq ft development, including about 7.6 lakh sq ft commercial) by 2030.
Managed pipeline: 24 hotels, 1,893 keys; two new Trident management contracts added (Amritsar, 150 keys; Pawna, 150 keys), signed between Q3 and Q4.

Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) renovation under way with structural works; reopening targeted September 2026. Oberoi Grand Kolkata cited as timeline issue; separately, Oberoi Gandikota site delay moved from 2028 to 2030 due to site change.

Renovations: about 90 rooms at Oberoi Bangalore in 18-room blocks over summer; Trident Nariman Point 4 floors (six months); 4 floors at Oberoi Mumbai one floor at a time; F&B overhaul at Trident Bandra Kurla later in FY27.
demand_pricing: Q4 industry occupancy 67-69%, below last year on West Asia war impact; industry ARR up 6-8% and RevPAR up 5-7%. FY26 industry occupancy flat, ARR up 9-10%, RevPAR up 10-12%.

Occupancy weakened through Q4 with a sharp drop in March; ARR for EIH owned hotels rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4. January RevPAR negative (about -6%), which management attributed to unexplained weak demand, possibly negative international press on air quality.
Delhi/NCR, Mumbai (T20 World Cup) and Bhubaneswar grew strongly; Bangalore hit by lower foreign bookings; Udaipur down on fewer weddings.
Room revenue: MICE and direct segments grew; corporate and leisure flat.
Management says India is significantly underpriced versus Europe, North America and parts of Asia at the top end; no reason to discount rates given rate premium strategy.

qa_highlights.question: What drove February ARR growth near 25% and why was January RevPAR negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was weak, with promotions having limited effect; the likely cause (unvalidated) was negative international press on North India air quality. February was strong, helped by the AI Summit, deferred winter travel and strong demand across leisure and city hotels.

qa_highlights.question: With few owned key additions in FY27-28, what drives growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Two levers: ARR (premium positioning, headroom if market stays buoyant) and cost elimination of waste rather than cuts. No specific growth guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 flight catering (OFS) revenue and was it new clients?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 145 Cr in Q4, mainly existing airlines expanding flights and market share, including some domestic airlines.

qa_highlights.question: Where do foreign tourist mix and Q4 FTA levels stand?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 foreign business about 50% historically; domestic share rose substantially in March and more than offset weaker foreign demand. Exact March quarter mix to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a financial loss from geopolitical issues in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: No financial impact calculated; lower foreign room nights were offset by domestic business.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise about 20% in Q4 and will Mashobra O&M continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher expenses from business growth, higher airport levy on OFS, higher R&M, CSR, legal and donation costs. Mashobra case settled in June; hotel operated until October 2026.

risks_watch: Margin pressure: Q4 EBITDA only 1% growth as OFS mix rises and airport levy and wage code costs increase; watch for margin recovery in FY27.
Managed hotel project slippage (Trident Goa, Dehradun, Rishikesh and others); management says owners control timelines and delays are not significant, but 2027 pipeline looks thin.
Oberoi Grand Kolkata renovation: structural issues found, reopening target September 2026 still stated; any change would be updated to the board and investors.
Oberoi Rajgarh (Khajuraho) connectivity: only seasonal Delhi flights; no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.
Geopolitical risk: West Asia war impact on foreign travel and occupancy; the company has not quantified the impact; March occupancy weakness may persist into Q1 FY27.
Supply risk in FY29-30 from new luxury keys in some micro-markets; management says the rate premium will be maintained rather than discounted.
500840|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand and pipeline but cautious on near-term occupancy; management acknowledged a challenging year and avoided forward numbers, deferring several specifics (foreign mix, flight catering split, consolidated room revenue) to offline follow-up.

So overall, if you look at our investor update, we've almost spent 600 to 700 crores of CAPEX in the current year.

rows.why: Oberoi Grand Kolkata (about 200 keys) reopening targeted September 2026 and Trident Vizag due 2027 via EIH Associated Hotels, with 825 owned/associate keys in pipeline by 2030, but Oberoi Gandikota slipped from 2028 to 2030 and the 2027 pipeline looks thin.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Room revenue growth is supported by Trident RevPAR up 10.2% and Oberoi RevPAR up 10.4% in FY26 versus the market, April-May trends better than expected, and OFS volumes rising with existing airlines adding flights, offset by foreign weakness and a negative January RevPAR of about -6%.

rows.when: FY27-FY28 at Rs 600-700 Cr a year, stepping up in FY29-30
rows.why: FY26 capex was about Rs 680 Cr and management guided to continue at Rs 600-700 Cr a year for one to two years, with a higher step-up in FY29-30 as larger hotels open; full-year owned-hotel occupancy is 76.8-77%, below the 80%+ level that would trigger a new capex call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: April and May were better than expected led by domestic demand, own-hotel RevPAR rose about 8.5% to about Rs 17,400 for FY26, and a big summit is expected in Q2-Q3 FY27, but management gave no forward numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 consolidated EBITDA grew only 1% and PAT fell on the Rs 30 Cr wage code charge; West Asia war hit foreign business (about 50% of Q4 historically) and March occupancy dropped sharply, though management has not quantified the impact.

rows.label: Rate premium strategy: ARR up sharply
rows.why: EIH owned-hotel ARR rose from Rs 24,548 to Rs 28,198 in Q4 (about +15%), and management says India is underpriced versus Europe and North America and will not discount rates.

rows.why: Oberoi Rajgarh (3,800 keys in business, about 400 international keys) opened November 2025 and dragged Oberoi Q4 RevPAR to +4.2% versus the luxury segment at +6%; only seasonal Delhi flights and no flights expected July-September unless IndiGo extends.

rows.label: Cash build to Rs 1,335 Cr
rows.why: Cash and funds rose to Rs 1,335 Cr from Rs 1,051 Cr (up Rs 284 Cr) despite capex of about Rs 680 Cr in FY26, giving room to fund the Rs 600-700 Cr annual capex plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term demand, the pipeline and RevPAR outperformance versus peers and April-May trends, but cautious on near-term occupancy, foreign mix and margins; analysts pushed on February ARR, the negative January RevPAR, the flight catering split and the 2027 managed pipeline.

500840|2026-06.headline: EIH Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% to Rs 698 crore and PAT to Rs 120 crore, but EBITDA grew only to Rs 207 crore as margin fell on Rajgarh ramp-up and one-offs.
500840|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to Rs 698 crore (Rs 609 crore) and EBITDA rose to Rs 207 crore from Rs 195 crore, so margin compressed. Management attributed the gap to Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up, about Rs 4 crore of extra marketing, IT/automation spend, power and fuel inflation from the West Asia conflict, and Rs 6-7.5 crore of renovation write-offs at Mumbai hotels. Growth was domestically led as foreign arrivals fell about 10% in Q1. Standalone numbers were stated to mirror consolidated. PAT of Rs 120 crore is not comparable with last year, which carried a Rs 110 crore Mashobra one-time impact.

qa_highlights.question: Did flight catering mix and renovation, Rajgarh ramp-up drive the margin gap, and will these persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations concentrate in lean months and Bombay renovations finish before October; Rajgarh should improve in winter. Flight catering was profitable and not a material margin drag.

qa_highlights.question: May and June RevPAR growth looked much higher than the quarter. Will that persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast the full year; said Q2 business on books versus last year was very positive.

qa_highlights.question: Will large events like BRICS and the Aviation show boost RevPAR?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, large events have a ripple effect across cities, with Delhi and Mumbai benefiting from overseas visitors to Bengaluru's air show.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Kolkata Oberoi delayed and how firm is the new timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Heritage building restoration uncovered fire and structural safety work, plus a Kolkata construction halt after a fatal incident about two months ago; halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost overrun on the Oberoi Grand from delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays add cost, the size depending on reasons, and the bigger impact is deferred revenue and profit from delayed market entry.

qa_highlights.question: Can the Mumbai outperformance continue, and what is foreign tourist trend in recent months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bombay market was strong and EIH beat it, but would not forecast 20% outperformance; Q2 foreign trend expected to stay weak.

qa_highlights.question: Rajgarh stabilisation timeline and winter outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 3 years to stabilise for a leisure hotel, with winter months from October expected to do considerably better.

qa_highlights.question: How much did the base business margin fall after adjusting for Rajgarh and one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ex-Rajgarh margin was about 30.6% vs last year, with roughly Rs 9 crore YoY impact from power and fuel, Rs 4 crore marketing, IT and renovation costs. Management declined to disclose management fee income.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on Oberoi Rajgarh ramp-up; management guides about 3 years to stabilise and expects winter months from October to be considerably better.
Foreign arrivals were about 10% below last year in Q1 and management expects Q2 foreign trend to stay weak; normalisation in Q3-Q4 depends on West Asia stabilising.
Power and fuel costs rose due to the West Asia/Hormuz crisis; ex-Rajgarh impact about Rs 9 crore YoY, with cost pressure expected to persist.

Kolkata Oberoi timeline pushed to 2029 with construction halt still in place pending building-by-building approvals; Oberoi Grand opening Sept 2028 with management declining to give percentage completion.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic demand, Trident and Mumbai share gains and Q2 bookings, but guarded on forward numbers, declining full-year guidance, Rajgarh revenue, flight catering margin and management fees; analysts pressed on margin drag, Kolkata delay and Oberoi Grand cost overrun.

500850|2026-03.headline: IHCL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% to INR2,845 crores with EBITDA margin of 37%; FY27 guidance is double-digit (12-14%) revenue growth.
500850|2026-03.overview: IHCL reported its 16th consecutive quarter of record performance, with Q4 consolidated revenue up 14% YoY to INR2,845 crores and EBITDA up 15% to INR1,052 crores. Standalone Q4 RevPAR grew 12%, the company said, with standalone EBITDA margin up 160 bps to 49.5%. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 16% to INR9,971 crores and consolidated PAT crossed INR2,000 crores for the first time. Management said March and early April were weak due to the West Asia conflict, with recovery from mid-April, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 12-14%, with Q1 FY27 growth expected above 12%.

segments.name: Standalone hotels
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR1,721 crores with 12% RevPAR growth and 49.5% EBITDA margin; FY26 revenue INR5,640 crores (+10%) and EBITDA margin 45.1% (+120 bps).

segments.name: New businesses (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Stays & Trails, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR753 crores, up 25%, with a 31% four-year CAGR. Ginger Mumbai Airport crossed INR100 crores revenue at a 56% EBITDA margin; Qmin has 100-plus outlets and GMV near INR200 crores.

segments.name: TajSATS (catering)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth of 16% was flattered by an airport levy accounting change; management said growth would have been about 11-12% on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Ginger consolidated (Roots and Ginger Mumbai Airport)
segments.commentary: Combined revenue about INR700-709 crores with a very high EBITDA margin; management now reports Ginger on a consolidated basis rather than Roots standalone.

guidance_outlook: FY27 double-digit revenue growth guided at 12-14%, with management confident of delivering it.
Like-for-like RevPAR planned at high-single-digit growth (about 7-9%) on a one- to two-year view; ARR is the main lever.
Non-like-for-like growth of about 4-5% expected in FY27 from around 60 hotel openings, and acquisitions expected to add over INR250 crores incremental revenue.
Q1 FY27 revenue growth expected to be above 12%, with domestic demand stronger than international.
Capex of INR1,000-1,200 crores annually; Ginger portfolio target of 250 hotels under development or operating by end-FY27.
Next Capital Market Day to be announced within weeks; capital-light share guided at 63% on the prior framework, with ANK & Pride amendments pointing toward about 70%.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex over INR1,000 crores: about INR650 crores on renovations, routine maintenance and digital, and the rest on greenfield projects.
Over the last three years, more than INR2,500 crores invested in capex; more than INR500 crores deployed across four acquisitions.
Portfolio of over 630 hotels and 64,000-plus keys; pipeline of 31,000-plus keys, 93% capital-light; 68% of operating portfolio under managed or asset-light formats.
FY27 openings of about 60 hotels (around 5,000 keys, give or take 5%); Frankfurt delayed to around June 2026; 15 ANK & Pride conversions expected to open in Q1 FY27.
Atmantan and ANK & Pride integration on track, with benefits expected in H2 FY27; President Mumbai renovation completed.
demand_pricing: Goa grew about 25% in April (some hotels 30%+); Mumbai and Delhi face high bases after strong prior years; Dubai and Maldives are down, London is okay, and domestic is strong.
West Asia conflict cost about INR40-50 crores of consolidated revenue and close to INR100 crores on an enterprise basis from last-minute event cancellations and rescheduling.

Foreign tourists are about 30% of standalone guests and this share has not moved much; management says foreign business arrivals are rising while leisure tourist arrivals remain below pre-COVID levels.
Rupee-denominated portal pricing; domestic drive vacations and MICE consolidation into domestic resorts are supporting demand.

Management says supply is tight for the foreseeable future, so RevPAR should grow at least at inflation; revenue management and a website channel shift added about 2 percentage points to distribution mix.
Lands End Mumbai runs at 90%+ occupancy, so growth there is rate-led.

qa_highlights.question: How are April and current trading, and what drives FY27 growth of 12-14%?
qa_highlights.answer: March and early April were difficult, with stability from mid-April and strong growth since. Management built the guide from key account rates, wedding bookings on the books, about 4-5% non-like-for-like growth from openings, and renovated inventory; ARR is the swing factor.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company cut the FY27 openings count?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the figure is roughly 5,000 keys on average per year, give or take 5%. Platform partnerships could add 300-400 keys, and most openings are management contracts, so the P&L impact is small.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ANK & Pride portfolio change the long-term capital-light mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix moved toward 70% capital-light from the 63% target at the Analyst Day, because ANK & Pride is largely capital-light with only a few owned hotels. The change is additive and does not reflect any sale of capital-heavy assets.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve and is there operating leverage left?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is still room for margin improvement because the newer brands are still scaling and acquisition costs were high. It is comfortable with the 35% consolidated margin provided new brands are not built with upfront capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q1 FY27 trading and the MICE cancellation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q1 revenue growth above 12%, with domestic outpacing international. Some MICE business was deferred rather than lost, such as the company's own hospitality conference; some nights are permanently lost.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict and its effect on international travel, Dubai transit traffic and London hotels.
Aviation cost and capacity cuts by domestic carriers, which could hit travel demand and pricing.
Frankfurt opening slipping to around June 2026 and the pace of the 60-hotel opening plan.
Mumbai and Delhi high bases, which could slow like-for-like growth.
Clarity of the new Capital Market Day guidance on ROCE and the capital-light mix.
500850|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the medium term, with guidance tempered by explicit caution on West Asia impacts in March-April. Management was candid on the weak start to Q1 and deflected some questions on specific numbers, e.g. the segment breakdown and the 7-9% ARR bridge, saying they are an art rather than a science.
key_quotes: We remain fairly confident that we will again deliver double-digit growth between 12%, let's say, and 14% in the FY '27 fiscal.
The business was a bit sluggish. I would say March was a difficult month. Beginning of April was difficult.
This time, we have none, and we have a lot of cash. So, it might throw other opportunities.

500850|2026-06.headline: IHCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR2,419 crores and PAT 21% to INR358 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.1%.
500850|2026-06.overview: IHCL reported its 17th consecutive quarter of record performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% YoY to INR2,419 crores, EBITDA up 18% to INR753 crores and PAT up 21% to INR358 crores. Domestic RevPAR grew 14% and hotel segment revenue 17%, driven by leisure markets like Rajasthan and Goa while international properties, especially Dubai, lagged due to West Asia disruption. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,298 crores with EBITDA up 30% to INR542 crores and margin of 41.8%. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for the year and said July and early Q2 trends were strong.

financial_highlights.change: c.+6 pts YoY (analyst cited 35% to 39%ish; mgmt said margin up 0.5%)

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel segment revenue grew 17% and makes up about 87% of business; domestic RevPAR grew 14%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands. Margin held at 32.6% despite about INR15 crores of Frankfurt ramp-up and TajSATS Noida kitchen costs.

segments.name: Growth brands (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger consolidated revenue INR183 crores, up 20% YoY with 39% EBITDA margin. Ama has 380+ bungalows, 196 operational; Tree of Life has 40+ resorts, 23 operational; Qmin at 100+ outlets.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Brij, Atmantan)
segments.commentary: Brij's 11 operational hotels generated INR11 crores revenue, up 42% YoY. Atmantan delivered INR19 crores consolidated revenue, up 19% YoY.

segments.name: TajSATS / air catering
segments.commentary: Air catering revenue rose 3% while EBITDA fell 1%, as second-largest airline capacity cuts hit flight catering volumes; non-flight catering grew mid-20s% at lower margin.

capex_capacity: Operational hotels at 382 with about 265 in pipeline; 20 hotels signed and 11 opened in Q1, 17 of signings under Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life.
Frankfurt new asset ramping up, with pre-opening and start-up costs weighing on Q1 and July-August.
Taj Ganges Varanasi new 100-room wing commissioned March 2026, PBT-positive in first quarter, revenue up 44% and EBITDA margin 40%.
Taj Bandstand (Mumbai) targeted for 2030-2031 with about 450 keys and INR1,000 crores revenue; excavation 95% complete.
Ginger Bangalore Airport and a 350-room Ginger/Vivanta combo in 12-14 months; 300-room Ginger at Mopa Airport Goa under construction; Kolkata Airport Ginger under construction.
First of three lodges opened in Kruger National Park; two more to follow in about 12 months.
demand_pricing: Leisure markets strong: Rajasthan RevPAR up high 20s to 27-29%, Goa ARRs up double digit; big city hotels up low to mid-teens.
Standalone occupancy 82% vs 76% in the previous quarter; occupancy up about 6% on comparable domestic base.
Taj Palace room revenue up 32% and Fort Aguada room revenue up 45% after renovations.
International: Dubai business at about 80% of prior revenue in total (JLT 60%), Taj Exotica Palm below 50%; San Francisco recovering; New York pipe-burst cut 49 rooms.
Wedding and banqueting subdued; Africa Summit cancelled a week before start in May, hitting Delhi F&B and conference; government MICE slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Are MICE and domestic demand shifts from international travel accelerating into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trends continue into Q2 with no softening; leisure markets outperforming, and foreign arrivals still needed in Q3-Q4 for the sector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee cost rise only 0.6% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to a reversal from labour code benefits; normal payroll increases are 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth reach the upper end of 12-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is tracking ahead, with July stronger than Q1; it hopes to beat, but gave no explicit guidance raise.

qa_highlights.question: How will Frankfurt be accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Full revenue is booked; the asset's impact turns positive from September, after pre-opening costs in July and August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international strategy and capital intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital-light model only, with no hotel purchases; leases on institutional-style returns of 5-7% and brand-led renovations in Singapore, Switzerland and London.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the like-for-like growth is affected by renovated assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Slide 9 excludes Taj Palace, Fort Aguada, Blue Diamond and Calicut, which were under renovation last year, to give an apples-to-apples comparison.

risks_watch: Air catering margin pressure as Air India and IndiGo capacity cuts persist; management does not expect a quick rebound in Q2.
Dubai and Maldives/Sri Lanka exposure, with Palm leisure and Emirates connectivity still impaired.
Muted Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals and wedding and MICE recovery dependent on government events.
Frankfurt ramp-up in July-August, and New York rooms returning in 2-3 months.
Ginger conversion pace (15 in Q1, targets of 40 in Q4) and quality of rebranding.

We are at a 645 figure and we remain confident of crossing this milestone during the current month itself.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it expects to sustain margins, strong cash generation and improved quality of earnings.

500850|2026-09.headline: IHCL raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% after Q2 revenue rose 22% to INR2,484 crores and standalone EBITDA margin hit 38.9%.
500850|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was strong: consolidated operating revenue grew 22% YoY to INR2,484 crores, operating EBITDA grew 24% to INR706 crores (28.4% margin, up 50 bps), and PAT rose 23% to INR349 crores. Standalone operating revenue grew 26% to INR1,336 crores and standalone EBITDA grew 40% to INR520 crores, with margin up 400 bps to 38.9%. Management raised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 15%-17% from 12%-14%, with Hotel segment growth of 17%-19%. Occupancy rose to 82% from 75%, and TajSATS remained a drag on margins.

financial_highlights.value: Revenue and EBITDA growth of 25% and 30%

segments.name: Hotels (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 25% and EBITDA up 30% YoY; domestic hotel RevPAR up 25% and standalone RevPAR up 28%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands.

segments.name: Management fees
segments.commentary: Income up 25% to INR156 crores, driven by 25% growth in managed room inventory, higher RevPAR, technical fees and new brand fees from branded residences and villas; management targets high-teens fee CAGR.

segments.name: Select service (Ginger, Qmin, Ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger revenue INR193 crores (+25%) at 40% EBITDA margin; Ginger reached 100 operational hotels and targets 150 by March 31, 2027. Qmin has over 130 outlets, Ama over 400 villas and bungalows, Tree of Life over 50 resorts.

segments.name: TajSATS (air catering)
segments.commentary: EBITDA declined sequentially in Q2 due to airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure; non-aviation institutional catering partly offset the decline. Management expects improvement in H2.

segments.name: International subsidiaries
segments.commentary: St. James' Court margins fell 360 bps YoY in H1 FY27 due to delayed renovation works and cost pressure; management expects London recovery with double-digit growth in October. Pierre (New York) is EBITDA-positive but not at target margins.

Implied H2 growth is well above the 14% midpoint arithmetic, per CFO, as TajSATS is a drag and H2 is seasonally strong; the guidance excludes OHL.
Plan to open 50 hotels in FY27; 30 expected in H2 (possibly 32-34). Standalone hotel count was 392 operational as of Oct 27, 2026, with 4 more openings in October.

OHL merger: 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares; appointed date April 1, 2027; expected to add 6%-7% to standalone operating revenue in FY28, not in FY27 guidance.
Management expects more than INR1,000 crores of management fee income in roughly two years and about 5,000 keys opened per year.
capex_capacity: Portfolio at 670 hotels with over 69,000 keys (operational or under development) at end-H1 FY27; 47 hotels signed and 20 opened in H1 FY27.
Pipeline of over 34,800 keys, 94% capital-light (81% management contracts, 13% leases).
H1 FY27 capex is 20%-30% above the annual average of the preceding 7-8 years, per management.

Asset upgrades at Taj Palace New Delhi, President Mumbai, Taj West End Bengaluru, Taj Fort Aguada and Taj Lake Palace; Taj Palace New Delhi room revenue up 132% YoY and crossed INR100 crores monthly revenue in September.
Expected upcoming Frankfurt ramp-up after start-up challenges; London and San Francisco expected to improve in Q3.
demand_pricing: Occupancy rose to 82% from 75% in Q2 last year; standalone and domestic consolidated occupancy each up roughly 6%-7%, so growth was balanced between occupancy and ARR.
Demand supported by MICE events (BRICS Summit, Bloomberg event, fintech event); management said Q2 ex-BRICS would still have been a comfortable double-digit RevPAR number.
Wedding nights next year are expected at about 95 versus 60-65 normally, a tailwind for social MICE.
Domestic demand is the main pillar; foreign tourist arrivals have a 3.9% 10-year CAGR, and management sees upside if this reaches 5%-6%. Room nights were flat YoY in Q2 per management.

Tier 2/3 supply: management says demand growth of 15%-20% in these markets is largely met by unorganised players, and that the 12% capacity CAGR headline should be viewed with caution given project delays.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 guidance implied by the revised numbers, and is occupancy at 82% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be mostly rate-led plus new hotels and international recovery (London, Pierre, San Francisco, Frankfurt), with occupancy gains also in the mix; H2 guidance is conservative given the 30-34 hotel openings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TajSATS EBITDA fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Airline schedule curtailments after West Asia fuel-price pressure, mainly from June; Q2 had the full impact. Non-flight catering grew, but at lower margin. FY27 is a consolidation year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14% implied H2 growth conservative and what are the uplift drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said H2 growth would have to be higher than the 14% arithmetic to hit guidance, given TajSATS drag, a high Q4 base and seasonally strong MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 25% growth in Q2 driven by renovation base effects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said renovations are routine for iconic assets; H1 capex is 20%-30% above normal and the growth reflects structural demand shifts, not only a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep international assets, given lower margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strategic value of the global Taj brand; international consolidated margin of about 35% is stated as industry-leading, with London profitable and Pierre EBITDA-positive but not at 20%-25% margins.

qa_highlights.question: What can standalone RevPAR be without BRICS, and how sustainable is the 400 bps margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs in Q2; margin gain from operating leverage, MICE, and management fee mix (booked standalone). Management did not give specific margin guidance but expects a positive margin trend despite new payroll and regulatory costs.

Chennai and Kolkata lag other metros on FTA-dependent demand; management expects recovery in next one or two quarters.

500870|2026-03.headline: Castrol India Q1 FY26 revenue rose 9% to INR1,545 crore and EBITDA 7% to INR329 crore, with management flagging raw-material cost pressure from Q2.
500870|2026-03.overview: Castrol India reported Q1 FY26 revenue of INR1,545 crore (up 9%), EBITDA of INR329 crore (up 7%) and PAT of INR242 crore (up 4%), with volume growth of 7-8% YoY. Management said the Middle East conflict and weaker rupee (about 6.5-7% down YoY) began to hit costs late in the quarter, but minimal raw-material inflation reached Q1 COGS because of inventory cycles. One round of price increases was taken at end-March, and the bulk of raw-material cost increases is expected in Q2. Operating expenses rose sharply QoQ, which management attributed partly to one-time employee costs expected to fall in coming quarters.

financial_highlights.change: about +10% YoY and about +23% QoQ (analyst figure, not disputed)

segments.name: Rural
segments.commentary: Volume growing at double-digit rate for several years; distribution expanded to about 40,000 outlets, 700 Rural Service Express bike units added, and direct reach into villages below 20,000 population. About two-thirds of rural product sales are motorcycle products.

segments.name: Urban premium (cars and bikes)
segments.commentary: Premium brands delivered double-digit volume and value growth in the quarter; cars are an emerging segment, estimated at 15-20% of revenue.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Management says CV has been strong and the Tata Motors partnership grew in double digits, but the wider CV and specialty range (truck engine oil, transmission fluids, greases) grew only high single-digit. Automotive two-wheeler plus CV together is about 60% of sales.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at double-digit for multiple consecutive quarters; weighted-average margin is lower than automotive, though some niche applications are high margin.

segments.name: Service network
segments.commentary: 800 Castrol Auto Services at end-March; 34,000 independent bike workshops and 13,000 multi-brand car workshops reached.

guidance_outlook: Structural EBITDA margin band of 21-24% retained as the target; management said Q1 is seasonally the softest quarter and Q1 margin dilution was not large.
Raw-material cost increases (crude, packaging, fuel, additives) expected to flow into COGS from Q2 FY26; one round of pricing taken end-March, with further price-plus-cost-cut actions possible.
One-time employee costs in Q1 opex are expected to decline, so future quarterly opex should be lower than Q1 levels.
Parent-level deal remains subject to global regulatory approvals; management says there is no change to Castrol India's structure, strategy or operating model.
No guidance given on data-centre cooling opportunity.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or utilisation figures were discussed on the call.
Base oil sourced from Indian refiners, Singapore and South Korea; imports driven by specification needs, and the company is open to other sources.
Term base-oil contracts are index-linked (Argus and ICIS); no scarcity premium reported as of call date.
MoU signed with Hindustan Petroleum Corporation to explore a re-refined base oil ecosystem in India.
Data-centre cooling (immersion and direct-to-chip) is at trial stage in India; no timeline or market size given.
demand_pricing: Hedging: 60-day policy linked to inventory cycle; about half of COGS is locally sourced (not hedged) and half imported (USD exposure hedged).
Pricing: no blanket increase; price changes set product by product to recover cost increases, with intent to hold margins.
Rural margins described as accretive, with premium bike oils (Activ) carrying high gross margins; car margins highest, then bikes, then CVs.
Competition in EV space: partnerships with Ather Energy (2W) and Tata Mobility (EV transmission fluids), with products for hybrid, E20 and gas engines already in market.
Middle East sourcing pressure: higher cost and less predictable lead times for feedstocks; no material supply disruption yet.

qa_highlights.question: Has the crude price spike in March flowed into Q1 raw-material costs, and how fast can price increases pass through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said minimal raw-material impact hit Q1 COGS due to inventory cycles, with the main impact being FX; most cost increases are expected in Q2. One round of pricing was taken at end-March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating expenses rise about 23% QoQ and 10% YoY, and what is the run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said total expenses grew 9%, in line with revenue, and COGS grew slower than volume. Some one-time employee costs sit in the quarter and should fall, so future quarters should be lower than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7-8% volume growth YoY or QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is Q1 FY26 versus Q1 FY25, YoY.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin should be expected for the year, given the drop to about 21%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the 21-24% operating EBITDA band. Q1 is seasonally soft and not heavily diluted, but short-term volatility could come as raw-material costs rise.

qa_highlights.question: Are base-oil prices showing a premium or scarcity pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Contracts are index-linked to Argus and ICIS, which have moved up. No separate scarcity premium is applied to term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data-centre opportunity, its timeline and its market size?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the work is beyond pilot, with trials under way in India, but gave no timeline, guidance or market size because technology choices are not yet firm.

qa_highlights.question: Which segment is pulling down overall volume growth despite double-digit growth in rural and premium urban?
qa_highlights.answer: Large commercial vehicle business, including truck engine oil, plus specialty products such as transmission fluids and greases, grew high single-digit, which pulls the blended rate to 7-8%.

risks_watch: Raw-material and feedstock cost inflation (crude, packaging, additives) and FX pressure from Q2 FY26, with only one price increase taken so far.
Margin band: whether EBITDA stays within 21-24% as the pricing and cost-cut response plays out.
Sustainability of opex: confirm that one-time employee costs decline in Q2 and beyond.
Middle East sourcing: lead-time unpredictability and possible supply gaps despite diversified sourcing.
Parent-level transaction: regulatory approvals pending; management says no operating change at Castrol India.
500870|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on Q1 execution and earnings quality, but noticeably cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly flagged near-term volatility and cost pressure from Q2. Answers on pricing quantum, the one-time cost amount and data-centre timelines were evasive or non-quantified.
key_quotes: We have delivered our 12th consecutive quarter of stable revenue and volume growth.
Given the inventory cycle, we saw minimal impact of these raw material increases into the COGS that we reported in quarter 1.
Structurally, we will recover the structural margin for the company, we will want to go back into that same range of 21%, 24%.
So, we don't see rural as a gross margin dilutor for us at all.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects raw-material cost increases (crude, packaging, additives, FX down about 6.5-7% YoY) to hit COGS from Q2, with only one price round taken at end-March; the 21-24% EBITDA band is held but short-term volatility is flagged, and Q1 EBITDA margin was about 21% (INR329 crore on INR1,545 crore revenue).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY26 volume grew 7-8% YoY with rural and premium urban growing double digit, though the CV and specialty range grew only high single digit; no volume guidance was given, so the call rests on the recent run-rate.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance raise was signalled; management reiterated the 21-24% band and flagged cost pressure from Q2 that is expected to weigh on margins.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material cost increases are expected to flow into COGS from Q2 with only one price round (end-March) taken so far, and pricing quantum and the one-time employee cost amount were not quantified, so the margin band could come under pressure.

rows.label: Further price-plus-cost-cut actions in response to raw-material inflation
rows.why: Management said further price-plus-cost-cut actions are possible after the one round taken end-March, with raw-material costs (crude, packaging, additives) flowing into COGS from Q2 FY26; quantum was not disclosed.

rows.label: Decline in one-time employee costs in opex
rows.why: Opex rose about 23% QoQ to about INR338 crore partly on one-time employee costs that management expects to fall in coming quarters, though the amount was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q1 execution (revenue +9%, volume +7-8%) but cautious on Q2 raw-material cost pressure and the margin outlook; pricing quantum, the one-time cost amount and data-centre timelines were not quantified.

500870|2026-06.headline: Castrol India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR1,871 crore and EBITDA 41% YoY to INR494 crore, helped by inventory benefits and pricing.
500870|2026-06.overview: Castrol India reported strong Q2 (April–June 2026) with revenue from operations of INR1,871 crore (+25% YoY, +21% QoQ), EBITDA of INR494 crore (+41% YoY and QoQ) and PAT of INR348 crore (+43% YoY). Growth was described as broad-based across consumer, industrial and institutional businesses, with two price increases in January–June 2026 and some benefit from older, lower-cost inventory. Management said cost inflation from supply disruptions and commodity volatility began to hit late in the quarter and will be more visible in Q3. The company declared an interim dividend of INR6.25 per share.

segments.name: Consumer (B2C, retail/auto care)
segments.commentary: Broad-based volume growth driven by rural operations and urban premiumisation; POWER1 (premium motorcycle) grew ahead of rest of business. Rural business growing at double digits; rural outlets ~45,000.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at high double digits over last couple of years; about 15% of overall business per CFO. Growth from advanced solutions and expanded customer base.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B (OEMs)
segments.commentary: Works with OEMs such as Tata Motors and Maruti; growth tied to OEM volumes. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin management framework remains 21%–24%; pricing actions are set to keep margins within this band.
Commodity and feedstock inflation expected to become more visible in Q3 FY27, with some raw material increases expected to spill over into Q3.
Management says price actions taken so far are sufficient to offset raw material increases from Q2, but will take further pricing if base oil or FX move adversely.
Lubricant industry expected to grow 3%–4%; company aims to grow at about 2x market.
Capex of about INR100 crore per year, roughly half in manufacturing and half in market (dealer/workshop visibility).
Sourcing guidance of ~55% domestic / ~45% imported broadly unchanged, with quarterly tactical variation.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, split roughly equally between manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and in-market investments.
Silvassa plant was shut for a few days in July 2026 due to heavy rain; fully back up with operating levels at Q2 peak per management.
Paharpur and Silvassa plants completed 9 years and 3 years respectively without significant recordable incident.

National footprint of ~160,000 outlets; auto care range in 40,000 outlets; 34,000 independent motorcycle workshops and 16,000 car workshops; 850 Castrol Auto Service (CAS) outlets; 950 rural service express units.
Building capabilities for specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids; data-centre business not yet material.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken in January–June 2026 (late Q1 and Q2), in the low double-digit percentage range; pricing aimed at offsetting supply chain volatility and inflation.
Volume growth described as broad-based across consumer and industrial; company declined to disclose absolute volume (million litres) for the quarter, departing from past practice of sharing it.
Competitor reportedly took around 4 price increases between March and July 2026; management said it will not follow competitor pricing blindly and is guided by RM outlook and margin band.
Group III base oil prices elevated, impacted by Middle East crisis.
Inventory: about half of raw materials bought locally and half from international suppliers; company says it runs lean inventory and that Q2 benefited from older, cheaper inventory being consumed.
E20 fuel: most passenger car brands already compliant; impact on lubricants seen as limited to engine-level fuel-choice issues.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the open offer linked to the BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is progressing but is large and multi-country; open offer timing depends on deal closure, after which SEBI and shareholder notifications and prescribed timelines apply. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs pricing split and Silvassa flood impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is broad-based but no specific figures given; price increases were in low double digits. Silvassa plant was halted briefly in July for safety and is now at peak operating levels, with no impact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said older inventory bought at softer prices was consumed in the quarter, benefiting margins; it declined to quantify and said profitability grew healthily even excluding this.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed payout percentage; dividend yield usually around 5% including interim and final; special dividends given occasionally. Interim window was advanced this year. Past three years' payout has been in the 80%–90% range per the questioner, which management did not confirm as policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are price hikes not enough to offset Q3 raw material cost, given diesel prices fell after June?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was modelled on inventory and FX scenarios for Q2 and H2; current pricing is seen as broadly reflecting Q3 costs, but the environment is volatile and further price action is possible. Structural cost reductions are also underway.

qa_highlights.question: OCI loss of ~INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fair-value revaluation of the Ki Mobility investment made about 4 years ago, using listed comparable companies, reviewed every six months; expected to move up and down with peers.

risks_watch: Commodity and base oil (Group III) cost inflation expected to hit Q3 margins more visibly; margin band 21%–24%.
Foreign exchange movements affecting input costs.
Possible volume trade-off or downtrading from the price increases, especially with competitor pricing reportedly higher.
Dependence on Silvassa plant and monsoon/weather disruptions.
Pending BP/Stonepeak divestment of Castrol global, with open offer timing uncertain.
Lack of volume disclosure reduces visibility into volume vs price split.
500870|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the broad-based growth story, but cautious on the outlook, citing inflation, volatility and monsoon conditions. Management was evasive on volume figures, inventory gain quantification, the open offer timeline and data-centre revenue.
key_quotes: And this is in context of a very volatile operating environment marked by supply disruptions and commodity cost inflation.
We, therefore, expect the impact of commodity and feedstock inflation to become more visible in the third quarter.
I think we pride ourselves on a very lean inventory profile.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was ~26% in Q2 but management holds a 21%-24% band, cost inflation from base oil and FX to be more visible in Q3, and Q2 was helped by older cheaper inventory that will not repeat.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity addition was announced; Silvassa was only down for a few days in July and is back at peak, and capex is held at about INR100 crore per year split evenly between manufacturing and in-market.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets about 2x the lubricant industry's 3%-4% growth, roughly 6%-8%, backed by two low-double-digit price rises, though absolute volume was not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is held at about INR100 crore per year with no new plant or board-approved expansion, and the call gave no utilisation figure to suggest a step-up is needed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin band and volume aim were both held rather than raised, and management said Q3 cost inflation will be more visible.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Base oil and FX inflation is expected to spill into Q3, and the 21%-24% margin band could be tested after Q2 EBITDA margin of ~26% helped by inventory benefit.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Company is building capabilities in specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids, but data-centre business is not yet material and no launch date was given.

rows.label: Further price action if base oil or FX moves adversely
rows.why: Two price rises in low double digits were taken in Jan-Jun 2026, and management will take further pricing if Group III base oil or FX move adversely, while competitors took about 4 increases between March and July 2026.

rows.label: Open offer tied to BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment
rows.why: The deal is multi-country and large, and open offer timing depends on deal closure with no timeline given.

rows.label: Interim dividend INR6.25 per share
rows.why: Interim dividend of INR6.25 per share declared, with H1 PAT of INR590 crore; past payout reportedly 80%-90%, though management did not confirm it as policy.

tone.note: Management was confident on the broad-based growth and the Q2 result, but cautious on Q3 cost inflation from base oil and FX; analysts pressed on volume split, inventory gain, the open offer timeline and whether pricing covers Q3 costs.

500870|2026-09.headline: Castrol India Q3 CY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR 1,735 crore, but EBITDA fell 19% to INR 262 crore (~15% margin) on raw material inflation.
500870|2026-09.overview: Q3 revenue from operations was INR 1,735 crore, up 27% YoY but down 7% QoQ, while EBITDA fell 19% YoY to INR 262 crore and PAT fell 23% YoY to INR 176 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to a sharp rise in commodity and raw material costs (cited as a 60-plus percent increase in the raw material bill) and adverse currency moves, partly offset by early-year pricing actions. Over nine months, revenue grew 20% to INR 5,151 crore, EBITDA rose 11% to INR 1,086 crore and PAT rose 9% to INR 766 crore. Management declined to give forward quarterly guidance and said margins will sit outside the 21-24% EBITDA band in the short to medium term.

segments.name: Industrial lubricants
segments.commentary: Delivered another quarter of double-digit volume growth in the September quarter; added close to 400 customers net over the full year and 9 months, with growth in steel and cement and new metalworking fluid launches (Hysol 35 XBB, Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free). Management said industrial margin is healthy and above last year's level.

segments.name: Automotive / consumer and commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: No separate volume figures given. Management said Q2 and Q3 were managed together and volume growth looked healthy; company claims market share held across categories. Institutional customers include Tata, Maruti and JCB.

segments.name: Thermal management / data-centre cooling
segments.commentary: Early-stage. Two latest products certified by NVIDIA about 1.5 months before the call for direct-to-chip cooling; business is in ongoing pilots and not a substantial part of revenue or profit today.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly guidance given; management cited unprecedented raw material volatility.
Medium-term EBITDA margin expected to fall outside the 21-24% band in the short to medium term; the 21-24% band remains the target over time.
Management said it will operate within a 21-24% EBITDA frame over the medium term while growing volume at least 1.5x to 2x the market growth rate.
Plant utilisation expected to stay in the 70-80% range through the year.
Market growth in India estimated at 3-4% in a normal year; this year may see headwinds, with Castrol tracking ahead.
Capex historically INR 100-150 crore per year, focused on plant innovation, capacity and consumer/trade visibility.

Stonepeak acquisition of Castrol from BP: completion targeted by end CY26 per the deal; management said licence work across 50+ countries is progressing well, with SEBI disclosure to follow on completion.
capex_capacity: Plants run at around 70-80% utilisation; expected to remain in the same range through the year, with seasonal flex.
Historical capex of INR 100-150 crore per year; no specific CY27 capex figure given.
Localisation of inputs and reformulation are being used to reduce bill of materials and cash cost.
Supply-chain efficiency work under way for 6-7 months to partly offset raw material inflation.
demand_pricing: Raw material bill up 60-plus percent in Q3; COGS as a percentage of sales up 61% YoY.
Pricing actions taken early in the year; further pricing to be taken as and when required, calibrated by sector, with no forward guidance.
About 40% of business is B2B; some B2B contracts have price-flex clauses for input-cost pass-through, while B2C pricing varies by channel.
Base oil prices: Base Oil 2 down about 5% and Base Oil 3 down about 7% in Q3 per an analyst; management said the cost environment remains substantially challenged versus last year.
Crude oil went from about $120 in Q2 to about $80, and is now back at $114-115 per management.

Network of about 167,000 outlets, including 46,000 in rural small-town India; Auto Care in 50,000 stores; about 870 Castrol Auto Service centres, 37,000 independent bike workshops and 16,000 multi-brand workshops; Rural Service Express at over 1,000 locations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume guidance and how is pricing balanced against market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance for the next few months given the unprecedented raw material moves; it reiterated the aim to gain volume and share, with pricing balanced to let consumers move to new price points.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex and margin guidance for CY27, and hedging plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex historically INR 100-150 crore; investments prioritise growth drivers. Margin protection is to come from a mix of pricing and cost prudence; no hedging detail was given.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Stonepeak acquisition and the DPS filing in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Licence work across more than 50 countries is progressing well; SEBI will be informed on completion, with no timeline beyond that.

qa_highlights.question: Is Castrol refocusing on the OEM business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not call out OEM as a separate focus; it said it works with OEMs such as Tata, Maruti and JCB on new engine platform technology.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise sales and Q3 volume trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth ahead of market over nine months; industrial grew double digits in Q3; automotive volumes were described as healthy across Q2 and Q3 combined, with no specific figures.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reference margin per litre, and does lower absolute EBITDA imply lower volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said per-litre EBITDA is an internal frame, and the external measure is percentage margin: 26% in Q2, 15% in Q3, 21% over six and nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Are plants and margins expected to recover, and what levers are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 21-24% band will be reached only once volatility subsides, with levers in supplier diversification, localisation, reformulation and supply-chain efficiency.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre cooling: size of opportunity and how sales are routed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said products are globally approved and sold through Castrol India, with NVIDIA certification as a base requirement; it declined to size the opportunity, saying it is not yet material.

risks_watch: Raw material and crude/FX volatility: margin per litre is the stated measure, but guidance has been withdrawn.
Q4 CY26 margin and volume recovery; watch pricing action and base oil rebates in Oct-Dec.
Volume softness in the short to medium term given market headwinds.
Stonepeak-BP transaction: completion by end CY26 and any change to the timeline.
Limited disclosure: analysts pressed for segment and volume detail, and an analyst asked for more specific guidance.
500870|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and the industrial and rural growth engines, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and guidance, citing raw material and currency volatility. Management was evasive on volume split, data-centre sizing and the timeline for the Stonepeak deal.
key_quotes: We are not giving a guidance for the next few months because it's unprecedented in terms of the raw material price movement, right?
For us, margin per liter is a true measure. And on that basis, we have fully absorbed cost inflation.
We will hold ourselves to the frame of operating the business at 21% to 24% EBITDA.

rows.why: Q3 EBITDA margin fell to ~15% from ~26% in Q2 as raw material bill rose 60-plus% (COGS/sales up 61% YoY), and management expects margins outside the 21-24% band in the short to medium term, recovering only once volatility subsides.

rows.why: Utilisation is only 70-80%, with no new capacity planned; capex is historically INR 100-150 crore a year and no CY27 figure was given.

rows.why: New metalworking fluids (Hysol 35 XBB, Hysol 61 XBB, boron-free) were launched recently, and two data-centre cooling products got NVIDIA certification about 1.5 months before the call, but the cooling business is still in pilots and not material.

rows.why: Management will take further pricing as required, calibrated by sector, and some B2B contracts have input-cost pass-through clauses covering about 40% of the business; Base Oil 2 is down ~5% and Base Oil 3 ~7% in Q3, but crude is back at $114-115.

rows.label: Stonepeak acquisition of Castrol from BP completion
rows.why: Completion is targeted by end CY26 per the deal, with licence work across 50+ countries progressing well and SEBI disclosure to follow on completion.

500877|2026-03.headline: Apollo Tyres Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 14% to INR 73.4 bn with 14.6% EBITDA margin, while India and Europe face a steep raw-material cost push.
500877|2026-03.overview: Consolidated revenue grew about 14% YoY to INR 73.4 bn and EBITDA margin was 14.6% versus 13% a year ago, despite roughly INR 100 crore of extra cricket-jersey sponsorship and activation spend. India revenue rose 14.3% to INR 52.4 bn on high-teens volume growth in both replacement and OE, with a 14.6% margin. Europe revenue fell 1% to EUR 170 mn, with EBITDA of EUR 25 mn (14.6% margin), and the Enschede plant closure carried a EUR 43 mn non-cash write-off. Management guided to a sharp raw-material cost increase (mid to high teens QoQ in Q1) and is taking two rounds of price hikes totalling 6-8%, with more needed.

financial_highlights.change: +14% YoY, c.+2% QoQ implied by India commentary
-1% YoY (c.-3% incl. other operating income drop)
from 0.7x at March 2025 and about 3x in March 2020 per management

financial_highlights.metric: Deferred tax benefit from concessional regime
financial_highlights.value: c.INR 570 crore+ positive net impact in P&L
financial_highlights.change: tax rate India cut from 34% to 25% from FY27

segments.name: India Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 52.4 bn (+14.3% YoY), EBITDA INR 7.6 bn at 14.6% margin; high-teens volume growth in OE and replacement, TBR replacement up 20%+ and PCR replacement single-digit OE/high-single to 20%+ per management split. Capacity utilisation about 90%.

segments.name: Europe Operations
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR 170 mn (-1% YoY) on muted market; passenger car outperformed market while truck supply was hit by India supply issues. EBITDA EUR 25 mn at 14.6% margin vs 14.3%.

guidance_outlook: Raw material costs expected to rise mid to high teens sequentially in Q1 FY27; Q2 could be marginally higher than Q1 if current levels persist.
Price hikes of 6-8% announced for Q1 FY27 in India (3-5% implemented, rest in May); at least two more rounds needed beyond this to offset cost push.
India margins to remain under pressure in near term; management expects margin normalisation with pricing catch-up over time.
A&P spend to normalise at around 2.5% plus of sales from 4% in Q4 FY26 (typical 2%).
Enschede plant last production day June 30, 2026; positive European margin impact expected from H2 FY27.
FY27 consolidated capex of INR 35 bn, about 80% growth/capacity; roughly INR 3,000 crore India, balance Europe (mainly Hungary passenger car expansion).
Europe cash outflow of about EUR 50 mn in FY27 for social plan; total cash provision of EUR 55 mn-plus already taken.
Europe blended tax rate about 20%; India 25% from FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex outlined at INR 35 bn, with nearly 80% towards growth and capacity expansion.
India capex close to INR 3,000 crore of the INR 3,500 crore (per transcript figures) covering truck and car tyre capacity expansion.
Hungary plant: passenger car tyre expansion already well underway; no truck expansion there.
Capacity utilisation at about 90% across India and Europe; management expects full utilisation and continues planned expansion.
Management said FY27 is largely committed for the previously announced large capex plan; some flexibility exists for FY28 if demand slows.
Export volumes to be deprioritised in favour of home markets India and Europe given tight capacity, especially in truck tyres.
demand_pricing: India volume growth high teens YoY in both OE and replacement in Q4; sequential volume growth about 2% QoQ, which accounted for all of the 2% QoQ revenue growth.
Standalone exports up mid-single digits in Q4; US market weak, though price increases of mid to high single digits announced there.
Market share: management believes it gained share in TBR replacement for FY26 and in PCR replacement, but not in PCR OE; based on internal estimates.

FY26 capacity utilisation was about 67% (71% in FY25), per CFO.
Management says capacity is not a constraint; growth will be supported by replacing lines with higher-capacity extruders.
Annual capex around INR100 crore for maintenance plus debottlenecking; no new greenfield or multi-location plant announced.

VCM supply: Middle East was a major VCM source; the company is shifting sourcing to Far East and Northeast Asia, and the monsoon shutdown of the VCM line for 4-5 months means no VCM run-rate impact in that period.
demand_pricing: April 2026 demand was subdued after prices peaked in March and then fell; May was somewhat better, and agri demand returned ahead of the monsoon.
Current agri demand is about 25-27% below the March price peak, per management.
Q4 PVC/EDC spread averaged $521/t versus about $793 average international PVC; current PVC/EDC spread is about $543 with international PVC near $900+.
PVC/VCM spread is currently about $108 versus about $179-180 average in Q4, a sharp fall that management acknowledged will weigh on the quarter.
Government imposed a 90-day import duty on PVC resin from April to 30 June 2026; management said ADD is not viable now, while MIP is a possible short-term option being pursued by CPMA.
Monsoon is delayed in Kerala by about 7-10 days and a lower-than-normal monsoon is forecast; management says agri losses will be partly offset by non-agri growth.

qa_highlights.question: What was the inventory gain in Q4, and is the margin sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about INR35-40 crore from March-April price rises; management said margin is at the higher side and will moderate, with FY27 EBITDA margin guided to sub-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume flat in Q4 when peers reported restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri volume fell because farmers expected prices to soften after the spike; non-agri volume rose, and total volume stayed flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall and finance cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Other income fell to about INR36 crore from about INR52-58 crore on lower mark-to-market gains on investments; finance cost rose to about INR7.8 crore from INR3 crore as the company built inventory and borrowed against it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company return surplus cash to shareholders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Board has not yet decided on the use of accumulated cash; the FY26 dividend came from current accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Does the VCM supply from the Middle East threaten PVC resin output in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the monsoon shutdown of the VCM line covers 4-5 months anyway, and that the company is switching to Far East and Northeast Asia sources, so no availability impact is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide sub-15% margin when the 10-year average is about 17.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the guidance is conservative because of geopolitical uncertainty and that the company expects to deliver higher margin toward year-end.

risks_watch: Monsoon timing and strength, which drives agri demand (about 63% of FY26 mix); a lower monsoon is already forecast.
PVC/VCM spread compression (from about $179 to $108) could weigh on Q1 FY27 margins, and inventory gains may reverse.
Middle East supply disruption for VCM and polymer price volatility.
Import duty on PVC resin expires 30 June 2026; any MIP or ADD decision is pending.
Volume growth lagging peers; FY26 volume fell about 4.4%.
Finance cost rising due to inventory-linked borrowing; other income falling as mark-to-market gains decline.
Capital allocation of about INR2,500+ crore of net cash remains undecided.

It was evasive on the cash return timeline, on the agri-versus-non-agri margin gap, and on capacity expansion plans, saying the Board has not decided.

Overall, the kind of margin that we have -- you have seen during the current quarter is obviously certain at the higher side, but going to be -- going forward, it is going to moderate to some extent.

500940|2026-06.headline: Finolex Q1 FY27: volume fell 27% YoY to ~68,000 MT, while EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin widened to 12%.
500940|2026-06.overview: Volumes fell 27% YoY to about 68,000 MT as PVC price volatility triggered channel destocking, with April the weakest month and May and June growing per management. Revenue fell 27% to INR884 crore from INR1,043 crore, but EBITDA rose 14% to INR107 crore and margin improved from 9% to 12%, which management attributed mainly to top-line realization rather than cost. PAT was about INR107 crore and cash stood at INR2,636 crore. Management said July was the best month of the four, with a minimum price floor from the MIP and customs duty withdrawal, but declined to give full-year volume or margin guidance beyond reiterating the sub-15% margin view.

segments.name: Agri pipes
segments.commentary: Agri was 69% of volume; agri volume fell 27% YoY. Fittings were 5% of agri and 11% of total volume.

segments.name: Non-agri / plumbing
segments.commentary: Non-agri was about 25% of volume (fittings 25% within non-agri per management); volume fell ~24% YoY, versus ~18-20% industry peers per management.

segments.name: CPVC
segments.commentary: CPVC was about 7% of volume in Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: No full-year FY27 volume guidance; management said it is too early and will revisit after Q2 trends.
Margin: reiterated the Q4 FY26 view of sub-15% EBITDA margin, with no revision.
Management expects a somewhat better Q2 on realizations after the MIP-driven price floor; said it was hopeful H1 volume could be flattish YoY, with a plus possible if July's pace holds.

Capex: capital outlay of INR125-200 crore per year for expansion and debottlenecking, unchanged. Installed capacity 520 (unit as stated), FY26 volume 333, headroom for 10-12% growth over roughly the next 1-1.5 years.
Other income of ~INR75 crore in the quarter is mark-to-market and driven by bond yields, so it is not guaranteed to recur at that level.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity stated as 520 (units not specified); FY26 volume 333. Management says there is headroom to grow 10-12% over the next 1-1.5 years.
Growth is coming through debottlenecking, replacing lower-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones, rather than large greenfield or brownfield projects.
Capex outlay remains INR125-200 crore, unchanged.

Ratnagiri PVC: EDC-based line running without interruption. VCM-based line does not run during the June-September monsoon months because the Ratnagiri jetty is fair-weather only. VCM availability is constrained by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints.
CPVC extrusion capacity is considered sufficient for near-term CPVC growth, according to management.
demand_pricing: Average PVC price in Q1 was about USD875/MT versus USD707/MT a year earlier (ICIS), carried over from elevated Q4 FY26 levels. A sharp intra-quarter correction in April triggered channel destocking.
Management cited INR96 to INR92 to INR82/kg as the PVC price path through April. Analyst cited a INR12-13/kg hike in the last 15-20 days after the MIP and duty changes.
Customs duty exemption on PVC resin was withdrawn in mid-July, and a minimum import price (MIP) was imposed. Management said these should support price stability and channel inventory.
Pass-through: management said almost all of the recent price increase (barring INR1-2) has been passed to customers.
Demand: July was the best month of the four, with a strong pickup; August to date was described as moving in the right direction.
Channel inventory is near normal, with some room left. A lot of stocking occurred in July in anticipation of price increases. Quantification in days was not given.
PVC-EDC spread was ~USD501/MT in Q1 FY27 versus ~USD522 a year earlier, and ~USD490 currently. PVC-VCM spread was INR122/kg in Q1 FY27 versus INR163 a year earlier.
Pricing: management said Finolex prices ~10-12% above Supreme-type peers in the market (ballpark only).
Market share: management said FY26 share of the top 5-6 reporting companies was about 22%, and it sees no change in Q1. An analyst cited FY23 share of about 27%.
JJM 2.0: management said the outlay is about INR67,000 crore, not higher than JJM 1.0. All sales go through channel partners, so there is no direct correlation to volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did realization not rise QoQ when peers reported 7-9% jumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said realization per kg was up ~15% vs the same quarter last year and was in line with peers. It said Q4 FY26 was an aberration with a sharp price rise, and that falling PVC prices in April drove the QoQ result. Discounts and incentives also affect net realization.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the volume decline was agri vs non-agri, and what were the monthly trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri fell 27% and non-agri fell ~24% YoY. April was the weakest month, May grew and June was normal. Management did not give monthly figures and said it would reach out separately.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion despite falling volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin was largely top-line driven, with costs range-bound. It cited backward integration and the timing of raw material procurement as a cushion. It did not quantify inventory gains or losses.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year volume decline? Can H1 be flat YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide full-year volume. It said July was a good month and that flattish H1 YoY is possible, with a plus if July's pace holds, while August and September are still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy the INR2,636 crore cash into CPVC capacity and shareholder returns?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CPVC extrusion capacity is sufficient and CPVC is about 7-8% of the PVC pipe market, which Finolex matches. It said the Board decides on cash deployment or returns and will announce when a decision is made.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin guidance sub-15% when Q1 delivered 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is holding the sub-15% guidance from Q4 because of volatility in Q1 and wants another quarter of data before revising it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VCM supply situation and the PVC plant utilization outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: VCM availability is limited by Middle East force majeure and Northeast Asia feedstock constraints. The VCM line does not run during monsoon months (about June to September) because of the fair-weather jetty. Management said efforts to secure supply are ongoing and H2 is uncertain.

We will continue with our same last quarter's margin, the anticipation that we have given.
And as soon as there is some decision, I think we would be happy to announce.

500940|2026-09.headline: Finolex Industries Q2 FY27 volume rose 28% YoY to 83,407 MT, but PBT was flat at INR153 crore as raw material cost lag squeezed margins.
500940|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 sales volume grew 28% YoY to 83,407 MT as channel restocking followed Q1 price-led destocking, and revenue rose 27% to INR1,094 crore. PBT was roughly flat at INR153 crore versus INR158 crore a year earlier, as higher-cost inventory consumed in Q2 lagged the rise in PVC prices. H1 volume fell 4% YoY to 151,106 MT and H1 revenue rose 4% to INR1,978 crore. Management guided full-year EBITDA of about INR15/kg (roughly 14-15%) and said October was a good month.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR158 crore in Q2 FY26 (flat to down)
vs 157,465 MT in H1 FY26 (-4% YoY)
Management said H1 EBITDA margin in line with last year

financial_highlights.value: About INR2,584 crore as of 30 Sep 2026

segments.commentary: Overall utilisation about 68% in Q2; agri to non-agri mix about 60:40 in Q2 versus 56:44 in Q2 FY26. Fittings were about 12% of Q2 local volume and CPVC about 8%.

segments.name: Resin (EDC/VCM)
segments.commentary: EDC line runs at full utilisation; VCM line is structurally idle during monsoon due to raw material unavailability. Q2 PVC-EDC spread was USD455/t and PVC-VCM spread USD171/t (ICIS SE Asia).

No large PVC price erosion expected in Q3 as the minimum import price remains until mid to third week of January and domestic supply-demand is slightly constrained.

Raw materials covered for Q3; management said procurement cost is in line with existing inventory cost, not below spot.

Debottlenecking replaces low-capacity extruders with higher-capacity ones; incremental capacity expected towards end of FY28.
Monetisation of idle plant was completed about two years ago; no current plan to monetise further land at Ratnagiri, Masar or Urse.
demand_pricing: Q2 volume recovery was driven by channel restocking after Q1 price-led destocking; PVC prices stabilised in Q2 with lower volatility.
Agri demand is at risk from El Nino and water scarcity, but management cited tractor bookings up 14-15% and rural 2-wheeler bookings above prior years.
Management said scheme and discount spend offset PVC price increases, flattening realisations despite higher PVC prices.
Q2 margin pressure attributed to a lag in raw material cost: inventory bought at lower prices in Q1 was consumed in Q2 while selling prices reset immediately.

Spot prices: EDC USD450-500/t, VCM USD900-950/t, ethylene USD1,150-1,200/t. The MIP on suspension-grade PVC resin is USD767/t CIF; DGTR has recommended CVD on PVC from China, with the Ministry of Finance yet to decide and the CVD likely to replace the MIP if adopted.

qa_highlights.question: Why are margins under pressure despite higher raw material prices and possible inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1-bought low-cost inventory was consumed in Q2 while realisations fall immediately, so the raw-material lag squeezed margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is full-year volume and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year EBITDA about INR15/kg, roughly 14-15%; October was a relatively good month and volume was slightly positive YoY to date, but management avoided firm guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growth equal to volume growth despite higher PVC prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix (agri growing faster than non-agri, 60:40 vs 56:44) and higher channel schemes and discounts.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and capital allocation of the large cash pile?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR150 crore planned for FY27; Board has made no decision on use or reward for cash, which stays invested at about 7.5-8% yield, with no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for agri demand given El Nino?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said El Nino impact expected from November; water-led pipe demand may rise but farmer income may be constrained, offset by strong tractor and rural two-wheeler bookings.

qa_highlights.question: Supply chain impact from Middle East disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the disruption affected crude and petrochemical supply chains, but teams re-established supply from other sources; EDC and VCM are 100% imported.

El Nino and water scarcity weighing on agri demand, which is about 60% of volume in Q2.

Trade policy: MIP status and DGTR-recommended CVD on Chinese PVC pending Ministry of Finance decision.
