501423|2026-03.headline: Shaily FY26 revenue rose 26% to INR991 crores and PAT 83% to INR170 crores, led by Healthcare revenue up 139% to INR393 crores.
501423|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9% YoY to INR237 crores with EBITDA margin of 29.3% and PAT of INR40 crores (up 40%). Healthcare doubled in Q4 to INR113 crores on Semaglutide pen injector commercial launches in Canada and India, while Consumer fell 31% to INR102 crores on weak US and European home furnishing demand. Management announced a semiconductor tray supply agreement and first commercial supplies to a consumer electronics customer, and an INR500 crore enabling fundraise resolution (described as annual, with no specific raise planned). The pen capacity ramp is behind plan: the 25 million-unit line added in March runs at about 45% efficiency.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR102 crores vs INR148 crores (-31%). FY26 revenue INR511 crores (-9%). Management cited weaker home furnishing demand in Europe and US, and some Middle East order cancellations in Q4 due to the war there.

segments.name: Industrial

Semaglutide line target to run at 65-67 parts per minute by year end, giving a combined 40-42 million pens from the two new lines.

501423|2026-06.headline: Shaily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR281 crore, with Healthcare up 85% to INR142 crore, now the largest segment at 51%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected cost impact from the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Pet coke has risen from around $120 to $136-140 CIF, adding about ₹200/tonne at clinker and ₹100-150/tonne at cement. Inventory cover runs to mid-Q2, and imported coal is being partly switched to domestic coal, with the outcome known by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise 28% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Around ₹11.5 crore was one-offs: about ₹7.5 crore mine bearing land (MBL) cess and about ₹3.24 crore DMF expense at a subsidiary, covering roughly 3-3.5 years of accrual. Promotional spend also rose. Excluding one-offs, growth is about 26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY27 volume of 7 Mt be achieved given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target relies on Jeerabad (+0.5 Mt), Andhra ramp-up (+0.9 Mt) and market growth; it chooses not to chase share at the expense of cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will Jeerabad clinker sales continue in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Some clinker sales are expected during the phased ramp-up, subject to clinker prices, with margin held at that location's level.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any cost reduction left after Andhra stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: Andhra clinker cost is now in line; the new VRM (by September) should deliver the planned savings. Margins are expected to be better in FY27 than FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net debt rise above guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter unsecured debt for the Andhra project was drawn after the planned rights issue became an OFS, and solar capex was accelerated for short payback. Debt is expected to fall from operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose sharply: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Credit days were extended in a difficult market, fuel prices were higher, and volumes grew. About ₹80 crore of US coal was bought in March on 180-day LC credit. Moderation is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Vizag land GO status and sale timing?
qa_highlights.answer: GVMC and UDA approvals are in place; the state GO is awaited, expected within six months. Management is assuming ₹350 crore over 18-24 months at the old reckoner rate of ₹4 crore per acre.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cost gap between standalone and Andhra?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly logistics and market spread, with the Andhra cost gap closing after investments; detail to be discussed offline.

502090|2026-06.headline: Sagar Cements Q1 FY27: volumes up ~13% YoY but loss after tax of ₹28 crore and EBITDA of ₹451/tonne on West Asia-driven cost inflation.
502090|2026-06.overview: Volumes grew about 13% YoY and revenue rose 5% YoY, with realisations broadly stable. Profitability moderated as energy, fuel and packaging costs rose amid West Asia tensions, leaving EBITDA at ₹451 per tonne and a loss after tax of ₹28 crore. Management maintained a 7 million tonne volume target for FY27 (excluding clinker) and reiterated FY27 EBITDA guidance of ₹500–550 per tonne, down from the earlier ~₹600 reference raised by an analyst. Capex completed in the quarter includes Jeerabad 0.5 million tonne expansion and the remaining 1.55 MW of Gudipadu waste heat recovery; the 0.75 million tonne Andhra Cements expansion is expected by quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7 million tonne FY27 volume target ex-clinker, and how much clinker will be sold in Q2 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: The 7 mt target excludes clinker. Clinker is still sold to Andhra Cements' sister unit Bayyavaram and some outside, and some at Jeerabad until ramp-up; management would not quantify volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Is double-digit volume growth possible in FY28, and what is the Q2 cost inflation and is the ~₹600/t EBITDA guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says FY27 and FY28 both see double-digit volume growth. Full-year cost pressure is about ₹100/t across fuel, raw material and miscellaneous, offset by savings; Q2 gets extra inventory and maintenance cost at three plants. Guidance is ₹500–550/t, assuming flat prices, not ~₹600.

qa_highlights.question: Are prices stable versus Q1 averages?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices have been flat from March exit to July and June to July; realisation was up about ₹50–60/t, with the cause unclear (mix or price hikes).

qa_highlights.question: Status of Vizag land sale and FY27 realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Awaiting a generic Government GO after the government signalled it would replace a case-specific order; the ₹150 crore for FY27 is still seen as doable. Management said buyer engagement exists but timelines were the issue.

qa_highlights.question: Which regions drive incremental H2 FY27 demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all incremental volume comes from the South (~80% of footprint). Madpradesh is also expected to rise after the 0.5 mt Jeerabad expansion, supporting the ~15% growth projected for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How does Andhra Cements' cost structure compare with Mattampally, and how should the three units be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Variable cost at Andhra is ₹100–125/t higher than Mattampally because it buys grid power without waste heat recovery; management says the kcal and unit metrics are at par. Andhra carries most of the debt, and management offered to share modelling details offline.

qa_highlights.question: Can Q1 EBITDA of ~₹425/t reach ₹600/t for full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹550/t is 'definitely doable', citing Gudipadu WHR savings, Jeerabad expansion and the Andhra cement mill due end-September, assuming stable prices.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex going to rise, and what is the debt reduction path?
qa_highlights.answer: No new capex beyond ₹30–40 crore annual maintenance through 2028. About ₹240 crore of ongoing capex spreads over FY27 and FY28; operating cash flow is not yet reflected in the gross debt path.

qa_highlights.question: What are the levers to manage power and fuel costs if the West Asia crisis escalates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has no control over prices and can only manage consumption, which it says is efficient. Inventory covers operations to mid-October; ₹100/t inflation is pencilled in (₹50 fuel, ₹50 other), and clinker is at its peak.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Tamil Nadu ban on rough stone and aggregate transport, and what limestone auction premiums are seen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no impact. Recent Telangana limestone auctions, about a year or 18 months old, went at 50–75% premiums; other auctions are pending in TN, AP and Telangana.

qa_highlights.answer: Parth Bhavsar asked about net debt trajectory. Management said the ₹150 crore land sale is in FY27 and about ₹200 crore in FY28.

502219|2026-03.headline: Borosil Renewables FY26 standalone sales rose 38% to INR1,534.83 crore and EBITDA margin hit 32% on higher solar glass realisations.
502219|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone sales were INR437.62 crore (up ~34% YoY, a record quarter) with EBITDA of INR144.61 crore at 33% of sales, helped by average ex-factory realisation of INR150.2/mm and about 15% higher volumes. Management attributed roughly half the quarterly sales jump to Ind AS revenue recognition timing (about 6% of Q4 sales), and said the run-rate is nearer INR400-410 crore a quarter. Fuel surcharges passed to customers during the West Asia-driven gas price spike had negligible net impact on realisation (under INR1/mm). The company wrote off its German exposure (Geosphere and GMB) with no additional P&L loss, as a provision was already made in Q1 FY26. Management also announced a rooftop solar branded-products venture, a 600 TPD furnace expansion targeted for Q4 FY27, and an enabling resolution to raise up to INR750 crore in equity.

segments.name: Solar glass (standalone, Bharuch)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR1,534.83 crore with EBITDA margin 32%; Q4 volumes up 15% YoY and 14% QoQ, with production run at full capacity and no curtailment during the West Asia disruption.

segments.name: Overseas subsidiaries (Germany)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 overseas net revenue INR2.3 crore and EBITDA INR0.82 crore, versus INR3.96 crore and INR1.90 crore in the prior quarter; German production shut from July 2025 and exposure to Geosphere and GMB written off.

segments.name: Rooftop solar (new division)
segments.commentary: Early-stage branded rooftop solutions business sourcing modules, inverters and batteries from outside vendors; first sales booked in March 2026, with a first-year target of about INR75 crore and expected initial EBITDA margin below 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management sees 30-33% EBITDA margin as achievable on a normal basis, barring unforeseen circumstances.
Run-rate quarterly sales of about INR400-410 crore after the roughly 6% Ind AS timing benefit in Q4 falls away.

600 TPD of new capacity (two 300 TPD furnaces) targeted for production within FY27; management said the first furnace is on track for around January 2027 and that sales contribution should come from Q1 FY28, with some sales possible in FY27.
Tax rate expected around 21% of PBT, with minimal cash tax while INR950 crore of expansion capex is capitalised.
SG1 and SG2 furnace rebuild capex of about INR100 crore expected in the next calendar year.
Customs notification for continuation of countervailing duty on Malaysian solar glass expected before the current duty expires on 6-8 June 2026.
capex_capacity: Expansion of 600 TPD (two 300 TPD furnaces) at the existing location is in full swing; nearly all orders placed and building construction on plan, taking capacity from about 1,000 TPD to about 1,600 TPD (around 60% uplift).
Management cited INR950 crore of capitalisation planned in the current financial year.

Domestic solar glass capacity is about 2,600 TPD (about 18 GW); about 33 GW of further capacity is expected by March 2027, mostly captive, taking the domestic total to about 51 GW against demand of about 65 GW.
Rooftop business: no capex for 1-1.5 years; the company may consider inverter assembly after 6-8 months to a year, but not module manufacturing.
Board approved an enabling resolution to raise equity up to INR750 crore, subject to shareholder approval; management said there are no current plans to raise capital.
demand_pricing: Realisation held near INR150/mm; management said pass-through of gas and fuel cost added less than INR1/mm, and that the price is tied to the landed cost of Chinese imports and near peak levels, with rupee depreciation providing only limited headroom.
Domestic solar installations were 44.6 GW in FY26 versus 23.8 GW in FY25, implying about 60-62 GW of glass consumption; imports still supply about 70% of demand.
ALMM-II (domestic solar cells) effective June 2026; solar cell capacity at 30 GW, expected to reach 75 GW by FY-end; ALMM-III for ingots and wafers from June 2028.

Indonesian Chinese-owned plant (about 1,500 TPD) has entered the market but has made limited impact so far; the Turkish producer's exports face high freight costs; the UAE plant is blocked by Strait of Hormuz conditions.
Export demand is low in major markets; the US may grow as customers seek non-Chinese origin glass, and Europe has niche demand for greenhouses and flat-plate collectors.

Cost pressure from oil-linked inputs is so far modest; vendors are seeking pass-through and the company is negotiating; gas quantities are secured under medium- and short-term contracts, but spot prices are high.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR150/mm realisation comes from fuel pass-through, and what would it be without it?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Jain said the pass-through contributed less than INR1/mm, about INR0.70-0.75, and a similar increase is visible in net realisation between Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will realisation or margins come under pressure as new domestic capacity arrives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no pressure for domestic producers; most upcoming capacity is captive, demand exceeds the 51 GW expected capacity, and Indonesian imports are not yet a price threat.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 13-15% sequential sales growth with flat realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly half was production gain (about 7%) and half was Ind AS timing: in-transit sales were lower at the end of Q3 and so were recognised in Q4, with the sales base reset to about INR400-410 crore a quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is gas supply secure given the West Asia crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Quantities are broadly secured under medium- and short-term contracts; the government gas cut is based on the past six-month average, and the rest is bought at market-related prices, so price rather than volume is the constraint.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar roadmap, capex and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: No capex for 1-1.5 years; modules, inverters and batteries will be outsourced; first-year target is about INR75 crore, with margins expected below 10% initially and little or no profit in year one; working capital is kept low by negotiating terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will the furnace expansion commissioning timeline hold, and what does it do to margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing is as currently planned (first furnace around January 2027), with sales from Q1 FY28; operating leverage and higher yield are expected, but management did not commit to a specific margin uplift.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and tax?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has fallen because older SG1 and SG2 assets are fully depreciated; current charge mainly reflects the 2023 expansion. Tax is around 21% of PBT, with deferred tax at a similar rate.

risks_watch: CVD on Malaysian solar glass expires 6-8 June 2026; a delayed or diluted notification would affect pricing.
Fuel surcharge and gas price volatility from the West Asia conflict; management said the Q1 FY27 reset depends on the 30 June stock-take.
Ind AS timing effects could make quarterly sales lumpy; management flagged the INR400-410 crore run-rate as the base case.
Indonesian Chinese-owned capacity could pressure prices; management suggested BIS and quality-control measures as a mitigant.
Rooftop business faces competition from Tata Power, Havells and Luminous, and early margins are guided below 10%.
Furnace commissioning slippage (first furnace January 2027 target) and the planned INR100 crore SG1/SG2 rebuild capex.
Export demand remains weak in Europe; freight costs are high because of Red Sea and Hormuz disruptions.
502219|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the domestic demand-supply gap and pricing, but cautious on the sustainability of Q4 sales, which management explicitly said were inflated by Ind AS timing. Management was evasive on expansion beyond the 600 TPD project, and on furnace timing beyond a 'we'll see' at the Q2 call. Tone on the rooftop venture was enthusiastic, with the chairman openly saying margins would be far lower.

502219|2026-06.headline: Borosil Renewables Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 53% YoY to INR405.69 crore and EBITDA to INR142 crore (35% margin), helped by a fuel surcharge.
502219|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales were INR405.69 crore, up 53% YoY from INR332.26 crore, while EBITDA rose to INR142 crore at 35% of sales versus 27.9% a year ago. Average ex-factory realisation rose to INR160.30 per sq m from INR150.20 in Q4 FY26, including a INR9.50 fuel surcharge introduced from 10 March 2026 after the West Asia war raised fuel costs. Management said the surcharge is now being cut as fuel prices ease, and that the 600 TPD furnace expansion is on track for commissioning in Q1 FY27-end (January to March 2027). Reported PAT of about INR169 crore in Q4 FY26 was inflated by a INR75 crore tax write-back, so the sequential PAT comparison is not like-for-like.

segments.commentary: Early-stage on-grid residential kit (module, inverter, battery) sold as a system. Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore against an internal FY27 target of about INR36 crore; EBITDA margin expected in single digits, versus 30-35% for glass.

guidance_outlook: 600 TPD expansion at the existing site: construction targeted by December 2026, commissioning January to March 2027 (SG4 and SG5, about one month apart). Management says revenue should be modelled from 1 April 2027, though the internal target is 1 March.
Once the 600 TPD is commissioned, sales are expected to rise about 60%, adding about INR80-85 crore of quarterly EBITDA at current run-rate and prices.
Realisation to fall as the INR9.50 fuel surcharge is passed back to customers; management says cost declines should offset this, so profit is not expected to be affected.

Management declined to give a formal guidance but said it expects to continue at similar revenue and EBITDA levels if conditions hold; expects extra profitability this year because prices were at full levels all year.
Ambition to grow from about INR2,500 crore to at least INR4,000 crore revenue in 3-4 years after March 2027; next expansion decision expected within about 6 months.
capex_capacity: Current capacity 1,000 TPD; expansion of 600 TPD at existing location takes it to 1,600 TPD, with the expansion fully funded per management.

Furnace SG1 and SG2 refurbishment: timing not fixed, possibly Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28, likely after SG4/SG5 are commissioned. A rebuild needs about 75 days of shutdown plus 15 days to restart, so about 90 days with no output from the furnace being rebuilt.
Any further capacity beyond the 600 TPD expansion would be a new building and facility, sized at 600 or 1,200 TPD, and not an add-on to the current layout.
Domestic solar glass capacity expected to reach 7,700 TPD by March 2027 (about 51 GW), against about 2,600 TPD (18 GW) today and about 11,000 TPD demand for 62 GW of module requirement.

Module capacity in India is 203 GW; solar cell capacity is 30 GW, expected to rise to 75 GW by 2027 under ALMM-2 (effective 1 June 2026). ALMM-3 for ingot and wafer starts 28 June, with about 50 GW expected by 2029.
demand_pricing: Management says domestic industry supplies only about 25% of demand; even at 7,700 TPD, supply would cover only 75%, so pricing is expected to hold, with import-parity pricing as the reference.
Exports to the US are very small and in niche applications; the company is focused on the domestic market.
A significant portion of new domestic capacity is captive, so the open-market supply gain is limited, according to management.
Management expects module makers to consolidate over the next 1-1.5 years because module capacity far exceeds requirement; Mono PERC players and those without cell supply may drop volumes.
CVD of 9.71% on solar glass imports from Malaysia extended for five more years from 2 June 2026, on top of anti-dumping duties on China and Vietnam since December 2024.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall from INR169 crore in Q4 to INR87 crore in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY26 PAT included a INR75 crore tax write-back tied to the write-off of the German subsidiary investment (INR325 crore provision). Excluding it, performance was not inferior.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days rose from 34 to 152; is that right?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 152-day figure, saying working capital is about 60 days, with a slight rise from stores inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic prices fall as capacity grows to 7,700 TPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is robust, with domestic supply covering only about 25% now, and that pricing is anchored to import parity, so no pricing challenge is foreseen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rooftop solar business worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal FY27 revenue target is about INR36 crore, Q1 revenue about INR1.3 crore, with single-digit EBITDA margins because it is a trading-style solution business.

qa_highlights.question: Any equity raise or debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: The current expansion is fully funded. Future projects will be funded from internal cash, with some debt if the project is large. No near-term equity raise is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is the gross margin around 80% calculated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management put gross margin at about 78% on a manufacturing-cost basis, with raw material at about 23-24% of sales, and said margin volatility is not expected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of the SG1 patch repair and the volume effect of furnace rebuilds?
qa_highlights.answer: A four-day patch on one furnace cost about INR3 crore in lost output. A full rebuild would shut the furnace for about 90 days, causing a volume loss in the year it happens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 25.2% should be assumed for the full year.

Commissioning risk: the 600 TPD expansion (SG4, SG5) must be commissioned by March 2027, with revenue only from April 2027. Any delay pushes the 60% volume uplift later.
Furnace SG1/SG2 rebuild: about 90 days of lost output per furnace, timing not fixed (Q4 FY27 to Q2 FY28); this could reduce FY28 volumes against the 1,600 TPD capacity.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers are about 65-68% of volume, and module consolidation could affect volumes.
Capacity additions in domestic glass (to 7,700 TPD by March 2027) could pressure prices, though management expects supply to stay short.
Rooftop solar and the overseas subsidiaries are small and early, with unclear profitability; the call gave no segment-level data.
Management declined to comment on press reports of a strategic investment. Next-phase project choice (glass furnace or adjacent business) is due in about 5-6 months.

502219|2026-09.headline: Borosil Renewables Q2 FY27 solar glass sales were INR382.1 crore with EBITDA margin down to 30.4% on furnace maintenance and a 2.8% price cut, with October output reported higher.
502219|2026-09.overview: Standalone H1 FY27 sales rose 12.8% to INR801.8 crore and EBITDA rose 18.5% to INR258.3 crore, but Q2 alone showed softer numbers. Q2 solar glass sales were flat YoY at INR382.1 crore, with EBITDA of INR116.34 crore at 30.4% margin versus 33% a year earlier, because of furnace maintenance (production down about 4.5-5%) and a reduced fuel surcharge after gas prices eased in July. The 600 tpd expansion (about 60% capacity addition, project cost raised by INR150 crore to about INR1,100 crore) is on track for commissioning toward end-Q4 FY27, funded internally without extra bank debt.

Anti-dumping duty on China and Vietnam in place until December 2029; management sees domestic supply shortfall supporting pricing.
Management says there is no cost-plus or pass-through for raw materials; the fuel surcharge was a one-off force majeure recovery, so productivity gains are needed to offset other cost increases.

Standalone Q4 revenue rose 2% YoY to INR2,894 crore, but EBITDA margin was hit late in the quarter by geopolitical supply-chain headwinds, and FY26 EBITDA fell 10% YoY to INR2,423 crore. The company has stopped giving volume guidance, is starting its on-highway push (TBR, 2-wheeler, PCR), and has approved an additional INR2,000 crore capex. Management signalled raw material and margin pressure into FY27 with only partial price pass-through so far.

Phase 1 CV radial capex of INR750 crore added 800 tyres a day of fungible CVR/OHT capacity; PCR launch is targeted by end of calendar 2026 with first-phase capacity of 6,700 tyres a day. Long-term vision is INR5,000 crore revenue by 2030.

502355|2026-09.headline: BKT signs Pirelli offtake deal to produce 800,000 Pirelli-branded premium car tires per year by 2030 at Bhuj PCR plant, starting CY2027.
502355|2026-09.overview: This was a short business update call on the Pirelli-BKT strategic offtake agreement, held at short notice, with Q2 FY27 performance explicitly off-limits under the silent-period policy. BKT will manufacture Pirelli-branded car tires (17-inch and above) at its newly built Bhuj PCR plant, ramping gradually from CY2027 to 800,000 tires per year by CY2030. Management said the offtake fits within the existing expansion programme, with no additional capex for the offtake, and pricing is raw material at actuals plus conversion cost.

Q4 gross margin rose about 300 bps QoQ, but EBITDA was held back by an other-expense charge of about INR57–58 crore from mark-to-market on rupee forward cover after the rupee hit INR94.80 on 31 March. Management said fabric price increases lag yarn by 2–3 months, so Q4 did not fully reflect the improvement and Q1 FY27 should be better. The call gave no formal numeric guidance; most outlook comments were qualitative and tied to cotton, the dollar-rupee rate and the FTA pipeline.

segments.name: Fabric
segments.commentary: Management said fabric price hikes are being pushed selectively, with a 2–3 month lag to yarn. The new performance (100% synthetic) fabric plant, commissioned last fiscal year, is expected to reach full use in 6–9 months.

Remaining ~10% of spinning modernisation to finish in the next 6–8 months; biomass boilers and other green power projects to commission in 1–2 months, with cost benefits from June or July.
Forex mark-to-market will reverse or add depending on where the dollar-rupee closes; no forecast was given.
Cotton: Vardhman normally holds 6–8 months of cotton cover; new Indian crop arrives around October, so stocks must be run down by September.
Management expects FTA-driven demand to build over roughly 12–15 months and is finalising capacity plans over the next 2–3 months.
capex_capacity: Spinning modernisation about 90% complete; remaining work to finish within the current financial year (next 6–8 months).

Performance fabric plant commissioned last fiscal year; 6–9 months needed to build order book. A fourth cotton and normal fabric line was also commissioned in FY26 but could not be fully used because of US tariffs; utilisation is expected in 6–9 months.
Open-end spinning project on hold to restart. New land in PM MITRA Park, Madhya Pradesh is expected by December or January, with plans to be finalised in 2–3 months.

Industry spindles: about 53 million rated; 11–12 million permanently stopped, leaving about 41–42 million working (industry estimate, not government data). Normal additions of 2–2.5 million per year were missed for three years.
Garment capacity expansion approved as a first step to viability; no decision on broader expansion.
demand_pricing: Chinese buying of Indian yarn rose to ~30 million kg per month over the last 4–5 months, against 7–8 million kg earlier. India's monthly yarn exports reached ~120 million kg-plus against a 100 million kg average.

Cotton: New York futures rose from ~$0.62–0.63/lb to ~$0.82–0.83/lb. Indian cotton moved from INR52,000–53,000/candy to INR67,000–68,000/candy; CCI selling price was INR67,000/candy after a ~INR5,000 rise in the last week.
Indian cotton is now priced around New York plus $0.05–0.08, close to the long-run relationship. Management said this removes the earlier disadvantage for spinners.

Pricing: fabric and garment price increases are being pushed across the chain. Brands are granting only small increases so far, with management expecting more clarity in 1–2 months. Yarn cost pass-through was described as comfortable given stronger demand.

Management noted US garment and home textile utilisation has recovered to roughly 90–100% after tariffs eased, from 50–60% earlier. Earlier, US tariffs reached 50%, which had forced discounting and loss-making orders.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yarn prices follow international cotton and that higher Indian cotton cost is absorbed by Indian producers. Demand and higher cotton costs have been passed on comfortably so far.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA margin expansion limited despite gross margin gains?

502986|2026-06.headline: Vardhman Q1 FY27 margins rose on spinning yarn-size gains and raw-material trading gains; fabric utilisation remains weak as US orders slipped.
502986|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 FY27 numbers improved in both percentage and absolute terms, driven mainly by the spinning business through better yarn sizes and a partial trading gain on raw material bought before the cotton price rise. The fabric business lagged: absolute volumes were roughly flat YoY and 3-4% below Q4 FY26, because US orders were lost after a missed sampling season tied to US tariffs. Management expects the spinning margin to moderate as cheap inventory runs out, but sees a 13-14% margin as a reasonable direction. Capex is mostly complete, with biomass boilers starting and the Dhar (PM MITRA) site dependent on land and power by around December 2026 and June 2027.

502986|2026-09.headline: Vardhman Q2 FY27: yarn business recovered on higher prices and trading gains, while fabric fell YoY and QoQ on export weakness and ~20% higher input costs.
502986|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as better than Q1 and the prior year, led by the yarn business, where yarn prices rose on export demand and higher cotton costs. Part of the yarn gain came from trading gains on cotton bought at about Rs 54-55k/candy that was later valued near Rs 64-65k/candy. Fabric was weak: top line and bottom line fell YoY and QoQ, with lower export volumes, a ~20% YoY rise in input costs, and limited pass-through. The performance fabric (synthetics) unit, commissioned in March, is still ramping and is guided to turn operating-positive in H2 FY27. Management also laid out long-term margin and growth guidance and gave a cautious view on new cotton-season prices.

segments.name: Yarn (spinning)
segments.commentary: Better performance on demand from exports and higher yarn prices, plus operational gains from recent modernisation and trading gains on cotton. Management said the trading gain may not repeat as new-season cotton costs are higher. Spinning utilisation is near 100%, with about Rs 500 crore of capex due in the next 6 months.

segments.name: Fabric (natural / processed)
segments.commentary: Weak quarter: lower export volumes amid US tariff uncertainty, domestic pricing pressure, and a 25%+ rise in processing capacity still being absorbed, so fixed-cost absorption was low. qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cotton prices and the duty-free import window?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Indian price is linked to ICE futures and is around Rs 65k/candy. The Dec 31 duty-free window is too short to bring in large volumes, so Indian cotton is unlikely to fall much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand-supply gap in yarn, and what investment is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited capacity exits of about 12 million spindles. A new 100,000-spindle plant would cost over Rs 1,000 crore, and the sector needs clarity on raw-material policy before investing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current spinning capacity utilisation and peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Spinning is at about 100% utilisation. The only near-term addition is about Rs 500 crore of capacity due in the next 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Bangladesh situation and how exposed is Vardhman?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said wage unrest is recurring and expected to settle around Taka 17-18k. Bangladesh takes about 30-35% of India's roughly 110 million kg/month of yarn exports.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fabric utilisation trend and peak revenue potential on current capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was about 70-75% in Q2 and is about 80% now. Management expects 90-95% and about 25% higher revenue on current capacity, with the increase over a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is M&A or inorganic growth in spinning being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to options, but small or distressed targets have not been viable. Its stated preference is organic growth through its own land and projects.

503100|2026-03.headline: Phoenix Mills FY26 consolidated revenue rose 16% to Rs 4,423 crore and EBITDA 22% to Rs 2,637 crore, with no new retail capacity added.
503100|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong broad-based growth: consolidated revenue Rs 4,423 crore (+16%), EBITDA Rs 2,637 crore (+22%), and PAT Rs 1,557 crore (+20%), achieved without adding retail area. Retail consumption hit a record Rs 16,587 crore (+21%), with Q4 up 31%, though retail rentals grew only 10% to Rs 2,157 crore, which management attributes to the MG-plus-revenue-share lease structure and ramp-up of newer malls. Offices expanded to 4.8 million sq ft with occupancy at 70%, and management expects a meaningful step-up in office income from FY27. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 1.19x despite the ISMDPL (CPP stake) buyout and peak construction capex.

qa_highlights.answer: Ex-jewellery and electronics, Q4 consumption growth was about 17-18%. Management expects the gap to narrow as revenue share kicks in, and says rental growth should hold even if jewellery and electronics moderate.

qa_highlights.question: When will office rental income start and how fast will it ramp?

503100|2026-06.headline: Phoenix Mills Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 13% to Rs 1,075 crore and operating EBITDA 14% to Rs 642 crore, with retail consumption up 32%.

Retail consumption grew 32% to Rs 4,730 crore, though jewelry and electronics drove much of that growth; ex-jewelry and electronics consumption grew 24% while rental grew 17%. Capex was Rs 1,085 crore, including Rs 716 crore paid to GAMADA for Chandigarh land, and net debt stood at Rs 3,658 crore (1.3x net debt/EBITDA).

503100|2026-09.headline: Phoenix Mills Q2 FY27 annuity EBITDA rose 21% to Rs 669 crore, with retail consumption up 25% and rental income up 15%.
503100|2026-09.overview: Annuity revenue (retail, offices, hotel, asset management) grew 16% YoY to Rs 1,055 crore in Q2, with annuity EBITDA up 21% to Rs 669 crore and PAT before minority interest up 31% to Rs 391 crore. Consolidated revenue of Rs 1,153 crore was held back by lower residential handovers (Rs 62 crore recognised in H1), with Rs 120 crore of sold units slated for H2. Office occupancy rose to about 79% in September 2026 from 70% in March 2026, and consumption grew 25% with no new retail area added. Management reaffirmed double-digit rental growth for FY28, stated retail rental guidance of 15% for FY27 could be exceeded, and disclosed progress on the ISMDPL stake step-up to 68.1%.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Rental income up 15% to Rs 605 crore in Q2 and 16% to Rs 1,200 crore in H1; retail EBITDA up 18% to Rs 639 crore in Q2. Consumption Rs 4,685 crore (+25%); excluding jewellery and electronics +22%.

segments.name: Offices
segments.commentary: Office income up 64% YoY to Rs 89 crore and EBITDA up similarly to Rs 56 crore in Q2; 54% of the new office portfolio is rent generating against 79% leased.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: The St. Regis Mumbai income and EBITDA up 13% in Q2, with average room rate up 20% and EBITDA margin at 44%.

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Revenue recognised on handover; only Rs 62 crore in H1 versus a significantly higher prior-year period. Rs 120 crore of sold units to be booked in H2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: Retail rental growth guidance of 14-15% for FY27 (given in April) expected to be exceeded by 1-2 percentage points, per management.
Rental growth of 14-15% factored for FY28 as the more tangible metric; double-digit rental growth expected in FY28 from existing assets.
Phoenix Mall of Asia expected to sustain healthy double-digit consumption growth in FY28.
October 2026 consumption expected at least 20% YoY on a normalised basis, with upside toward 25%; full-month figures due late November.
ISMDPL stake to rise from 58.33% to 68.1% on completion of capital reduction, expected November 2026, for Rs 1,350 crore consideration. Credit rating upgrades expected in one to two weeks.
capex_capacity: Kolkata mall: fit-outs to start around Q2 FY27 (calendar), launch about six months later; about 90% leased. Kolkata residential launch expected in about two quarters.
Surat mall: 50% leased, completion by 2027 and opening in 2028. Bengaluru Whitefield retail expansion (1-1.5 lakh sq ft): completion by 2027, about 70% leased.
Palladium (Lower Parel) Rise 1 expansion: about 150 stores, 60% leased, rentals expected above Rs 500 psf pm; mall operational in calendar 2027. Rise offices targeted for 2028.
Thane, Chandigarh and Coimbatore malls targeted for operations in calendar 2030. Bengaluru first-phase office (about 400,000 sq ft) and Grand Hyatt Bangalore hotel to become operational.
Lucknow Palassio adds about 100,000 sq ft (about 100 stores) with a further floor; Palladium adds 150 stores. Land spend H1 about Rs 800 crore, construction spend H1 about Rs 700 crore.
demand_pricing: Consumption up 25% YoY to Rs 4,685 crore in Q2 and 28% to Rs 9,415 crore in H1; every mall delivered double-digit consumption growth.
Trading occupancy rose only about 3 percentage points YoY; management attributed not more than 3% of the 25% growth to added trading area.
Fashion and accessories (about 60% of trading area) +22%; F&B +21%; entertainment +16%.

Phoenix Mall of Asia consumption +68%, rental +44%, trading occupancy 96% vs 84%. Bengaluru MarketCity consumption +19%, rental +25%, occupancy 93% vs 82%. Pune Avenue of Stars consumption +21%, rental +16%, occupancy 90% vs 82%.
Trading density crossed Rs 3,300 psf pm. Rent-to-consumption ratio at 13%, against a long-term range of 13.5-14%.
About 50% of retail area lease expiries fall between FY27 and FY29; repricing typically gives about 20% uplift on prior minimum guarantee rents.
September was seasonally weak; 2-3% of quarterly consumption lost to fit-outs, with 5% of leasable area under active fit-out.

qa_highlights.question: Why is residential at Kolkata not yet launched more than three and a half years after land acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited an initial plan change from a different use to pure residential and approval delays linked to elections; launch expected in about two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-leasing status of upcoming malls (Kolkata, Surat, Bengaluru, Palladium)?
qa_highlights.answer: Kolkata about 90% leased, Surat 50%, Bengaluru expansion about 70%, Palladium Rise 1 about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: Is October consumption growth tracking?
qa_highlights.answer: Normalised for Diwali timing, October is expected at least 20% YoY, possibly toward 25%; final figures due late November.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 rental growth exceed the 15% guidance given the 16% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects guidance to be raised by 1-2 percentage points and is optimistic it can be exceeded, pending festive-season data.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 10-city pipeline raise the 1 million sq ft annual addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said land is not yet secured for the new cities, so no timelines or guidance change; new cities expected in the 2035-36 plan. Benchmark per new mall moves to 1.3-1.4 million sq ft.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 1,440 crore H1 capex in the cash flow reconcile with lower construction spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Difference is land: Chandigarh land completion payment of about Rs 700 crore in Q1, plus smaller Coimbatore and Kolkata parcels and an advance for an acquisition under discussion.

Residential revenue lumpiness; Rs 120 crore of sold units to be recognised in H2 FY27.
Office leasing conversion: 79% leased but only 54% rent generating; targets of 70% by March and 80% by mid-2027.
Pending acquisition with advance already paid; undisclosed size and timing.
Credit rating upgrades and ISMDPL capital reduction completion expected November 2026.
Management declined to guide beyond FY28 rental growth.

Consumption is driven by many factors, whether gold prices or electronics or some new stores or categories doing well or not doing well.

503101|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated PAT of INR 206 crores, the company's highest ever, alongside INR 900 crores QIP and INR 576 crores FY26 presales (MNRL share).
503101|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as transformational, citing record PAT of INR 206 crores on total income of INR 639 crores and EBITDA of INR 261 crores. The INR 900 crore QIP was used for about INR 340 crores of debt repayment, roughly a third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores earmarked for new acquisitions, of which only about INR 54 crores (call also cited ~INR 50 crores) was deployed. The company acquired controlling interests in three Kanjurmarg entities (~INR 70 crores investment) with a six-project pipeline of over INR 840 crores GDV, and took a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd. The amalgamation has received no-adverse-observation letters from BSE and NSE and documents have been filed with NCLT, with hearing awaited.

segments.name: Marathon Futurex (Lower Parel, commercial)
segments.commentary: Presales rose 15% YoY to INR 466 crores on leasing and absorption; management says prices firmed about 15% YoY and rates rose 50-60% over five to six years. Inventory may take 12-15 months to exhaust.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, luxury residential, 40% revenue share)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 391 crores in FY26. Tower B has OC up to the 45th floor, with the 45th-65th floors topped out and expected complete by December 2026. Tower C is built to 17 floors; Tower D is unlaunched; a commercial Tower 5 may launch in 12-18 months.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Presales of INR 104 crores. Phase 3 launched with about 4.9 lakh sq ft carpet area and INR 600 crores GDV. Phase 2 towers Antilia, Triton and Atria received full OC.

segments.name: Neo series (Bhandup)
segments.commentary: NeoValley, NeoPark, NeoSquare and Bhandup projects together recorded about INR 65 crores presales; NeoSquare received OC. Newly launched Neohome has INR 370 crores GDV.

segments.name: Mulund Millennium (commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 21 crores presales in FY26 from small offices and retail spaces.

segments.name: Kanjurmarg (acquired, PTC/B2B model)
segments.commentary: Six residential projects with GDV over INR 840 crores; one project at 5th slab of a 23-storey building; about INR 225 crores+ of GDV to launch within 12 months. Company holds 50% controlling interest and one-third economic interest in the transit camp model.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA margins of 30-40% on the Kanjurmarg projects, in line with current company margins.
Remaining INR 250 crores-odd of the INR 300 crore new-project allocation is yet to be spent on acquisitions.
Monte South Tower B floors 45-65 expected to complete by December 2026, adding to revenue recognition.
Post-merger, around 418 acres of land is expected to come into the listed entity; management cited Panvel plotted development possibly launching in FY27 or FY28.
Bonus issue timing is uncertain; management said it may or may not happen after amalgamation.
Strategic focus for FY27: accelerate execution, expand presales, pursue redevelopment and acquisitions, scale PTC-led B2B vertical, maintain prudent capital allocation.
capex_capacity: Unsold value of the listed entity (MNRL share) around INR 6,500 crores, plus the INR 840 crores Kanjurmarg pipeline; the company said this covers about five years of inventory.
Unsold launched inventory is about INR 2,000 crores, with cost to complete about INR 1,600 crores.
Management's thumb rule: unsold/unlaunched projects need about 60% of cost still to be spent.
Revenue recognised on percentage-of-completion basis; completion percentages are shown in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management says Grade A office demand in South and Central Mumbai is strong; supply is lower than before, and Futurex prices firmed about 15% YoY.
Futurex serves more than 300 institutional and leasing clients, including Nykaa, ZEE, L'Oreal, SBI and HDFC; leasing ticket sizes start from 1,500-2,000 sq ft.
Luxury segment inventory at premium addresses is said to be tight, supporting pricing at Monte South.
Infrastructure tailwinds cited: Navi Mumbai airport, Atal Setu, Panvel-Karjat rail, EduCity, Kharghar commercial complex, GMLR (Goregaon-Mulund Link Road) and Dombivli bullet train station.
BMC cleared 384 unauthorised structures in Mulund, Amar Nagar and Khindipada for the eastern GMLR section (about 12 km).

qa_highlights.question: Launch timelines, capital deployment and margins for the Kanjurmarg projects?
qa_highlights.answer: GDV is over INR 840 crores and could go higher depending on PTC or pre-sale model. About 10% is ongoing; more than INR 225 crores will launch within 12 months. Expected EBITDA margins are 30-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: No-adverse-observation letters received from BSE and NSE; all documents filed with NCLT. Company awaits the hearing; stakeholder meetings to be dispensed with given NOCs.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 900 crore QIP be allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 340 crores repaid as debt, about one-third for existing project execution, and about INR 300 crores for new acquisitions. More than 30 projects evaluated; about three shortlisted; two acquired (Sunset Spaces and Kanjurmarg).

qa_highlights.question: Will commercial share of the portfolio increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to balance the portfolio by adding a new commercial project as each is sold; Monte South Tower 5 is a future commercial project.

qa_highlights.question: Remaining balance-sheet and unsold inventory question for Monte South and the 50% share?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on percentage of completion; sold area's revenue is recognised per completion, and unsold value is yet to be recognised. Tower A delivered, Tower B has OC to 45th floor, Tower C launched with 17 floors built, Tower D unlaunched.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a bonus issue after amalgamation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot commit; policy has been bonus after a few years, and currently 97% of capital is bonus capital.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for premium office assets in South and Central Mumbai?
qa_highlights.answer: Samyag Shah said demand is very strong, supported by both institutional sales and leasing; Futurex inventory could last 12-15 months and a new commercial portfolio is planned.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg pipeline (GDV INR 840 crores+) is not yet launched beyond the ongoing project; launch timing relies on the next 12 months.
Amalgamation depends on NCLT approval; timing of hearing not specified.
About INR 250 crores of the INR 300 crore acquisition allocation remains unspent.

Collections in Q4 (INR 203 crores) were well below booking value (INR 156 crores) only in the sense of lower bookings; FY26 collections of INR 781 crores vs INR 576 crores presales should be tracked for sustainability.
Cost-to-complete of about INR 1,600 crores on launched inventory will need funding from the balance sheet.
Monte South Tower B completion and Tower D launch timing are key delivery milestones.

We try to balance our portfolio. So as soon as one commercial portfolio gets completed and sold, we try to add a new one.
That's very difficult to say right now. I mean Marathon has always had a policy of declaring bonus after a few years.

503101|2026-06.headline: Marathon Nextgen Q1 FY27 total income hit INR 217 crores, a multi-quarter high, with PAT of INR 52 crores and INR 900 crores of new redevelopment GDV added.
503101|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR 217 crores (multi-quarter high), EBITDA of INR 66 crores and PAT of INR 52 crores. Sales on the existing portfolio were 38,000 sq ft with booking value of INR 86 crores and collections of INR 118 crores (MNRL's 40% share of Monte South); including the merged portfolio, sales were 46,000 sq ft, booking value INR 108 crores and collections INR 146 crores. Two redevelopment projects (Versova and Sewri, INR 450 crores GDV each) were added, and the company says it is debt-free with about INR 200 crores of acquisition capital after a INR 900 crore QIP. The merger with group entities is awaiting NCLT shareholder and creditor meetings in early September 2026.

segments.name: Monte South (Byculla, JV, 40% stake)
segments.commentary: Sold ~35,000 sq ft with booking value INR 125 crores and collections INR 140 crores. Tower A has OC; Tower B has RCC to 65th floor and part OC to 45th floor, with balance OC expected this FY; Tower C RCC at 28th floor.

segments.name: Marathon Nexzone (Panvel)
segments.commentary: Sold 14,000 sq ft with booking value INR 17 crores and collections INR 43 crores. Full OC received for Cedar and Daffodil towers, enabling handovers.

segments.name: Bhandup (NeoPark, NeoSquare)
segments.commentary: Sales of 8,000 sq ft with booking value INR 14 crores and collections INR 9 crores. NeoSquare has OC; NeoValley and NeoPark under construction per schedule.

segments.name: Commercial (Futurex and Millennium)
segments.commentary: Futurex combined sales ~4,000 sq ft, booking INR 19 crores, collections INR 23 crores; Futurex has OC. Millennium sold over 1,000 sq ft, booking INR 3 crores, collections INR 1 crore; under construction.

segments.name: PTC (Permanent Transit Camp) vertical
segments.commentary: Started after Kanjurmarg land acquisition in Q4 FY26, focused on Bhandup; no presales yet, but management expects some in coming quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management said FY27 outlook is positive and better than last year, but declined to give forward numbers; bookings from newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases expected to show in coming quarters (booking recognised on registration).
Collections this year expected to be on the heavier side, supported by ready-to-move inventory (about 3-month TAT on sales at Futurex and Monte South) and percentage-completion receipts.
Surplus capital of about INR 200 crores expected to be fully deployed into new projects this FY27.
Target EBITDA margin of 30-35% for project acquisitions.

Merger: shareholder and creditor meetings planned for first week of September 2026, followed by a second NCLT hearing; completion timing uncertain, dependent on NCLT dates (management said it was not sure whether it would complete by December).
capex_capacity: Upcoming pipeline GDV: Monte South Commercial ~INR 3,400 crores; Monte South Residential Tower D ~INR 1,600 crores; Marathon Neo Series (Bhandup) ~INR 2,800 crores.
Existing portfolio estimated unsold GDV ~INR 8,000 crores.
Redevelopment additions: Versova (via subsidiary Sunset Spaces, ~1.5 acres, GDV >INR 450 crores, first society redevelopment) and Sewri (cluster redevelopment JDA, ~7,500 sq m, GDV ~INR 450 crores).
Merger to bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and ready inventory at Futurex into the listed entity.
Panvel-Karjat corridor deadline cited as December 2026; Monte South commercial to launch ~5 minutes from Futurex.
demand_pricing: Management cited strong demand at Monte South (footfalls up sharply), commercial space (limited Grade A supply near Futurex), and newly launched Bhandup and Panvel phases.
Ready-to-move inventory at Monte South Towers A and B is sold at a premium, per management.
Redevelopment selection: prime locations and strict financial metrics; management said it avoids high-premium deals that may get stuck.
PTC demand from neighbouring redevelopment projects in Bhandup; area serves western suburbs (around Malad, P-South ward), Mulund, Ghatkopar and parts of Chembur.

qa_highlights.question: What are the launch timelines for the INR 900 crore redevelopment GDV, and how much more can be added in 12-24 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two new projects (Sewri and Versova, INR 450 crores each) add INR 900 crores in the quarter; no launch timeline or further 12-24 month addition was quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 business outlook and which projects will drive acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers but said the outlook is positive and better than last year, citing Monte South, commercial, and new Bhandup and Panvel phases, with bookings flowing in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections trend over the next 2-3 quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ready-to-move sales at Futurex and Monte South convert to collections in about 3 months; Monte South Tower C is at the 28th slab, with about 40% collection on that basis. Collections expected to be heavier this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A Futurex investment-property floor was not sold in the quarter, so no rental/sale income was recognised from it.

qa_highlights.question: Will the amalgamation complete by December 2026 or slip into 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Shareholder and stakeholder meetings are planned for early September, followed by a second NCLT hearing; management said it is not sure of the timeline because NCLT benches are heavily loaded.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the redevelopment pipeline beyond INR 900 crores, and how are deals selected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Mumbai redevelopment opportunity is very large; selection focuses on prime locations and strict margin thresholds, and it avoids over-priced deals that can stall.

qa_highlights.question: How much capital will be deployed in FY27 and what return thresholds apply?
qa_highlights.answer: Target EBITDA margin 30-35% on acquisitions; about INR 200 crores of surplus capital to be fully deployed this FY.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PTC vertical's pipeline and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: PTC business started after the Q4 FY26 Kanjurmarg land acquisition; strong demand from neighbouring redevelopments; presales may start in next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst (Jain Securities) asked about FY27 margin drivers and the share of yarn consumed internally.
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher stretch-product sales (up about 30-40%) and internal use of value-added yarn. About 40% of yarn is consumed internally, and that share may rise.

qa_highlights.question: Individual investor asked whether double-digit revenue and margin growth is possible over the next 2-3 years.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on course for at least double-digit growth and an overall double-digit EBITDA margin. It flagged synthetic price increases of 25-30%, freight costs and power costs as headwinds, and aims to gain market share at better margins.

risks_watch: Raw-material pass-through lag: polyester up 25-30% and PTA/MEG higher; management expects pass-through only in H2.
Working capital and net debt: net debt INR515 crore, up INR43.28 crore in H1; inventory of slow-moving yarn and receivables still elevated.
Export freight and vessel availability are delaying customer lifts and yarn export orders.
Surat customs NOC and de-notification timing (Nov 2026 to Feb 2027) could push production start beyond April 2027.
Volume declines across yarn, fabric and garments in H1; fabric Simon brand expected increases did not materialise.
Power and employee costs are pressuring the cost base. Europe FTA timing (June-July 2027) is an assumption.

Q2 transcript had misstatements: EBITDA growth wording, and garment utilisation numbers for H1 and last year were swapped in the call, corrected in-call. Treat call figures as indicative until the presentation is checked.

503811|2026-03.headline: Siyaram Q4 FY26 total income rose 16.1% YoY to INR 871 crores, PAT up 30.6% to INR 95 crores; FY27 revenue growth guided at about 12%.
503811|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR 871 crores (up 16.1% YoY) with EBITDA of INR 152 crores (17.4% margin, up 21%) and PAT of INR 95 crores (up 30.6%). Full-year FY26 total income reached INR 2,653 crores (up 15.5%), EBITDA INR 413 crores (15.6% margin) and PAT INR 228 crores (up 14.8%). Management said demand improved gradually in Q4 on wedding and festive season, while input-cost volatility and geopolitics remain a concern. The company announced a special interim dividend of INR 4 and final dividend of INR 5 per share (INR 16 total for FY26), plus a small residential project at Dombivali. Store count reached 44 (27 ZECODE, 17 DEVO), with a target of about 70 by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 capex and store guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 100 crores capex: INR 50-60 crores maintenance plus about INR 40 crores for stores, taking the count to about 70 by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No change; management retained about 14% EBITDA margin guidance with 150 bps retail drag, subject to input price volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Retail FY26 revenue and margin drag?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue about INR 80 crores versus INR 70-80 crores estimate; EBITDA drag was within the 150 bps budget. FY27 drag again guided at about 1.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY26 store openings short of guidance (35 planned)?
qa_highlights.answer: Lean start-up team focused on operations; some sites were under-construction properties, delaying openings. FY27 target set more conservatively at about 70 total stores.

qa_highlights.question: Growth split between market share and channel inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth was largely market share gain, with favourable wedding season; fabric market grows only a small percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and debtors rise about 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Partly new stores (inventory held on books), partly build-up ahead of a strong Q4; inventory days stable at about 135-138. Operating cash flow about INR 150 crores, with large part absorbed by inventory and debtors.

qa_highlights.question: Other income composition for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest about INR 27 crores, profit on sale of assets about INR 21 crores, MTM gain about INR 12.73 crores, capital subsidy INR 5.31 crores. Remaining government grants about INR 5-6 crores pending.

qa_highlights.question: Residential project economics and revenue recognition?
qa_highlights.answer: Outlay about INR 45 crores over the 24-month project on owned land, revenue about INR 80 crores; revenue to be recognised on completion certificate as per standard.

503811|2026-06.headline: Siyaram Silk Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.4% to INR466 crores, EBITDA up 22.3% to INR40 crores at 8.6% margin, PAT INR11 crores.

EBITDA rose 22.3% to INR40 crores, margin 8.6%, and PAT more than doubled to INR11 crores (PAT margin 2.4%) on operating leverage. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ~12% revenue growth and ~14% EBITDA margin including retail, with a ~150 bps EBITDA drag from ZECODE and DEVO. Adhik Maas moderated wedding demand in the quarter, and Diwali is expected to be ~3 weeks later this year.

Retail drag on annual EBITDA margin guided at ~150 bps; management said it expects to be well within that budget. Stated as a ballpark, including all store costs (rent included per management).

Franchise model considered an option later but not pursued; company is using internal capital for stores.

qa_highlights.question: How are ZECODE store profitability and breakeven tracking amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said stores are ~18 months old and profitability is targeted in 1.5-2 years; some stores are EBITDA positive, including some under a year old, but it is too early to conclude.

qa_highlights.question: How much EBITDA loss does retail carry and is the 150 bps drop inclusive of rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ~150 bps annual EBITDA drop is a ballpark that includes all store operating costs and rent; it is not measured quarterly and the company will not disclose separate ZECODE/DEVO numbers yet.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Q1 margin improvement, excluding the INR24-25 crore land development cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land cost was moved from inventory to expenses, so the net effect is nil and EBITDA margins are unchanged; the quarter should not be modelled alone given seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the retail revenue outlook and what would trigger faster store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail revenue was ~INR30 crores in Q1 with FY27 at ~INR160 crores; management will accelerate expansion only after store maturity and scale in infrastructure and technology.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation expected to affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some pass-on was taken in Q1 with more possible if margins compress, and it reiterated the ~14% EBITDA margin guidance including the retail drag.

qa_highlights.question: Is other income one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said other income is mostly recurring (delayed payment interest, rent); management said about 30% is a mark-to-market gain that varies quarter to quarter.

503811|2026-09.headline: Siyaram Q2 FY27 total income rose 15.1% to Rs 827 crore, but PAT fell to Rs 75 crore from Rs 87 crore; revenue guidance raised to 14-15%.

504028|2026-03.headline: GEE Q4 FY26 turnover rose to INR112 crore and FY26 to about INR370 crore, with EBITDA margin near 9% and a 25-30% revenue CAGR target to FY29.

Q4 EBITDA was about INR33 crore at a 9% margin, and PAT about INR13 crore (3.5% margin). Management framed FY26 as a stabilisation year after the May 2025 promoter restructuring, and set targets of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY29-30, FY27 revenue above INR500 crore and EBITDA margin above 10%. Growth is tied to defence, power (nuclear, thermal, hydro), railways and exports, with flux-cored wire production slated to start in July 2026.

segments.commentary: Export share is under 10% of revenue, down from earlier years. Approvals were obtained from ADNOC (UAE) and a Saudi breakthrough, with NAKS approval from Russia in trial. 504028|2026-06.headline: GEE Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 30% YoY to INR 103 crores, with EBITDA margin up 204 bps to 7.8%.

Management set a North Star of INR 1,000 crores revenue by FY29-30, with 10-13% EBITDA margin ambitions, supported by a NPCIL approval, new SAW wire, SAW flux and flux cored wire lines, and a Thane land monetisation. 504132|2026-03.headline: Permanent Magnets Q4 standalone revenue rose 47% YoY to INR 66 crores; FY26 revenue INR 225 crores (+13%), with Relays ramp pushed to H2 FY27.

FY26 EBITDA margin was 17% versus 14% a year earlier, helped by product mix and second-half scale-up; Q4 margin was 15%, up YoY but down sequentially. The new Alloys furnace was installed in January and commercialised in Q4, while the Relays project slipped to commercial ramp from H2 FY27 and no rare-earth revenue was booked in FY26 due to Chinese export restrictions. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-30% with EBITDA margin of roughly 15-18%.

504380|2026-09.headline: Flomic's Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 37% YoY to INR156 crore and PAT turned to INR4.32 crore profit, driven largely by freight rate spikes.
504380|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR156 crore, up about 37% YoY, with EBITDA of INR16.94 crore (margin 10.88%, up roughly 300 bps) and PAT of INR4.32 crore against a loss of about INR1 crore a year earlier. H1 FY27 revenue was INR275.65 crore (up 28.15%), EBITDA INR28.14 crore (up about 80%) and PAT INR6.39 crore versus a loss of INR3.99 crore. Management attributed most of the growth to sharply higher freight rates on India-US and Latin American lanes, with volumes up about 6-7% in Q1. Warehousing expansion at Bhiwandi (vertical multi-tier and pallet racking) was completed in Q2 with customers already occupying the new space.

H2 FY27 priorities: scale warehousing to customer demand, strengthen project cargo and specialized logistics, deepen integrated services with existing customers, and use technology for efficiency.

capex_capacity: Bhiwandi multi-tier storage (ground plus three tiers) commissioned July 2026 and completed September 2026; adds 15,000 sq ft, lifting leasable area of the same footprint from 5,000 to 20,000 sq ft; purchased outright, not leased. Quick commerce customer occupying since September.

Long-span pallet racking (G plus five levels) installed September-October 2026, adding more than 2,000 pallet positions and taking the Bhiwandi warehouse to about 8,000 pallets; FMCG customer occupying since October.
Current overall space utilisation about 97.5%, per management.
Management said racking/shelving investments in existing sites pay back in two to three years; new warehouses are opened only with anchor customers in hand.
Network: 25 branches and more than 30 warehouses across India; new sales offices being considered based on manufacturing and import-export potential.
demand_pricing: Freight rates on India to US 40-foot containers rose from about $2,800 (end February/March) to about $9,600 (August/September), per management; rates doubled to tripled.
Growth in Q2 was described as largely driven by freight rate increases rather than volume; Q1 volume growth was about 6-7%.
Gross margin percentage is roughly constant on freight, so higher turnover lowers GP margin percentage while lifting absolute profit.
Repeat customers were 51% of FY26 business; top 15 customers were more than 20% of turnover. Over 5,000 active customers; more than 42,000 shipments in FY26.
Air freight: contractual space agreements with several carriers; export focus on US, South America and Africa.
Geopolitical disruption (Gulf) has lengthened lead and transit times, but cargo is still moving via alternate routings.

qa_highlights.question: Plans to expand the domestic branch network and location selection criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to opening new sales offices where potential exists; selection is based on manufacturing base and import-export potential of the region.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity and initiatives in air freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Air import and export are both being expanded with carriers on new airport capacity (including Navi Mumbai); export demand is strong, with contractual space agreements and profitability described as good, without figures.

qa_highlights.question: Business mix evolution over 3-5 years, particularly warehousing?
qa_highlights.answer: Warehousing expected to rise from 13-14% to 17-18% and then about 20% of revenue, with investment only where anchor customers exist.

qa_highlights.question: Warehouse strategy: utilisation of existing sites or new leased facilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 97.5%; further expansion will be made only if profitable, with racking in existing space paying back in two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: How are geopolitical issues and shipping disruptions affecting demand and volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the situation is unpredictable, but new routings are being found; lead and transit times have risen somewhat, though cargo is moving.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue growth came from freight rates versus volumes; what drove EBITDA growth of about 90%?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was largely freight-rate driven; costs are largely fixed for an asset-light model, so margin gains flow to EBITDA; new software and tight control on employment and other operating costs also helped; interest cost rose with working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Expected annualised revenue and profitability from the Bhiwandi expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR50 lakh a year from the 15,000 sq ft; about INR40-50 lakh from pallet positions once occupied; about INR1 crore total at full utilisation. No profitability figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Growth opportunity in specialised warehousing for e-commerce, quick commerce and FMCG; global partnerships?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialised warehousing is seen as a promising growth area; overseas presence is via the WCA network, and future global presence is planned mainly where the company controls cargo flows.

504614|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 44% to INR2,025 crores and PAT 58% to INR1,109 crores, with Q4 PAT up 53% YoY to INR155 crores.
504614|2026-03.overview: Management reported record FY26 thermal (4,155 MU ex-captive, +84% YoY) and hydro (661 MU, +31%) generation, with the energy segment contributing about two-thirds of EBITDA. Consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR5,928 crores, and net debt fell to INR215 crores from INR1,566 crores. Q4 was dented by a 30 MW captive unit shutdown, a 300 MW turbine maintenance outage in January, seasonal hydro slowdown and the coal mine hitting its 1.8 MTPA approved limit. Management outlined a doubling of energy capacity to 1,200 MW by FY30 after the Supreme Court dismissed appeals on the SKS Power acquisition, plus a Raipur pellet expansion to 2 MTPA.

segments.name: Thermal power (ex captive)
segments.commentary: Generation reached a record 4,155 MU in FY26 versus 2,238 MU in FY25 (+84%), helped by SKS Power integration. Around 400 crore sellable units are guided for FY27 versus about 375 crore units sold in FY26; FY26 realisation was above INR5/unit.

segments.name: Hydropower
segments.commentary: Generation hit a record 661 MU in FY26 versus 508 MU in FY25 (+31%), helped by the 25 MW Rehar project. Management said the hydro segment EBITDA was about INR386 crores, and that two hydro projects have long-term PPAs.

segments.name: Steel, sponge iron and pellets
segments.commentary: Iron ore pellet output hit a record 826,293 MT and sponge iron 345,066 MT in FY26; HB wire record 40,425 MT. Steel realisation improved YoY and QoQ in Q4 but FY26 averaged below FY25.

segments.name: Coal mining (Gare Palma IV/7)
segments.commentary: FY26 output hit the 1.8 MTPA permissible limit after CECB consent for expansion from 1.68 MTPA; Q4 volumes were lower as the annual cap was exhausted. Domestic coal sales were about 150k MT, as most output is captively consumed.

guidance_outlook: SKS Power capacity to double to 1,200 MW by FY30; management now says commissioning is around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being sought after the earlier one expired.
Acquisition of a majority stake in Adishankar Khuitam Power (66 MW, Arunachal Pradesh) approved; DPR being finalised, with the project expected to start by end-2026 and take 3-4 years.
Three small Chhattisgarh hydro projects (74 MW in total) may take 3-4 years to commission.
50 MW captive solar expected by end of Q1 FY27 (about September per later remarks); 30 MW TG set replacement to be back by end-June 2026.
Shahpur West high-grade coal mine targeted for commissioning before end-FY27; full-year operations expected in FY28.
Raipur pellet plant expansion from 0.9 to 2.0 MTPA, capex about INR500 crores, completion within 2.5 years; EC in place and DPR under preparation.

Annual hydro capex of about INR500-700 crores; the 600 MW IPP expansion to bring 'full blast' capex from next year, which will be substantially higher. Management did not give an investment figure for SKS expansion yet.
Management is evaluating separation of the renewable energy business (not the full power business); no conclusion yet.
Capex of about INR150 crores over the next two years at the Binjkot plant to improve PLF.
capex_capacity: Gare Palma IV/7 coal mine expansion to 1.8 MTPA with CECB consent; approvals for Gare Palma IV/5, Bartunga and Senduri coal mines progressing.
Binjkot (SKS) plant: over INR140 crores capex invested to date, with about INR150 crores more planned over the next two years to lift PLF.
Raipur pellet plant: 9 lakh tons to 20 lakh tons; about INR500 crores capex; 2.5-year build.
Mineral wool project installed to use industrial waste; management expects it to add to bottom line as it ramps up.
FY27 earnings drivers named: full-year Rehar hydro, efficiency gains at the IPP, 50 MW solar and the 30 MW TG set; FY28 driver is full-year Shahpur coal mine.
demand_pricing: Power exchange prices averaged INR3.75/unit in Q4 FY26, versus INR4.30 a year earlier and INR3.33 in Q3. Peak demand hit a record 270.8 GW.
Indian coal index rose 8% from March 2025 and 9% from December 2025 levels, due to import disruption from the West Asia conflict.

Steel prices recovered by about 10-15% in Q4 FY26 after reaching multi-year lows. Management expects long-product prices to rise once the conflict settles, but would not give Q1 FY27 realisation guidance.
Management said NMDC and OMC have cut iron ore prices, so end-product prices may fall.
India crude steel output grew over 11% in FY26; steel consumption about 164 million tonnes. Safeguard duties have reduced Chinese imports.

About 300 MW of the 600 MW IPP capacity is under PPA (medium/long term), with about 200 MW under PPA this year, rising to 300 MW next year. Management said PPA prices give more visibility than the volatile spot market.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the company restarting steel/pellet capex after holding back for a long time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited environment clearance and land/water already in place, and expected many Chhattisgarh iron ore mines to open within 2-2.5 years. The Raipur pellet expansion is designed to be ready when they do.

qa_highlights.question: Is there room to improve IPP efficiency and EBITDA per unit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is scope to improve PLF at Binjkot, with about INR150 crores of capex planned over two years and spares and pending capex being completed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company demerge steel and power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only the renewable energy business is being examined for separation, with no conclusion yet; the full power business is not part of it.

qa_highlights.question: When will the SKS 600 MW doubling be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commissioning is now expected around 2030-31 because fresh environment clearance is being obtained, as the earlier clearance had expired. Capex amount will be given after configuration is frozen.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-FY28 capex and growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Annual hydro capex is about INR500-700 crores, with the 600 MW expansion adding substantially higher capex from next year. FY27 growth comes from efficiency, full-year Rehar, the IPP, solar and TG set; FY28 from full-year Shahpur mine.

qa_highlights.question: What were FY26 sellable units and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Previous-year sellable units were about 375 crore units and FY27 is guided to about 400 crore units. Average realisation was more than INR5 per unit.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Godawari Power shares bought in the open market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it normal treasury operations with no specific plans. Liquidity is about INR2,400 crores and the stake was about 1% of that.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: the outcome affects steel, ferro alloy and coal prices, and demand. Management said a renewed war could weaken demand.
Timelines are slipping: SKS doubling is now 2030-31 and the 3 small hydro projects may take 3-4 years. The Chhattisgarh 74 MW and 66 MW Khuitam projects are at DPR and approval stages.
Coal mine output is capped at 1.8 MTPA, so Q4 showed weaker volumes; approvals for other mines are still pending.
Management did not disclose cost of generation or Q1 FY27 steel realisations, and did not give a capex figure for the SKS expansion yet.
Q4 disclosures were inconsistent on the domestic coal sales figure (150k MT) and on EBITDA definitions for the hydro segment.
