504614|2026-06.headline: Sarda Energy Q1 FY27 total income INR 1,717 cr, EBITDA INR 762 cr and PAT INR 478 cr (+9.4% YoY), helped by a one-time INR 110 cr net benefit.
504614|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly EBITDA and PAT despite planned shutdowns, unplanned outages and weak small-hydro generation from delayed monsoon. Net profit included a one-time net benefit of INR 110 cr from regulatory approval of the final project cost of the 113 MW Sikkim hydro plant, which management said was worth about INR 162.6 cr of revenue and INR 18 cr of interest income. Energy contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA, and the company said it is now net debt-free with liquidity above INR 2,500 cr as of 30 June 2026. Metals volumes fell QoQ because of captive power and furnace shutdowns at Raipur, Vizag and Siltara. Management declined to give numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Energy (IPP and captive power)
segments.commentary: Contributed nearly 70% of consolidated EBITDA. Medium and long-term PPAs cover over 380 MW of 710 MW saleable capacity; about 330 MW of these are at SKS, at INR 5-6/unit. Small hydro output was hit by the delayed monsoon, and the company said it is roughly 1% below last year.

segments.name: Sikkim 113 MW hydro
segments.commentary: Shut from 18 June to 5 July 2026 after a transmission tower collapsed in heavy rain and landslide. Management said it is now running at full capacity, with about 5 days of July generation lost and the restoration cost covered by insurance apart from a minimal excess.

segments.name: Steel and ferro alloys (metals)
segments.commentary: Consolidated revenue fell QoQ on planned outages: a 30 MW captive unit replacement at Raipur (trial run now, commercial operation expected mid-August), a 23-day Vizag captive shutdown, and a 53-day Siltara ferro alloy furnace refurbishment. Steel prices were range-bound with a mild negative bias; ferro alloy prices improved modestly.

segments.name: Mineral wool (new)
segments.commentary: Running at about 60-65% of capacity, with production constrained by imported equipment held up by the West Asia crisis. Management said the project is not yet profitable, and it expects FY27 revenue of INR 90-110 cr.

segments.name: Mining (coal)
segments.commentary: Shahpur West is due to commission before end-FY27 (0.6 Mt). Bartunga Hill (2.1 Mt) is due by end-FY28. Gare Palma IV/5 (2.0 Mt), Gare Palma IV/7 (1.8 Mt) and Senduri (0.6 Mt, provisional) make up the mining plan; the target is 7.1 Mt capacity.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 PAT or EBITDA guidance; management said the company does not give forward profitability figures and that the market is volatile.
Q2 expected to be better than Q1, driven by hydro generation and higher power prices. July IEX prices were about INR 5/unit versus INR 4.19-4.20 a year earlier.
FY27 IPP generation expected to exceed last year's 415 crore units, with the captive plant utilisation also improving after the 30 MW unit restarts.
Steel and ferro alloy prices expected to remain stable. Ferro alloy margins may firm as raw material prices soften; steel may rise after a West Asia settlement and after monsoon.
Real power tariffs expected at INR 5-6/unit for the year, rising with inflation and peak demand, especially for hydro.

Full-year FY27 pipeline: 50 MW captive solar expected by end of next quarter (after a railway right-of-way delay); 74 MW Chhattisgarh small hydro approvals on schedule; Arunachal 66 MW hydro detailed engineering to begin this year.

SKS 600 MW to 1,200 MW expansion: TOR submission in about 3 months, then public hearing and 6-8 months for EC, then 6-8 months to appoint a consultant. The new unit is targeted for FY31 completion (per management, asked on the last call).
capex_capacity: SKS thermal expansion from 600 MW to 1,200 MW is awaiting regulatory approval, and the company describes the brownfield project as capital-efficient, using existing land, water and evacuation infrastructure.
Waste heat recovery power plant at Vizag, about INR 300 cr, for energy efficiency; all expansion projects funded through internal accruals.

Coal mining: Shahpur West commissioning before end-FY27; Bartunga Hill by end of next financial year; Gare Palma IV/5, IV/7 and Senduri approvals in progress. Management said the Gare Palma IV/7 expansion from 1.8 Mt to 5 Mt is not in the immediate plan as new higher-grade mines take priority.
Shahpur West coal is high grade and is destined for sponge iron and ferro alloy plants, not the power plants.
Plans to quadruple mining capacity and double energy generation capacity, per management.
demand_pricing: India power generation grew 9.4% YoY to about 523 BU in the quarter; thermal grew 7.5%; solar generation rose about 45%; small hydro fell about 30% and large hydro about 7%.

504973|2026-03.headline: Chola MS FY26 combined ratio rose to 115.2% (112.2% ex-1/n) on motor claims and crop loss; PBT Rs454 crore, ROE 10.4%.

The FY26 claims ratio rose about 2.71 percentage points, driven by motor OD claims and a stepped-up motor third-party reserve, pushing the combined ratio to 115.2%. FY26 PBT was Rs454 crore after labour-code gratuity provisioning, and ROE was 10.4% against a 3-year average peak of about 14.4%. Management will seek forbearance to move statutory accounting to Ind AS from April 1, 2027, and Rajive Kumaraswami takes over as MD from June 1.

504973|2026-06.headline: Chola MS Q1 FY27 combined ratio rose to 120.4% with GWP up 6.7% to Rs 2,130 crore and motor OD loss ratio still elevated.
504973|2026-06.overview: Chola MS (general insurance arm of Cholamandalam Financial Holdings) reported GDPI of Rs 1,860 crore (+2.6% YoY) and GWP of Rs 2,130 crore (+6.7%), below management's expectations. Claims ratio rose to 85.6% (vs 81.3%) and combined ratio to 120.4%, driven by motor reserve strengthening, elevated motor OD claims and a large fire loss (Rs 12.4 crore net). Profit before tax was Rs 116 crore on operating profit of Rs 71 crore. Management said the OD loss ratio is unacceptable and targets a high-70s level first, while the Supreme Court motor TP (homemaker) judgment remains unprovided pending review.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Largest line (~70% of book per management); portfolio grew ~5.7% in Q1, mainly commercial vehicles. Mix: private cars 48%, two-wheelers ~9.5%, commercial vehicles ~42.5%. Motor combined ratio 128% in FY26 vs 123% in FY25; OD loss ratio now 80-86% range per analyst framing, not disputed by management.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: Portfolio declined 8.6% in Q1 vs industry fire decline of ~28%; Chola MS fire decline limited to 15.5%. Growth in marine, engineering and liability.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Growth moderate; decline driven by pricing corrections in PSU bank group platform and migration of business to retail platform. Claims settled within 30 days for 99%; NPS 73. Health is being rebuilt from the ground up.

guidance_outlook: OD loss ratio near-term target: bring it to high-70s, then progressively to mid-70s; management said it expects below 80% over time, with a couple of quarters needed for measures to show results.

Corrective measures across motor (new vs renewal mix, NCB focus, ACS control, repair vs replacement analysis) and health (product redesign, pricing revisions, SME push) expected to become visible over coming quarters.
Expects greater property pricing discipline after June NATCAT events; reinsurance market correction more likely at next renewal cycle.
Ind AS / IFRS transition effective April 1, 2027 (one-year IRDAI forbearance granted); no profitability impact estimate yet, preliminary observations possibly next quarter.
Industry CAT loss estimate of Rs 3,000-4,000 crore from multiple events in Gujarat, Assam, Jamshedpur and Maharashtra.
capex_capacity: Reinsurance capacity for fire and engineering secured at start of FY27, described as comparable to leading private players.
Motor issuance platform rolled out across bank channel; workflow enhancements under way in motor claims.
Health network exceeds 13,000 hospitals via PSU bank retail health partnerships.
Readiness work ongoing for Ind AS, Risk-Based Capital (RBC) framework and DPDP requirements.
demand_pricing: Industry GI premium growth ~8.3% in Q1 vs 8.9% a year earlier; motor and health led growth, fire under severe pricing pressure.
Industry combined ratio ~117.8% in FY26 vs 112.6% FY25; Chola MS 115.2% FY26 vs 110% FY25.
Motor TP is tariff-based; premiums do not keep pace with claims inflation and court award trends.
Inward reinsurance growth cited as a driver of GWP outpacing GDPI; sources are commercial-lines participation and group health.
GIFT City reinsurers cited as contributing to soft commercial-lines pricing; management expects limited sustainable lead-line capacity from them.

qa_highlights.question: Has any additional motor TP provision been made for the Supreme Court homemaker judgment, and what is the path for motor OD loss ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision taken in Q1 for the Supreme Court judgment; review petition pending. OD loss ratio not accepted as the new normal; immediate target is high-70s, then mid-70s over time. Management said the 84.4% motor figure cited by analyst was not confirmed in the call, and said OD loss ratio below 80% is achievable over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did retail and group health decline when the industry is growing strongly?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health decline reflects virtually no gross-subsidy business left, standalone accounts required to be individually profitable, and PSU bank group platform pricing corrections with migration to retail platform. Focus shifts to multinational single-mandate clients, SME and GPA cross-sell.

qa_highlights.question: Is the claims ratio rise from new book or from reserve provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase reflects claims inflation assumptions in reserving (expected ULR), not pure reserve strengthening; motor TP is tariff-based so pricing lags claims cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor two-wheeler reduced and how does the Supreme Court ruling affect claims?
qa_highlights.answer: Two-wheeler reduction was deliberate given profitability; courts have not uniformly applied the Rs 30,000 threshold and evaluate cases individually. Solvency impact of an adverse outcome not quantified; reserves said to include margin for adverse deviation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IFRS/Ind AS profitability and ROE impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Implementation effective April 1, 2027 after one-year forbearance; no reliable estimate yet, special-purpose financial statements not yet filed with IRDAI. Preliminary observations possibly next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is inward reinsurance growth sustainable and what is the CAT and reinsurance renewal outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inward reinsurance comes from commercial lines participation and selective group health; sustainable only as underwriting appetite allows. Hours-clause structure means separate deductibles per event, so P&L impact could be larger, supporting pricing discipline; reinsurance softness more visible at next renewal.

505010|2026-03.headline: Automotive Axles Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 18% QoQ to INR6,643 million, with PAT margin steady at 8%; FY26 revenue INR21,777 million (+5%).
505010|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR6,643 million, up about 18% QoQ and 18.5-18.7% YoY, with EBITDA of INR825 million (12.4%) and PAT of INR539 million (8%), matching Q4 FY25's PAT margin. Management said the industry's 7.5T+ CV market closed FY26 at about 480,000 units (+16%), and that the company operates at 70-80% of capacity in soft months after about 90% in Q4. Management said Phase 1 and 1A capacity will be complete by end-December 2026, with a next capex phase to be defined over the next 6-12 months.

505010|2026-06.headline: Automotive Axles Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 13.6% (from 12.4% QoQ) on revenue of Rs 5,168 mn and PAT of Rs 455 mn.
505010|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 5,168 million, EBITDA of Rs 702 million (about 13.6%), and profit for the year of Rs 455 million (about 8.7%, EPS about Rs 30). Management described EBITDA as one of the highest margins the company has achieved, helped by mix, a one-off, and lower employee costs versus the high-volume Q4. Management now sees the FY27 M&HCV industry down 5-10% versus last year, against an earlier 15-20% decline assumption, with Q4 expected to be a peak quarter. Capacity expansion (Phase-1 and Phase-1(a)) is about 40% complete.

segments.commentary: Management says demand is driven by replacement cycle and the shift from 6x2 to 10x2 or 4x2 tractor-trailers; heavy-duty (40 t and above) is the core focus. Overlap with American Axle described as minimal.

segments.name: Exports (to Meritor/CDBS global plants)
segments.commentary: Exports were about 13% of the quarter's revenue, versus a traditional 8-12% range; management guides to 8-12% for the year, with sea freight the main logistics challenge.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Defence contributes about 5-10% of revenue depending on tender timing; long gestation of 3-10 years from RFQ to SOP.

segments.name: Bus axles and new products
segments.commentary: Low-floor bus axle launch is still in validation, and is being reworked for upcoming pass-by noise norms. A 160 tandem axle is entering production with a large customer.

Management guides to a steady-state PAT margin of 7.5-8.5% for the coming quarters and frames it as an overall band.
Capacity additions of roughly 25-30% are planned to cover the next two to three years of market growth, with Phase-1 and Phase-1(a) about 40% complete.
Management says it will not give specific volume guidance but expects better conversion and margins if volumes exceed the prior year.

Management says capacity must also be matched by supply chain readiness.

Management says the delayed monsoon is supporting freight and replacement demand.
Management says share of business with Ashok Leyland was maintained; the company confirmed it is a single source for some new products, with dual sourcing common at OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: How are exports and OEM opportunities split between Automotive Axles and American Axle (Bharat Forge)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two are competitors, that it cannot comment on the competitor's plans, and that exports go mainly to CDBS global entities.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company lost market share at Ashok Leyland?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a loss of share; the gap reflects product mix and seasonal/segment shifts. Confirmed Ashok Leyland share was maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How was the cost of steel and gas handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel and other commodities are passed through fully. Conversion cost increases were absorbed in Q1 with recovery from customers being negotiated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revised industry outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry down 5-10% versus the earlier 15-20%; best case is flat with last year, Q4 a peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the regulatory outlook for bus axles and new product launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Bus axle product launch is in validation and is being reworked for pass-by noise regulations; a 160 tandem axle is entering production.

505160|2026-03.headline: Talbros Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR241 crore with record 18.7% EBITDA margin; FY27 guided to 15-20% growth.

Forging equipment is in place; manpower and leadership issues reportedly resolved, with new CEO Ashish (appointed April 1) spending about 50% of time on forging.
Stellantis programme in the chassis division started production in Q1 FY27 after about 2 years of design changes and start of production.
Plastic EV components for JLR at about INR25 crores in orders, maturing from next financial year; JLR EV rubber components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. with supply from Q1/Q2 CY27.
Possible chassis plant in Gujarat under discussion with Tata Motors (management to meet Tata Motors chief within 90 days).
demand_pricing: Industry context: PV sales about 1.27 million units (+26% YoY), 2-wheelers 5.63 million units (+~20%), CV about 2.83 lakh units (+15%), EV PV volumes +87%, EV 2W about +68%.
Data centres: about 5% of gasket revenue today; estimated INR30-40 crores annual potential, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years; Cummins sales of INR25 crores in Q1 vs INR90 crores last year.
Management said 7 OEMs are looking to shift supply chains from China to India; BMW giving more business, Volvo a potential new gasket customer, and Stellantis opened for Marelli.
Cummins America expected to contribute INR30-40 crores by FY27-28 (wire harness, aftermarket and data-centre gaskets).
Forging orders: about INR500 crores over 5 years (about INR100 crores p.a.) cited; Marelli and Dana/Carraro orders maturing in Q3-Q4.
Gasket pricing: management said data-centre gaskets are the same product as regular gaskets, with pricing unchanged; margins not separately disclosed.
Management stated pricing pass-through of input costs from OEMs is expected in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How far along are the ~7 OEMs looking to shift supply chains from China to India, and what is the status of new Stellantis and Kia projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European customers are weak; BMW is giving more business, Volvo is a potential new gasket customer, and Marelli has opened doors with Stellantis. JLR is a new plastic EV component customer, Cummins America is a slow starter expected to yield INR30-40 crores by FY27-28, and a Gujarat chassis plant is being discussed with Tata Motors (meeting within 90 days).

qa_highlights.question: Any progress on the stake transaction in Marelli?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no firm update yet; they are in court proceedings and expect a clearer picture by end-September, with details to be discussed offline.

qa_highlights.question: What share of gasket revenue comes from data centres, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About 5% of gasket revenue today. Cummins sales were INR25 crores in Q1 versus INR90 crores last year; data-centre business is estimated at INR30-40 crores a year, rising toward INR100 crores in 2-3 years. Talbros is single source to Cummins for the engine component.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth expectations for gaskets and forging, and the longer-term potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Gasket growth expected around 17% in FY27 (about INR680-700 crores). Forging Q1 was up 4%; Q2 expected at double-digit growth and FY27 forging growth of 15-20% to about INR340-350 crores. Longer term, gaskets INR850-900 crores and forging INR600-700 crores within 3-4 years, with management referencing FY30.

qa_highlights.question: Why did forging Q1 growth lag and why has the forging guidance come down from earlier expectations of around INR400 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 hit by manpower shortages, LPG price spikes, lower BMW and GKN schedules and some orders taking time to move into execution; productivity dipped. Loss of Meritor business (INR30-40 crores p.a.) due to US tariffs is a key reason. Management said July was better than June and cited a INR500 crores, 5-year order book (about INR100 crores p.a.).

qa_highlights.question: Why did Marelli margins fall in Q1, and which segment will grow fastest in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower other income plus new manpower and shared rental costs; management expects margins to recover by year-end. Marelli is expected to grow 30-40% in FY27, forging about 20%, gaskets about 16-17%, and Talbros Marugo 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Is data-centre gasket margin different from the rest of the gasket business, and what is the EV revenue mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Same gasket product sold for a new application, with pricing unchanged; margins not split out. EV-related supply was INR12.5 crores in Q1 (about 3.27% of sales) versus INR10 crores in Q4 FY26 and INR9 crores a year ago; management targets around 5% in 2 years and a minimum of 5% over 5 years. JLR rubber EV components worth INR15-20 crores p.a. start in Q1/Q2 CY27.

risks_watch: Pass-through of steel, aluminium and labour inflation from OEMs has not yet happened; FY27 margin guide of about 17-17.5% depends on it.

Export share at about 25% against a 35% FY28 target; EV share at 3.27% of sales against a 5% goal.
key_quotes: Talbros has delivered yet another record quarter, achieving its highest ever quarterly revenue and surpassing the previous high recorded in quarter 4 of '26.
But we are very positive that we will get these increases from the OEMs in the coming quarters.

Plus, we are supplying bushes to BMW of EV vehicles, where sale has gone up a little bit there.

505192|2026-03.headline: SML Mahindra FY26 revenue rose 18% and PAT 31%, but Q4 PAT grew only 2% on a 16% revenue rise as commodity inflation hit.
505192|2026-03.overview: This was the first investor call since Mahindra's 58.96% controlling acquisition completed on 1 August 2025, about eight months post-takeover. Management said FY26 volumes grew 28% in cargo and 12% in passenger vehicles, with market share up 20 bps in cargo and 80 bps in passenger for the full year. Q4 showed a cargo share dip, which management attributed to pre-poned institutional orders executed in Q3, while bus share gained 170 bps in the quarter. Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost (roughly 3.5-3.7% annualised), and a price increase of about 2-3% was taken from 15 April 2026.

financial_highlights.change: up two notches from AA minus

segments.name: Cargo (trucks)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 28% with market share up 20 bps for the year; Q4 cargo share declined, attributed by management to Q3 pre-ponement of institutional orders. Q4 cargo volume grew 10%.

segments.name: Passenger (buses)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume up 12% with market share up 80 bps; Q4 bus share gained 170 bps in the peak school-bus season. Q4 passenger volume grew 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management aspires to a top-three position in India's ILCV trucks and buses segment, with focus on HCVs, and targets 10-12% combined market share by FY31 (currently about 6%).
Around FY31, the company targets about Rs 15,000 crore revenue, per the Global Investor Day, against a 3.5-tonne-plus revenue pool of about Rs 1.25 lakh crore last year.
Q1 FY27 plans are largely unchanged from original plans as of the call; management said a diesel price increase is the key swing factor.

Commodity inflation is expected to be partly temporary; management said price increases and commodity hedges should largely cover headwinds, and inflation is not expected to persist through FY27 if the Middle East situation eases.
First EV bus is to be launched in FY27; management gave no capex or volume figures for it.
A longer-format strategy session is planned for July 2026, close to the AGM.
capex_capacity: Service network: combined touchpoints to rise from about 300 to 450 by pooling 150 service setups across both brands; 70 are operational and 80 more are due by end of Q1 FY27.

Engineering and manufacturing synergies are being pursued to reduce product cost and capex outlay, including sharing engine (4-valve diesel and CNG 3.8-litre) and ADAS development with Mahindra teams.
ADAS regulation compliance (due in about 1.5 years) is a joint project with Mahindra, with cost detail deferred to launch.
EV bus development is underway; management said capex for scale-up will depend on market evolution.
demand_pricing: Industry grew about 2% in H1 FY26 and about 22% in H2 post-GST reform; ICV trucks +42%, LCV trucks +20%, MCV trucks +28%, ILCV +8% in that period.
Management sees no demand deferment yet and cites pent-up replacement demand, though a diesel price hike and Middle East disruption could moderate demand.
Q4 commodity inflation was about 1.3% of cost; Q1 FY27 saw further increases in some commodities (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases), with some volatility.
Price increases of about 2% (some 3%) on SML products effective 15 April 2026; more may follow based on analysis.
Electric bus industry share is below 1% of the segment; private buyers are not yet buying e-buses beyond STU purchases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook, market share trajectory and synergy timing?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry shifted from about 2% growth in H1 to about 22% in H2. Management said synergies come on both the back end (sourcing, engineering, manufacturing) and the front end (common dealers in unrepresented territories), with growth as the main thesis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan to merge the two companies or delist SML?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no delisting plan. On a merger, it is working on long-term strategy and will update at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: What are the supply chain and cost impacts of the current crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: No vehicle production was lost through Q4 despite gas, aluminium and polymer shortages. Steel, aluminium, copper and polymers rose, and gases trade at a premium; management expects most increases to be temporary.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ADAS cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called ADAS a significant development and said cost and detail would be shared at launch.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any demand deferment seen in March or April?
qa_highlights.answer: No deferment as of now; peak school-bus season is underway and Q1 plans are largely as originally planned, but management flagged diesel price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What was the Q4 margin headwind and what pricing offset is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 inflation was about 1.3% of cost (about 3.5-3.7% annualised). Price increases of about 2-3% began 15 April, and hedges will provide a partial offset, though steel cannot be hedged. Management said pricing should largely cover headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EV bus and e-mobility strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The first EV bus launches in FY27 with product details to follow closer to launch. Capex scale-up will depend on market evolution, as private buyers are not yet buying e-buses.

risks_watch: Diesel price increase and Middle East disruption could moderate CV demand after Q1 FY27.
Commodity inflation (steel, aluminium, copper, polymers, gases) may persist; hedges do not cover steel, and pricing actions may lag.
Q4 PAT growth of 2% vs revenue growth of 16% indicates margin pressure that must be tracked in Q1 FY27.
Cargo market share dip in Q4 FY26 tied to order timing; watch whether share recovers in FY27.
Integration delivery: service network expansion to 450 touchpoints and cross-badging, plus dealer-channel sensitivity.
Timing and scope of the July 2026 strategy session and merger-related updates.

505196|2026-06.headline: TIL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 86% YoY to INR117.1 crore, with EBITDA margin at 6.2% (vs 1.5%) and PAT at negative INR5.5 crore.
505196|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue of INR117.1 crore included Tulip Compression (TCPL) only from 8 May to 30 June 2026, so the quarter is a partial-period read. Standalone revenue grew 25% YoY to INR78.6 crore, with EBITDA up to INR3.4 crore (4.3% margin vs 1.5%), but standalone PAT was negative INR7.2 crore. Management flagged that blended margins will stay volatile for the next six to eight quarters because of product mix and supply-chain localisation, and gave no near-term margin guidance. The company delivered nine ReachStackers and reported a current order book of INR211 crore against a pipeline of about INR373 crore.

segments.commentary: FY26 aftermarket about INR56 crore. Management's long-term aim is 40-45% of revenue; parts margins 25-35%, service margins slightly better.

qa_highlights.question: Can the current order book deliver more than INR200 crore this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm the figure. It said the order book is exhausted over about nine months and new orders will add to it, and expects a significant jump in turnover.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall from Q4 to Q1, and what is the margin outlook?

qa_highlights.question: Tulip's business, revenue, margin, and plans to raise stake.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 14-15% medium-to-long-term EBITDA margin, equity infusion up to INR50 crore, and a 74% stake target over a few years. Export to Nigeria has just begun.

qa_highlights.answer: Debtors rose at end-FY26 due to a large IAF missile crane order in late March. Target is 60-75 days; TIL is now an MSME, which should speed customer payments.

qa_highlights.question: Chinese competition and pricing.

Q4 price increase of 1.75% in April; Q4 margin pressure of 90 bps from costs, with 70 bps blended price increase taken in January and 20 bps offset by cost reduction and mix.

Mid-size bike CAGR and inquiry momentum cited; no quantified category growth number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 retail outlook for the mid-size motorcycle category, and what are the expansion plans given thin dealer inventories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 industry sales were 1.11 million, up 23%, with no structural demand correction; bookings are 7-8 days, temporary supply issues are expected to clear in a week to 10 days, and capacity is going to 1.6 million units by June-July with the Cheyyar expansion by Q2 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is being passed on through pricing, and how much is being offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 50% of the 3-3.5% material cost headwind is recovered through the 1.75% April price increase, with the remaining 50% addressed through austerity measures and engineering savings; the Q4 margin hit was 90 bps, of which 70 bps was recovered in January pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Volvo financing JV see profit benefits and will it be a capital-hungry business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the JV will run independently with its own risk profile and that EML will invest up to INR750 crore for 50%; the target has INR1,806 crore AUM; management expects to grow AUM to INR9,000-10,000 crore over 5 years with no hurry to scale.

qa_highlights.question: What are the product pipeline and timelines, including the Bullet 650 and any plans below 350cc?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the project timelines shown at EICMA are on track; the Bullet 650 dispatch has started and the S6 was shown; the company focuses on 250-750cc, with platforms at 350cc, 450cc and 650cc.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the Andhra Pradesh greenfield plant and its capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the land MoU was signed this week, with the 261-acre parcel to be acquired; a plant is typically 24-30 months from land to full operation; no greenfield capacity timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MHCV outlook and how are fuel price hikes and labour shortages affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: VECV management said it took about 2% price increases from 1 April, with pass-through lagging due to time-bound transporter contracts; labour and LPG disruptions lasted 2-3 weeks and supply is improving.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: 3-3.5% material cost headwind in Q1 FY27 from the geopolitical situation, with only 50% expected to be recovered through pricing; watch Q1 gross margin.
Supply chain: elections, LPG availability, power issues and migrant labour movement disrupted production and deliveries in April-May; management expects normalisation within 1-2 weeks.
Fuel price hikes may hit transporter economics and the CV secondary market; VECV's pass-through is lagged by time-bound contracts.
Europe continued to degrow due to pre-registration effects of OBD2B, delaying billing; US tariff matters described as settled but still a drag.
Volvo financing JV: capital commitment of up to INR750 crore and dependence on a new business with a longer-term payoff.
Greenfield Andhra Pradesh plant: no timeline given beyond the 24-30 month window; the Cheyyar 2 million capacity target is set for Q2 FY28.
Replacement cycle yet to kick in; the digital platform's traction is slightly better but from a low base.
Q1 FY27 volume tracking to 1.6 million capacity by June-July; watch whether the capacity ramp meets festive-season demand.

505200|2026-06.headline: Eicher Motors Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 6,632 crore with record Royal Enfield volumes of 332,940 units.
505200|2026-06.overview: Eicher Motors posted its best-ever Q1 with consolidated revenue of INR 6,632 crore (up 32% YoY), EBITDA of INR 1,591 crore and PAT of INR 1,463 crore (up 21%). Royal Enfield sold a record 332,940 motorcycles (up from 261,326), and VECV recorded its highest-ever Q1 sales of 24,815 units (up 14.8%). Management flagged a tight dealer inventory of 10-12 days ahead of festive season, with capacity ramp-up at Cheyyar and a greenfield Tada (Andhra Pradesh) plant approved. Commodity inflation of 4-4.5% of costs was partly offset by price hikes and value engineering, and softening was noted.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 1,203 crore in Q1 FY26 (highest ever)
+21% YoY from INR 1,205 crore; prior year included INR 168 crore share of VECV profit
vs INR 511 crore YoY; margin 8.4% vs 9.2%
1.2% price hikes, 1% international mix, 0.4% currency, 0.6% allied business; offset by lower value

financial_highlights.value: Above INR 1,000 crore, about 15.3% of revenue

financial_highlights.change: INR 30 crore timing (Q4 ad campaign and launches) plus INR 22 crore marketing control

segments.name: Royal Enfield (India)
segments.commentary: 301,174 motorcycles sold in India; management cites about 32% volume growth and 350cc models (Classic, Bullet, Hunter, Meteor) up about 34% YoY. 450cc and 650cc models are back to pre-GST price levels, with Guerrilla 450 at about 2,400-2,500 units per month and 650cc twins at about 4,000-4,200 per month.

segments.name: Royal Enfield (International)
segments.commentary: Global volume 31,766 motorcycles; Brazil is the largest overseas market (about every fourth exported motorcycle), with a planned CKD facility. Europe remains in a market adjustment phase; US shows early green shoots after a tariff cut.

segments.name: Flying Flea (EV)
segments.commentary: Flying Flea C6 launched and deliveries started this quarter; about 100+ units delivered in two months, with Bengaluru expansion to 10 touchpoints and about 6 further cities planned.

segments.name: VECV (commercial vehicles)
segments.commentary: Total 24,815 units (up 14.8%); Eicher heavy-duty 5,275 units (up 15.2%, 8.8% share); light and medium-duty 9,993 units; Eicher buses 6,126 units; Volvo trucks and buses record 598 units; exports 1,450 units (up 14.7%); spares sales INR 931.3 crore (up 15.3%).

segments.name: Allied / aftermarket
segments.commentary: Allied businesses about 15% of revenue; about 9 lakh service job cards per month (up about 20% YoY); accessories and apparel growing above 30%, with accessory attach rate at about 87% per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects growth momentum to continue; no formal numerical guidance given. Commodity outlook not quantified because the situation is described as volatile.
Royal Enfield Cheyyar brownfield (INR 958 crore announced in Feb 2026) expected to reach 2 million units per year capacity by FY28.
Tada greenfield Phase 1 (INR 1,225 crore, approved today) adds about 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, with completion expected in FY30; total capacity to reach 2.45 million units by FY30.
Next Cheyyar module expected to kick in by first week of October 2026.
Indonesia CKD decision expected within the current quarter.
capex_capacity: Current Royal Enfield build capacity about 1.5 million motorcycles per year after first Cheyyar module, which started in July 2026 (in time); delivery rate reached about 5,000+ per day.
June 2026 production about 1.16 lakh motorcycles, with about 4,500 per day rate; Oragadam and Vallam running three shifts since April.
Tada greenfield in Andhra Pradesh: INR 1,225 crore Phase 1, additional 4.5 lakh units per year at full utilisation, built in modules.
Depreciation rise attributed to about INR 346 crore increase in average gross block, mainly Flying Flea start of production and new capacity, plus tools and dies depreciation.
Indonesia: CKD assembly partner identified to get around 10,000-unit annual import quota limit; luxury tax about 160%+ applies to bikes above 250cc regardless of CBU/CKD.
demand_pricing: Royal Enfield India retail growth about 30-32% YoY in Q1; booking, walk-in and telephonic inquiries growing slightly faster than volumes.

Dealer inventory at about 10-12 days, described as lean; in-transit inventory about 5 days and depot inventory about 4-5 days additional, per Q&A. Management targets saving another 4-5 days via more direct billing (about 4.5-4.7x increase vs prior year).
Gross margin: commodity and input inflation net impact about 4-4.5% of costs in Q1; value engineering benefit about 0.4%; 350cc price hike of 1.75% from April 2026 gave about 1.2% benefit.
Hunter 350 first-time buyers about 50% share; overall RE customer mix about 70%+ upgraders, about 25% first-time buyers, about 5-6% repeat RE-to-RE.
VECV: spares growth 15.3%; Pro X SCV entry with 1,041 units including 172 EVs; PARIVARTAN fleet modernisation MoU for NCR targets over 2 lakh vehicles, implementation being finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the brownfield capacity ramp and what is channel inventory ahead of festive?
qa_highlights.answer: First module started July 2026, output about 5,000+ per day delivery; inventory about 10-12 days, lean; direct billing and vendor 3-shift planning aimed to build stock before festive; next module by October first week.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross margin bridge and the drivers of lower other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Net commodity/input impact about 4-4.5%, value engineering about 0.4%, price hikes about 1.2%, mix 0.2%. Other expenses down about 7%: INR 30 crore from Q4 timing (cricket ads, two launches) and INR 22 crore marketing cut. No forward commodity guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What is demand outlook into the back half given high base from October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management points to strong funnel growth, a middleweight segment that grew from 70,000 to 1.2 lakh units per month in three years, planned launches, and a marketing ramp-up after scaling back in Q1 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue gap between standalone and consolidated and its sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Gap driven by subsidiary growth, mainly Brazil, with some offset from India-booked exports; international market size about 0.8-1 million units, Royal Enfield share 8-9%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ASP up and what is driving non-vehicle revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: ASP up 2.8% QoQ: price hikes 1.2%, international mix 1%, currency 0.4%, allied 0.6%. Allied about 15% of revenue, service job cards about 9 lakh per month.

qa_highlights.question: Any plans to list or hive off VECV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no crystallised plan; focus at Eicher level is on EV; VECV growth described as phenomenal across segments except heavy-duty buses.

risks_watch: Inventory tightness at about 10-12 days ahead of festive; ability of vendors to sustain 24/7 three-shift output and the October module timing.
Commodity inflation (aluminium, crude, steel, copper, precious metals) and logistics disruption; management declined to guide on Q2 commodity headwind.
Higher-cc (450cc/650cc) softness in Super Meteor, Himalayan and Shotgun in Q1 per analyst; management plans marketing and refreshes.
High base from October for the next 12 months after GST-related price cuts.
Europe and APAC still weak; Indonesia import quota and luxury tax constrain ASEAN growth; Flying Flea scale-up and EV economics still early.

505255|2026-03.headline: GMM Pfaudler FY26 revenue rose about 10% and EBITDA about 11% to INR 403 crore; Q4 gross margin fell, with no FY27 numeric guidance.
505255|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA rose from INR 361 crore to INR 403 crore, with full-year margin up about 1 percentage point. India was the standout, with revenue up about 12%, EBITDA up about 24% and PAT up about 40%. Q4 margins fell year-on-year and sequentially on a large HE (heavy engineering) shipment and higher gas and metal costs, which management called quarter-specific. FY26 order intake reached INR 3,714 crore (up about 20% from INR 3,100 crore) and opening backlog on April 1 was up about 34%. Management declined to give numeric FY27 guidance and said it would present a three-year plan to the market later.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 12%, EBITDA about 24% and PAT about 40% in FY26. Heavy engineering (Ahmedabad) did about INR 300+ crore revenue in FY26, and the Vatva facility (GMM Inox, Poland) grew double digits.

segments.name: Europe / International
segments.commentary: Execution was slow; international EBITDA margin cited at about 10%. German restructuring is expected to save INR 45 crore a year once fully absorbed. Europe order intake was much stronger in FY26, including large systems orders.

segments.name: Mixing / Edlon / SEMCO
segments.commentary: Edlon (semiconductor-linked high-purity linings) is now about USD 25 million revenue, which management called high margin. SEMCO (South America) won a USD 12-13 million agitator order in Q1 FY27; MixPro (Canada) is growing and profitable.

guidance_outlook: No numeric FY27 guidance; management said it expects improvement in FY27 on a 12-month basis, citing order intake, backlog and restructuring.
Medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration of at least 15% at consolidated level, versus about 11.4-11.5% today.
Three-year strategy (growth, cost, organisation) prepared; market presentation targeted for August-September, possibly later given Middle East crisis.
Expects no significant one-off restructuring cost in FY27; the INR 45 crore German saving starts next year and fully materialises as staff retire.
Plans to repay about USD 20 million from group cash and reduce debt, but timing of the financing restructuring is not confirmed by end of FY27.
Target of at least double-digit revenue growth over about three years, but management said 20% growth in a year is unlikely to be planned for.
capex_capacity: GMM Inox (Poland, 51% owned, strong local partner) is full; two more sheds are needed as soon as possible to serve European sites with lower cost.
Vatva facility (GMM Inox) could reach about INR 700-800 crore revenue with small further investment; beyond that a new facility is needed.
UK and Hyderabad facilities shut; German factory downsized; Poland plant now operating.
Edlon and SEMCO acquisitions added intangibles and goodwill; split not given on call, to be shared offline.
demand_pricing: Order intake up about 20% to INR 3,714 crore; nearly 50% from non-traditional industries (semiconductors, defence, oil and gas, petrochemicals, metals and minerals, nuclear).
Two large systems orders (one US, one Eastern Europe) drove much of the increase; open systems opportunities could yield USD 20-30 million order intake per year.
Chemicals (especially agrochemicals and European chemicals) remain slow; pharma (CDMO, GLP drugs) improving; China business recovering in some segments.
Raw material pass-through depends on contract: long-term projects have a 5% expedition clause; fast-moving contracts absorb cost changes.
Q1 FY27 order intake continuing at a decent level, including an Edlon order of USD 8-9 million.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 gross and consolidated EBITDA margins (55.4% gross) drop, and what are sustainable margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to a large HE order shipped at lower margin and higher gas and metal costs that have since stabilised. It said quarterly margins are volatile and FY26 margin was up about 1 pp; it prefers 12-month views.

qa_highlights.question: Why no guidance for FY27, and what drives the growth and margin plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% order-intake rise includes systems orders that convert over 2-3 years, so it avoided a bullish number. It plans a three-year strategy to be presented to the capital markets once confidence improves, targeting at least double-digit growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the German restructuring saving and will exceptional items recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The German restructuring saves INR 45 crore a year, starting next year. No significant one-off cost is planned for FY27, though future restructurings would be reported as one-offs. FY26 exceptional items were about INR 65 crore, including German severance and the India labour code impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the finance cost high relative to a small net debt, and how does the company plan to reduce it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited FX on an intercompany loan between Germany and Luxembourg, and a financing agreement in place until 2028, which it intends to restructure within the next year. It said the high cash balance is partly customer prepayments needed to finance large systems orders.

qa_highlights.question: What are the long-term margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aspires to a 15% consolidated EBITDA margin in the medium term, as a minimum, versus about 11.4-11.5% today, and said it could come faster if initiatives work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the segment reporting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the reporting format will change from next quarter (Q1 FY27), with a new organisation aligned by product, vertical and industry, rather than mid-year.

risks_watch: Gross margin and mix volatility: Q4 margins fell and management said it is quarter-specific; watch whether FY27 margins recover.
Tax rate: international tax remains high, mainly from the Luxembourg entity and an intercompany FX loan; Q4 international rate was about 30%.
Finance cost of about INR 120-130 crore against low net debt; restructuring timeline is uncertain and may slip beyond FY27.
Middle East conflict and geopolitical tension could delay investments in Europe and Asia; management said it may delay its capital markets presentation.
Chemicals demand remains weak; systems orders are lumpy and convert to revenue over 2-3 years.
Changed segment reporting expected from Q1 FY27; SEMCO purchase price allocation split was not disclosed on the call.

505255|2026-06.headline: GMM Pfaudler Q1 FY27 revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 925 crores, but EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores on pricing pressure and organisation-building costs.
505255|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16% YoY to INR 925 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR 22 crores, while EBITDA fell 7% YoY to INR 94 crores (up 25% QoQ). Order intake was flat YoY at INR 1,007 crores, and the order backlog reached a record INR 2,289 crores (+20% YoY, +4% QoQ). The company moved to four global technology divisions (CRT, PPT, HET, PST) and disclosed segment results for the first time. Management said debt reduction (about EUR 7 million by end-Q2) and refinancing are under way, with no numeric debt target given.

segments.name: CRT (Corrosion Resistance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 466 crores (+10% YoY); order intake INR 502 crores (+23% YoY). Glass-lined pharma and chemical demand described as stable; large aftermarket and service base.

segments.name: PPT (Process Performance Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 255 crores (+23% YoY); order intake INR 367 crores (+64% YoY). Covers mixing, filtration, drying, and sealing; pharma and food & beverage adoption cited.

segments.name: HET (Heavy Engineering Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 74 crores (flat YoY); order intake INR 58 crores (up more than 700% YoY). India-led, oil and gas, petrochemicals, with nuclear and power entry and EIL approvals.

segments.name: PST (Process System Technologies)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 131 crores (+46% YoY); order intake INR 80 crores vs INR 363 crores in Q1 FY26, which included one large defence order. Skids and engineered systems for semiconductor, defence and pharma.

guidance_outlook: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 15%, described as a minimum target; management said current verticals are roughly around this range, with no timeline given.
Management expects improvement YoY across all businesses but declined to give a specific margin number; quarter-on-quarter margin tracking was framed as the approach.
Debt: about EUR 7 million to be repaid by end of Q2 FY27; further reduction via refinancing over 12 to 18 months. No year-end debt target disclosed.
Tax rate: work with around 30%, possibly slightly lower in the long term, expected within 18 to 24 months after refinancing and entity restructuring.

505283|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 sales rose 21% to INR706 crore and FY26 PBT hit a record INR356 crore, but management flags 18-20% EBITDA as sustainable, not the 21.7% delivered.
505283|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 sales were INR706 crore versus INR583 crore a year earlier, with raw material-to-sales falling to 50.06% from 56.35%. FY26 EBITDA was INR388 crore (21.7% of total income) and PBT INR356 crore (19.6%), supported by in-house backward integration and a selective order-acceptance stance. The unexecuted order board rose 15% to INR1,863 crore as of April 1, 2026, including Precision Components, and the company remains debt-free with about INR460 crore net cash. 505533|2026-09.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16% to INR7.47 billion, with same-store sales up 10.1% on double-digit guest count growth.

Operating EBITDA rose 29% YoY (management also cited about 26% in one answer), with margin up 130 bps to 13.1% despite about 190 bps of inflation across commodities, utilities and employee costs. The company opened 11 restaurants, taking the network to 492 across 80 cities, and reiterated its 580+ restaurant target by March 2028. Management said momentum continued into October, and guided to 100-150 bps of annual profitability improvement and 2-4% price increases over the year.

505537|2026-03.headline: Zee Q4 FY26: digital revenue up 71% YoY to INR4,700 mn and ZEE5 EBITDA positive for FY26, but ad revenue fell 4% on a March West Asia hit and a INR4,084 mn one-off charge.

Linear advertising revenue declined 4% YoY as advertisers pulled spends in March amid the Middle East conflict; management said it would have been low single-digit growth excluding March. A one-off charge of INR4,084 million from a change in movie rights amortization (front-loaded to 50% over two years) and additional impairment was taken in the quarter, and the adjusted EBITDA margin was 6.9% on a 7% decline in operating revenue. Management gave no formal guidance, and the call was mainly Q&A on Zee Music, Bullet, live events, ad spend and manpower costs.

ZEE5 revenues more than doubled YoY and grew 37% QoQ to INR6.3 billion, the highest quarterly digital revenue to date. EBITDA was INR708 million with a 3.2% margin, hit by FIFA programming and advertising costs and marketing spends on new initiatives (Bullet, KidZ, sports); management said the margin would have been mid-to-high single digit excluding those spends. PAT was INR456 million. Advertising was flat YoY and up 20% QoQ, and management said the ad decline has stabilised.

505700|2026-03.headline: Elecon Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell to INR746 crore (from INR798 crore) as Gear sales dropped 21%; FY27 guidance held back.
505700|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue declined moderately YoY to INR746 crore, with EBITDA of INR158 crore (21.2% margin) and PAT of INR108 crore before a INR102 crore goodwill impairment. Gear Division revenue fell 21% YoY to INR472 crore on customer-led delivery deferrals, mainly in steel, while MHE grew 37% to INR274 crore. Management attributed the March shortfall to geopolitical-driven deferrals and said it will not give FY27 guidance, citing limited visibility. Open order book rose to about INR1,292 crore from INR948 crore a year earlier.

505700|2026-06.headline: Elecon Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore, but management guided only low double-digit FY27 growth on raw-material-driven order conversion delays.
505700|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 11.9% YoY to INR521 crore over adjusted Q1 FY26 revenue of INR465 crore, with EBITDA up 3.9% to INR109 crore at a stated 21% margin and PAT of INR70 crore (13.5% margin, up 2.3%). Gear division drove growth, with revenue up 16.3% to INR416 crore, while MHE revenue fell 2.9% to INR105 crore on project execution delays and EBIT fell 25.3% to INR27 crore. Order intake rose 23% to INR755 crore and the consolidated open order book rose 36.8% to INR1,518 crore, yet management guided only low double-digit FY27 revenue growth, citing raw-material price spikes that slowed enquiry-to-order conversion and PSU-linked capex delays.

segments.name: Gear division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR416 crore (~80% of consolidated), up 16.3% YoY; order intake INR570 crore (+18.8%); open order book INR1,043 crore (+46.9%). EBIT INR75 crore at 17.9% margin vs FY26 full-year EBIT margin of 18.8%; mix 54% catalogue / 46% engineered.

segments.name: MHE division
segments.commentary: Revenue INR105 crore (-2.9% YoY) on project execution delays for power-sector orders; order intake INR185 crore (+38.1%); open order book INR475 crore (+18.8%). EBIT INR27 crore at about 25.6% margin vs FY26 full-year 24.7%; secured overseas port order of about INR21 crore.

segments.name: Overseas business
segments.commentary: Revenue INR151 crore (+21.9% YoY), led by Middle East and US; overseas order intake INR194 crore (+63%), including INR21 crore from MHE; overseas open order book INR256 crore (+73%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided to low double-digit percentage, described as conservative given macro uncertainty; management said it could be revisited next quarter.
Consolidated EBITDA margin to be maintained at the FY26 level (about 21%).
Gear division EBITDA margin guided to about 24%; gear EBIT margin expected around 19-20% over the next year and one year after.
MHE sustainable EBITDA margin guided at 22-24% for the year.
Exports expected to grow at least double digits in FY27; Europe recovery expected to take at least two quarters.
Mid-term FY30 revenue target of INR5,000 crore described as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue.
Gear revenue conversion expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 as stabilised prices are accepted; Q2 to show only gradual pick-up.
capex_capacity: Previously announced capex programme of approximately INR400 crore over FY26 to FY28 stated as on track; further capex under evaluation for board approval in near future.
Assembly centres outside India (Middle East, US and others) set up for customer proximity; some sub-assemblies locally outsourced.

Defence business has dedicated manufacturing and operating vertical built over the last 3-4 years; defence orders expected to execute over 2-3 years with working capital about 15-20% higher than the gear average.
Gear manufacturing cycle is 2-3 months for catalogue products and 4-5 months for engineered products.
demand_pricing: Gear order intake drivers: power (about 27% of order intake, including a large single order flagged in Q4 FY26), steel, cement and MHE; catalogue vs engineered order mix 27% / 73% in the quarter.

Raw-material BOM cost up about 5% on average (steel 5-7%, bearings 6-7%, fabricated gear cases about 7%, tooling 6-10%); most Q1 orders accepted with price increases and raw materials locked back-to-back on order acceptance.
Management attributed slower conversion to a sharp raw-material price increase that lengthened enquiry-to-order cycles, and to competitors holding low-cost inventory that pressured quotes.

MHE margin decline attributed to about 2.5-3% from input costs, about 3% from sales mix, and about 3% from lower throughput; MHE delays linked to design-engineering clearances on two large power-sector orders routed through EPC contractors.
Middle East growth came from orders on hold in Q4 FY26 that resumed dispatch; Middle East weakness mainly in cement and mining and minerals; Europe weak.
Sugar outlook muted due to prolonged monsoon; defence orders showed no significant update in the last 90 days; aerospace certification not being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the MHE margin fall is mix versus input costs, and what is sustainable MHE margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split the decline into about 2.5-3% input costs, about 3% sales mix and about 3% lower volume; sustainable MHE EBITDA margin guided at 22-24%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gear revenue growth lagging order book growth and why only low double-digit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw-material spikes slowed enquiry-to-order conversion; about INR70 crore of finished goods could not be recognised as sales in Q1 because title transfer criteria were not met by 30 June; Q2 expected only gradual pick-up, with Q3-Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Can gear costs be passed on given the small share of gear in customer capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PSU-linked demand (thermal power, cement, steel) is sensitive to budgets; Q1 was a correction phase in pricing, with Q2 expected to be an acceptance phase. About INR160 crore of the gear order book extends beyond FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for gear standalone margins and does the business return to mid-20s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided gear EBITDA to about 24% and gear EBIT around 19-20% over the next year and one year beyond, versus 18.8% EBIT in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY30 aspiration and segment split?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR5,000 crore FY30 revenue target was reiterated as challenging but achievable, with Gear at 70-75% and MHE at 25-30% of revenue; Gear includes marine.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital impact of defence orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders over 2-3 years carry higher working capital days, about 15-20% above the gear average in past similar orders, which management said would be absorbed by higher margins.

505714|2026-09.headline: Gabriel India consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR1,608 crore, with EBITDA up 12% to INR141 crore at an 8.8% margin.

qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the HL Klemove and FORVIA seating JVs as key steps and said ADAS and seating are high-value product areas. It did not give numbers or formal return thresholds, but said it does not compromise on ROI.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not seasonal. Commodity and logistics costs have outpaced customer price recovery across businesses. Dana is offset by export forex gains.

qa_highlights.answer: The JV will be the single point of contact for the full seating system. Mechanisms, about 15-20% of seat content, will be bought from FORVIA's 100%-owned Indian mechanism company. FORVIA's seating business in India moves into the JV except mechanisms.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an anchor order for the seating JV and is a royalty payable?
qa_highlights.answer: The JV takes over existing won business, including a Volkswagen program. Value will be disclosed after closing. A royalty will be paid for technology from the Indian R&D centre, which management called normal for such deals.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PV shock absorber and CV revenue growth trail the market?
qa_highlights.answer: Atul Jaggi said CV growth matched the market given more than 85% share, with aftermarket and railway lumped into CV numbers. PV lagged mainly because of mix, with small-car models underperforming.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sunroof volume position, and what is the outlook for the next two years?

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and margin perimeter for the Faurecia seating business transfer?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing is targeted for December end. The frame business, about INR150 crore in size, transfers at its current margin. Mechanisms are excluded.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth expectations for HL Mando and HL Klemove?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both to grow above the market. HL Mando is about 60-65% Hyundai/Kia and is adding Tata, Maruti Suzuki and Mahindra. HL Klemove is already with Hyundai, Tata and Mahindra, and is adding Maruti Suzuki.

505726|2026-03.headline: IFB Industries Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11.0% to INR 1,456 crore and PAT to INR 33.7 crore, but FY26 commodity and forex hits of INR 84 crore were only partly offset.

April-May commodity and forex headwinds of about INR 49 crore are only partly offset (INR 29 crore from cost initiatives so far).

505790|2026-09.headline: Schaeffler India says automotive demand is growing about 29-30% on GST 2.0 and localization is at 80%, with no explicit numbers on Q2 FY27 financials.
505790|2026-09.overview: This was an investor group meeting (Sept 28, 2026), not a formal results call, so no quarterly financial figures were given. Management said automotive growth of roughly 29-30% was driven by GST 2.0 and BS-VI product transitions, while industrial growth was mixed, with infrastructure, steel, cement and railways strong and construction equipment and mining weak. Exports were framed as a by-product of localization, with management targeting 15-20% of revenue from exports. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input costs, with about 70% of cost increases typically recovered from customers, and that Vitesco's India integration has no timeline. E-mobility was described as loss-making and early-stage, with adoption under 5% today and about 15% expected by FY31.

506222|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores and PAT rose 58.6% to INR84.3 crores, despite total income down 6.3%.
506222|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income fell 6.3% to INR658 crores while EBITDA rose 51.9% to INR126 crores, with margin up 734 bps to 19.2%. Management attributed the stronger profitability to product mix (lower GPPS volumes) and opportunistic pricing in tight segments, and said there was no significant inventory gain. Volumes fell 4.6% YoY to 46.1 KT, driven by GPPS weakness, while ABS and HIPS grew. Management declined to quantify the Thailand breakeven change or the power-savings benefit, citing short-term market distortion from the Middle East supply crisis, and reiterated that India ABS capacity additions remain on track for the second half of FY27.

segments.commentary: Grew YoY in Q4 volume per management; 60-70% of ABS volume is formula or contract based. ABS capacity expansion reaffirmed on schedule for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4).

segments.name: HIPS (India)
segments.commentary: Volume grew YoY in Q4; formula/OEM-based share now well above 50% of HIPS business. Capex decision on a dedicated HIPS plant still under study.

segments.name: GPPS (India)
segments.commentary: Significant volume decline in Q4 due to muted demand, unorganized market, and import dumping; Styrenix chose not to chase low-price volume. Capacity already expanded but under-utilised. Formula-based share above 70% across GPPS business.

segments.commentary: Volumes fell 20-30% YoY in Q4 per analyst, partly due to customer pre-buying in the prior-year Jan-Mar quarter ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch. Management says most business retained; breakeven requires 60-70% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand breakeven utilisation (65-70%) now easier to reach given current pricing and raw material availability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said breakeven targets should not change; short-term tightness gains are arbitrage that may not last. Thailand still needs to reach 60-70% utilisation to generate returns.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 volume drop in India and the 20-30% drop in Thailand explained?
qa_highlights.answer: India dip was from GPPS only; ABS and HIPS grew YoY. Thailand comparison was distorted by prior-year pre-buying ahead of the INEOS-to-Styrenix brand switch, and Jan-Mar is seasonally weaker. Most business was retained.

qa_highlights.question: Is the spread at spot prices better or worse in FY27 versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Contract and formula margins are similar or slightly better. Spot margins are better for specific grades where Korean suppliers' quality is weak, but this is opportunistic.

qa_highlights.question: Should capex be preponed for ABS given Korean import disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said capex is proceeding as planned with no acceleration.

qa_highlights.question: What share of sales is formula-based versus spot?
qa_highlights.answer: ABS: 60-70% formula or contract. HIPS: well above 50% formula/OEM. GPPS: formula-based pricing above 70% for the business overall, with volumes dropping as the company avoids unformulated segments.

qa_highlights.question: Will Thailand ever reach breakeven given normalised spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated that returns start at 60-70% utilisation and the plant is still below that level.

506222|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA rose 133.9% to INR201.4 crore (26.1% margin) even as sales volume fell 26% to 38.9 KT.
506222|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income grew 6.6% to INR770.5 crore and PAT rose 150.3% to INR137.3 crore, driven by a sharp margin jump, while volumes dropped 26% as non-OEM buyers held back amid Middle East-driven raw material price volatility. Consolidated (India plus Thailand) volume was 50.8 KT, EBITDA INR223.6 crore at 22% margin. Management described the margin gain as a snapshot of a volatile quarter, not a sustainable run rate, and gave no volume guidance. The ABS capacity expansion is said to be on track for completion in FY27 without a firm commissioning month, and Thailand volumes remain subdued.

segments.name: ABS (India)
segments.commentary: Demand fell in the quarter, with a smaller drop than polystyrene; OEM is about 70% or more of ABS sales. Management did not give a segment volume split.

segments.name: Polystyrene (India)
segments.commentary: Hit harder than ABS, mainly in the non-OEM/unorganised segment; OEM is about 50% of PS sales. Management did not give volume numbers.

segments.name: SAN
segments.commentary: Merchant sales run at about 15,000-20,000 tonnes a year against roughly 100,000 tonnes of capacity; most output is used captively, and merchant sales will continue after the ABS expansion.

segments.name: Thailand
segments.commentary: Running at low utilisation on specific products; volumes were broadly maintained quarter on quarter, but new business has not yet translated into meaningful volume growth. Validation cycles run 12-24 months.

No new capex or capital allocation changes beyond the ABS expansion; polystyrene expansion to be decided when the business case is clearer.
capex_capacity: ABS expansion is a brownfield project at a running site, so commissioning is complex; management expects completion within FY27.
SAN capacity of about 100,000 tonnes against merchant sales of 15-20 KT a year; expansions planned across rubber, SAN and compounding sites.
Thailand cost base is described as higher than India's; no reduction timeline was given.
demand_pricing: Demand fell in Q1 due to a Middle East-driven price spike from March and high volatility; buyers in the non-OEM/unorganised segment held back. Management put the volume decline at about 15-25% on total polymer.

Styrene monomer went from about $1,000/t pre-war to $1,600-1,700, then about $1,200, and has since traded in a $1,100-1,400 range. Acrylonitrile moved from $1,200 to about $1,800-1,900 and is now $1,400-1,600. Butadiene (bought locally) went from $1,000 to above $2,500 and has since eased.
Styrene monomer is now sourced from alternate suppliers with 10-15 days longer lead times; management said it is 'fully covered' and carried slightly higher raw material inventory at quarter end.
Price pass-through is handled through short-term mechanisms and global price markers; management said previous-quarter pricing was significantly higher and moderated toward quarter end.
Imports: management said it has seen no significant change in import volumes, with some Asian exporters constrained by energy and naphtha shortages. Official import data is not available.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the volume decline was in line across ABS and PS, roughly 15-25% on total polymer. The non-OEM segment was hit harder than OEM, which was affected only muted.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was a snapshot of an unusual event and is not indicative of sustainable earnings; pre-event performance is the right base. It did not give a number.

qa_highlights.answer: SAN merchant sales will continue. The ABS expansion will be completed in FY27, but exact timing was not disclosed because the project runs alongside an operating plant.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any new capital allocation plan given extra cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new plan; cash will go to planned capex with the rest returned to shareholders in line with existing policy. No specific dividend or buyback was announced.

qa_highlights.question: What are Thailand's volume and sales plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Thailand sales strategy is to win validations in China, Japan, Vietnam, Korea and others; validations take 12-24 months. No volume guidance was given.

ABS expansion timing (within FY27) and execution risk on a brownfield site.
Thailand utilisation and validation progress; cost base still above India's.
Raw material lead times and alternate sourcing for styrene monomer and acrylonitrile; freight and energy disruptions.
Limited import data availability, which makes competitive import pressure hard to track.

506395|2026-03.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.
506395|2026-03.overview: Q4 operations were strong: consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 494 crore, with the fertilizer plants run full after the annual turnaround. Reported PAT of INR 115 crore compared with INR 578 crore last year, which included a INR 347 crore land-sale exceptional gain; this year carried a INR 71 crore impairment on drone-business investments and goodwill. Fertilizer margins compressed sharply as Middle East disruption spiked ammonia and sulphur prices, while crop protection, specialty nutrients, retail and NACL performed well. Management gave no quantitative guidance on fertilizer margins or subsidy outcomes, pending government support.

segments.name: Fertilizers (DAP/NPK/SSP/Nano)
segments.commentary: Record fertilizer production of 3.5 million tons and record DAP+NPK sales of 4.3 million tons (+7%), with 17.5% phosphatic market share; Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA was below INR 3,500 per ton versus over INR 5,000 per ton last year. SSP sales hit a record 8.4 lakh tons, and Nano DAP volumes grew 60% to about 42 lakh bottles.

segments.name: Crop protection (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to INR 3,054 crore and profit 55% to INR 569 crore for FY26; FY26 revenue mix was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore. Q4 standalone crop protection growth was about 2%, attributed to export sales being moved into Q1 and a bio export order shipped earlier.

segments.name: NACL (Nagarjuna Agrichem, 53% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated crop protection with NACL reached about INR 4,000 crore; NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) and EBITDA INR 103 crore, with margin at 6-7% and guided to 9-10% next year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew over 30% in FY26 with more than 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Dhaksha (drones, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Impairment of INR 71 crore taken on investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution; management expects recovery after first large order executes this year.

guidance_outlook: Crop protection (standalone) revenue growth guided at 20-25% for the coming year, with domestic formulations growing 20-25% and six new product launches.
Sarigam active ingredient expansion of 20,000 tons is due around mid-2026 with payback under two years; Dahej Mancozeb debottlenecking of 10,000 tons has payback under one year.
Granulation capacity expansion expected to commission by December 2026.
Rock phosphate output in Senegal to rise 30-40% in FY27 from more than 3.5 lakh tons in FY26.
Trading margin of roughly 4-5% per ton; trading volumes may fall in Q1 FY27 on DAP availability, with second-half recovery expected.
Management declined to give fertilizer EBITDA per ton or margin guidance for FY27, citing fluid conditions and pending subsidy compensation.
Raw material cover secured for Q1 FY27; Q2 cover depends on Middle East resolution. Sulphur visibility is up to June.
capex_capacity: Kakinada: 2,000 tpd sulphuric acid and 650 tpd phosphoric acid plant commissioned in March 2026 (about 200,000 tons per year phosphoric acid); in trial runs, with stable operations expected from April-May 2026.
Dahej: technical plant commissioned in FY26 and Mancozeb capacity expanded by 10,000 tons; Sarigam expansion of 20,000 tons under way.
Technical MAP plant and seaweed granulation capacity under development.
Fluorination chemistry investment planned for CDMO opportunity; small-scale capacity to be created this year, production next year.
Coromandel has invested over INR 3,000 crore across segments in the last two years.

NBS rates for kharif 2026 raised about 10% for N, P and S, which management said do not reflect the sharp rise in raw material prices and rupee depreciation.
Ammonia and sulphur are trading around USD 840-850 and USD 800 per ton respectively; phosphoric acid price for the quarter fixed at USD 1,360 versus USD 1,290 previously.
Q4 rupee range of 89.75-95.23 per USD; management said depreciation helps the crop protection export business.
Crop protection raw materials said to be covered, with input cost increases passed through; Mancozeb cost increases passed through to customers.
Rabi season demand was muted due to late monsoon withdrawal, with lower-than-expected liquidation.
Unique grades remained at about 35% of fertilizer sales on an annualized basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between consolidated and standalone P&L, and how will BMCC's depreciation and profitability evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BMCC (mining) has turned profitable on better volumes and fixed-cost absorption, and the gap is mainly consolidation amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, not operating loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will fertilizer margins hold up given only about a 10% NBS increase against sharp raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking additional subsidy and cost-to-cost reimbursement for June-September, with discussions at an early stage; it declined to quantify the amount. Any remaining gap may be passed on through MRP corrections, and industry has already made some MRP corrections in the last one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the crop protection growth, margin and NACL margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone crop protection targets 20-25% revenue growth with margins sustained near 19%; NACL margin improved to 6-7%, can reach 9-10% next year, and restoring 7-8% needs no major investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year split of subsidy versus non-subsidy EBITDA and of crop protection revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy share of EBITDA was 57% in Q4 and 66% for FY26. Standalone FY26 crop protection revenue was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore; NACL FY26 revenue was INR 1,584 crore and Q4 INR 361 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertilizer finished goods inventory and trading exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished fertilizer inventory is about 5.5 lakh tons, of which trading is about 60,000-70,000 tons. Trading margin is roughly 4-5%, and FY27 trading volume may fall in Q1 because of DAP import shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone crop protection growth only about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is off-season, export sales were deliberately moderated to shift into April-May, and a bio export order was executed earlier in December; full-year crop protection growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulphur and ammonia sourcing position, and is Q2 covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur has visibility up to June, with diversified spot sourcing from Canada, South Asia and Japan; ammonia and sulphur prices are about USD 800-850 per ton. Management said Q2 coverage depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Dhaksha, the drone subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical gaps are fixed and a large order is awaiting execution, with the first order this year expected to build confidence; a larger facility is due around May 2026.
